counters.reason: Yang Jian's damage scales with the Health Dr Bian has already lost, so every trade makes the next one worse.
Mai Shiranui strips magical defense before she dashes in, leaving Dr Bian no room to reset the distance.

passive.description:
Dr Bian's Basic Attacks and skills place a poison mark on enemies for 7s (up to 5 stacks), dealing 20 (20 + 5% magical attack) magical damage per second.
Healing skills place a healing mark on teammates and himself for 7s (up to 5 stacks), restoring 3 (3 + 2% magical attack) Health per second to teammates, and 3 (3 + 2% magical attack + 0.15% extra Health) Health per second to himself.
passive.name: Malicious Practice

skill1.description:
Dr Bian throws a vial of lethal poison that shatters upon impact, releasing a pool of poison for 4s. Every second, it deals 65 (65 + 14% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the area and slows them by 30% for 2s.
Dr Bian stocks 1 vial every 12.5s. Up to 3 vials can be stocked.
skill1.name: Deadly Panacea

skill2.description: Dr Bian throws a concoction, dealing 130 (130 +30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and restoring 65 (65 +15% magical attack) Health to nearby teammates.
skill2.name: Fatal Diagnosis

skill3.description:
Dr Bian detonates all nearby marks, dealing 150 (150 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies while restoring 70 (70 + 20% magical attack) Health to teammates. Each stack of mark increases damage and healing by 50%.
He also recovers 400 (400 + 30% magical attack + 5% extra Health) extra Health.
skill3.name: Master of Life

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Dr Bian lacks the burst to finish enemies quickly, so he doesn't force early trades. He clears waves with Deadly Panacea's poison pools and prioritizes keeping his Health up. Vials recharge over time and he can stock several, so keeping one in reserve for self-defense is safer. While the enemy jungler is unseen, dropping a pool at his feet before backing off slows anyone who chases. His passive poison also applies with basic attacks, so stack marks with basic attacks from a safe distance.
strategy.midGame: As his items come together, he can drag skirmishes out. In fights over Tyrant or Overlord, throw Deadly Panacea at enemies' feet from behind the front line and cycle Fatal Diagnosis for chip damage and team healing. Once poison marks have stacked up, detonate them with Master of Life. Lining up poison pools before Shadow Tyrant or Shadow Overlord forces enemies to fight while being worn down.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, he plays the role of stacking marks rather than making flashy engages. Once the fight starts, throw Deadly Panacea where enemies are clumped and Fatal Diagnosis at an easy-to-hit frontliner while healing nearby teammates. When both teams are tangled together, detonate all nearby marks with Master of Life. Popping them while several enemies carry stacked poison delivers area damage and a team recovery at the same time. If an assassin dives him, break a vial at his own feet and back off toward his team while they walk through the pool.

combos.title: Stack the Marks, Then Pop Them
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Deadly Panacea: poison pool) → Skill 2 (Fatal Diagnosis: chip and heal teammates) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (Master of Life: detonate marks)
combos.description: Don't pop them early; detonate once the marks have built up. Timing it as teammates start losing Health keeps the healing from going to waste.

combos.title: Drop Poison at Your Feet and Back Off
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Deadly Panacea: at his own feet) → Skill 2 (Fatal Diagnosis) → Skill 3 (Master of Life: extra self-heal)
combos.description: He has no movement skill, so when dived, make the enemy walk through the poison instead of trying to outrun them. Enemies in the pool are slowed, giving him time to back off toward his team. Master of Life detonates marks and also gives Dr Bian extra healing, buying him time to retreat.

strengths: He advances poison on enemies and healing on teammates with the same flow of skills
Master of Life's detonation delivers area damage and team healing at once
He can stock several Deadly Panacea vials, making it easy to line up poison pools and hold an area
weaknesses: No movement skill, so he struggles to escape on his own when assassins get close
Marks take time to stack, so his damage is low in short trades
Enemies with healing reduction items cut into his ability to support his team

playstyle.style: Dr Bian is a mage who places poison marks on enemies and healing marks on teammates and himself, then detonates them all with his ultimate, Master of Life. Every Basic Attack and skill hit stacks a poison mark, chipping away at enemy Health over time. The more marks have stacked, the bigger the detonation's damage and healing.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who would rather stack marks and drag fights out than win quick trades. He has no movement skill, so he needs to keep throwing poison pools and vials from behind the front line. How much he contributes depends on whether you can hold the detonation until the marks have stacked up.

synergy.reason: Diaochan needs repeat casts on the same targets, and Bai Qi's taunt buys her exactly that time.
Yaria's shield scales with the target's extra Health, so it grows thickest on a Health-stacking Bai Qi.

counters.reason: Lu Bu's enchanted halberd adds true damage on top, which Bai Qi's stacked defense cannot cut down.
Mozi's barrier stuns anything touching it, so Bai Qi's Lay Waste jump leaves him locked in place.

passive.description: Bai Qi gains Shadow Power when dealing or taking damage, which increases his Movement Speed by up to 70 and healing by up to 80%.
passive.name: Reaper's Revenge

skill1.description:
Bai Qi swings his scythe, dealing 252 (180 + 40% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range and recovering 90 (90 + 2% extra Health) Health.
Passive: Bai Qi has a 20% chance of automatically triggering this skill whenever he takes damage.
This skill can be charged up. The longer he charges for, the higher the damage and recovery effect, up to a maximum of 3 times the base damage and recovery. Effect is halved against non-hero units.
skill1.name: Blood Echo

skill2.description:
Bai Qi summons scythes which retract after 1.2s and pull enemies back, dealing 325 (325 + 120% extra magical attack) magical damage and slowing them by 25% for 2.5s.
Passive: He deals 30% extra damage to enemies below 30% Health.
skill2.name: Deathscythe

skill3.description: Bai Qi instantly gains maximum Shadow Power and jumps to the target location, dealing 481 (300 + 100% magical attack) magical damage and taunting enemies. Base taunt duration is 1-1.5s, and every 1,000 extra Health increases the duration by 0.2s, for a maximum duration of 2.5s.
skill3.name: Lay Waste

strategy.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. Bai Qi roams from the opening minutes, but his taunt only comes online at level 4 and lasts barely a second while his bonus HP is low, so deep dives backfire. Hold the space between mid and farm lane and play interceptor: thread Skill 2's scythe through ganking enemies and drag them back. The scythe returns 1.2 seconds after the throw, so aim it across the target's walking path rather than at their feet and it connects far more often. Taking damage has a chance to auto-cast Skill 1's heal, so tanking minion aggro to hold ground is less painful than it looks.
strategy.midGame: Two HP items done around 10 minutes is Bai Qi's power spike. Every 1000 bonus HP adds 0.2 seconds of taunt, and by now you're holding enemies for close to 2 seconds. When setting up vision at Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant, the real play is your Ultimate from a bush: the taunt forces enemies to attack Bai Qi, instantly sealing away the enemy carry's skills and combos. After landing, drag retreating targets back with Skill 2 and charge Skill 1 to heal while your team arrives.
strategy.lateGame: Full-build Bai Qi taunts for up to 2.5 seconds, and late-game teamfights come down to who eats it. The ideal is dropping it on the enemy marksman or mage — if your team burns them during 2-plus seconds of lockdown, the fight becomes 5v4. Miss the Ultimate, though, and your gap closers are spent, leaving a walking target. Discipline yourself to hold it until you've seen the enemy's dashes. Skill 2 also deals bonus damage to enemies below 30% HP, so you can finish runners yourself more often than you'd expect.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, one thought is enough: land your Ultimate on the enemy's most dangerous hero. Catch several with the AoE taunt and their entire damage output points at Bai Qi for seconds while your team swings freely, essentially untouched. Every hit you take stacks Shadow Power through the Passive, boosting your healing, and Skill 1's auto-proc stacks on top — melting mid-taunt is rarer than it looks. As the taunt expires, scythe their squishiest survivor toward your team as a parting gift and the numbers advantage keeps rolling.

combos.title: Taunt, Then Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (jump, taunt) → Skill 1 (charge and release) → Skill 2 (pull, 2.5s slow)
combos.description: The taunt runs 1-1.5s at base, plus 0.2s for every 1,000 extra Health, capped at 2.5s. Early on that is barely a second, so don't dive on it. Charge Skill 1 while they are locked and the release deals and heals up to three times as much. Anyone backing off as the taunt ends gets dragged back by the scythes.

combos.title: Peel Off the Backline
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pull, 25% slow) → Skill 3 (taunt)
combos.description: Hook the diver off your carry with the scythes, then taunt to force their attacks onto Bai Qi. The scythes retract 1.2s after they are summoned, so lead the throw into where the enemy is heading. Targets below 30% Health take 30% extra damage, which sometimes ends the chase on the spot.

strengths: AoE taunt scaling to 2.5 seconds with bonus HP seals away entire enemy combos
Auto-proc Skill 1 and the healing-boost Passive make him tougher the deeper the brawl
Skill 2 hits harder below 30% HP, letting him finish fleeing targets himself
weaknesses: The scythe's 1.2-second return delay makes it dodgeable once the path is read
Missing the Ultimate leaves no gap closer — he becomes a walking target
Early taunts last about a second, so early dives tend to backfire

playstyle.style: The taunt tank: he forces enemies to attack him, embodying aggro control. His scythe pulls and self-healing sustain the frontline — rated easy, but the craft runs deep.
playstyle.suited: players at peace with being the one who gets hit — the taunt pulls enemy damage off your team and runs longer the more bonus Health you carry, so everything rides on where you jump in.

synergy.reason: Dolia's Celestial Melody resets Mi Yue's longest cooldown, handing her a second Umbral Moon.
Bai Qi pulls enemies in and taunts them, so Mi Yue's Ravenous Tether stays linked instead of snapping.

counters.reason: Sun Ce stacks slows and then launches with his ship explosion, leaving Mi Yue nowhere to move.
Marco Polo stacks Destruction with every hit, and the true damage that follows cuts straight through Mi Yue's defenses.

passive.description:
Mi Yue summons shadow servants when using skills, which automatically attack nearby enemies. Each strike deals 50 (50 + 7% magical attack) magical damage while restoring 20 (20 + 0.5% extra Health) Health to her. Strikes deal an extra 80 (80 + 14% magical attack) magical damage to minions and deal half damage against monsters.
She gains 30 Shadow Power when summoning shadow servants, which grants up to 30 Movement Speed and a 10% bonus to all healing.
She can have up to 6 shadow servants around her at a time. When Shadow Power reaches zero, the servants will disappear.
passive.name: Eternal Youth

skill1.description:
Mi Yue unleashes shadow energy, dealing 200 (200 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
Upon using this skill again, she manifests herself at the shadow energy's location and deals 200 (200 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
She summons a shadow servant if she hits an enemy at the new location.
skill1.name: Dark Transfer

skill2.description:
Mi Yue sends out a tether forward, linking to the first enemy hit for up to 4s. Every 0.5s, she slows the linked target by 1.25%-2.5% (increases with skill level), steals 10 physical attack and 30 magical attack, deals 30 (30 + 7% magical attack) magical damage, and recovers 10 (10 + 0.25% extra Health) Health.
The tether will break if the distance between her and her target exceeds 1,000 units. If the tether remains intact for the full 4s, she will summon a shadow servant.
Passive: Her Basic Attack is enhanced, dealing 200 (40 + 100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) magical damage, slowing enemies by 10%, and granting 10 Shadow Power.
skill2.name: Ravenous Tether

skill3.description:
Mi Yue disappears into the shadows for 2s, removing all debuffs and gaining 30% Movement Speed and immunity to all effects.
Upon disappearing and returning, she deals 380 (380 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
If she lands a hit upon returning, she summons a shadow servant.
skill3.name: Umbral Moon

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Mi Yue can start trading as soon as she has Ravenous Tether. Keep trading from the start to build up her servants. Don't chase a retreating opponent; recast Dark Transfer to return safely to the wave.
strategy.midGame: After leaving lane, her main role is holding one-on-ones in a side lane. Push the clash lane wave and meet the fighter who comes to stop her with a war of attrition started by Ravenous Tether. Even if the enemy jungler joins for a two-on-one, Umbral Moon makes her immune to effects for a moment, so she can wait out their burst and then turn around. Making a habit of using it after seeing an enemy assassin dive cuts down on deaths. Rather than forcing herself into Tyrant fights, taking a tower on the other side of the map is more her style.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, don't walk in from the front; her first move is linking Ravenous Tether to the enemy's main fighter or marksman from the side. An enemy whose attack is being drained cannot deal their usual damage. When the enemy turns toward her, back off with Dark Transfer's two-step movement, and make chasers whiff with Umbral Moon. While she has plenty of servants, she heals just by walking around, so dragging the fight out is itself a way to win.

combos.title: Stay Tethered and Win the Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Ravenous Tether: link and steal attack) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 1 (Dark Transfer) → Skill 1 (recast to manifest)
combos.description: While tethered, she drains attack from the target and damages and heals at the same time. Holding the tether to the end adds a shadow servant. It breaks with distance, so if the target backs off, recast Dark Transfer to close the gap again.

combos.title: Time the Immunity After Their Move
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Umbral Moon: vanish and remove debuffs) → Skill 1 (Dark Transfer) → Skill 1 (recast to move)
combos.description: While she is in the shadows she is immune to all effects and her debuffs are removed, so don't use it first; time it after seeing the enemy's big ability. Nearby enemies take damage both when she vanishes and when she returns, and a hit on return adds a shadow servant. Afterward, use Dark Transfer's second step to reach safety.

strengths: Ravenous Tether steals the linked enemy's attack, and with her servants' healing she outlasts duels
Umbral Moon makes her immune to all effects for a moment and removes her debuffs
Each skill adds servants, so the longer a fight lasts, the more her damage and healing grow
weaknesses: No hard crowd control, so she has few ways to protect allies or catch enemies
Her damage builds over time, so her healing cannot keep up in burst trades
She suits small fights and has less impact in head-on teamfights

playstyle.style: Mi Yue summons shadow servants every time she uses a skill, wearing enemies down with their automatic attacks and her tether. Ravenous Tether steals attack from the linked enemy while she keeps healing. Her ultimate, Umbral Moon, makes her vanish into the shadows and become immune to all effects for a moment, letting her dodge an enemy's key ability and reset.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who want to pressure with both her servants and herself and win long brawls. She has no way to stop enemies, so vanishing with Umbral Moon at the dangerous moment is the core of her staying power. She does better holding one-on-ones in a side lane than in head-on teamfights.

synergy.reason: Dolia's Celestial Melody resets the longest cooldown, which for Lu Bu means a second Tremble, Mortals.
Guiguzi pulls enemies into one spot and stuns them, so Tremble, Mortals lands on the whole group.

counters.reason: Marco Polo's true damage ignores the defense of Lu Bu's ring, and his blinks keep him out of reach.
Zhang Fei knocks Lu Bu out of his own ring, and Unbridled Outburst makes Zhang Fei immune while roaring.

passive.description:
Lu Bu's Crescent Halberd becomes enchanted for 8s after striking an enemy hero. Basic Attacks and skills deal an equal amount of true damage while it is enchanted. When not enchanted, Basic Attacks and skills gain 35% Physical Pierce.
While his weapon is enchanted, Lu Bu recovers 80 (80 + 1.3% extra Health) Health on each Basic Attack hit.
passive.name: Bloodthirsty Ancestry

skill1.description: Lu Bu slashes in the target direction with his Crescent Halberd, dealing 600 (600 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. He loses his enhanced state if the slash does not hit an enemy hero. While enhanced, he recovers 130 (130 + 2.5% extra Health) Health whenever he hits an enemy with his Skill 1.
skill1.name: Impaling Thrust

skill2.description:
Lu Bu captures the souls of enemies in the target area, dealing 100 (100 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage and reducing their Movement Speed by 15% for 3s.
Each captured soul grants him a shield, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack of shield negates 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) damage. He converts 25% of his remaining shield to Health every second, gaining 1 Health for every 2 points of shield.
skill2.name: Souleater

skill3.description:
Lu Bu leaps to the target location and creates a ring of slaughter, launching enemies within range for 1s. He gains crowd control immunity during the leap. Upon landing, he swings his Crescent Halberd, dealing 650 (650 + 240% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. While his Halberd is enchanted, he recovers 130 (130 + 2.5% extra Health) Health for every enemy hero hit.
He gains 150 physical defense and 150 magical defense within the ring. Enemies that touch the edge of the ring take 150 (150 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage and are slowed by 30% for 2s. He restores Health for every enemy hero who takes damage this way.
skill3.name: Tremble, Mortals

strategy.earlyGame: In lane, Lu Bu aims Impaling Thrust at the enemy hero rather than the minions. Missing enemy heroes while enchanted strips the enhanced state, so avoid swinging just to clear the wave. Open trades with Souleater and let its shield absorb the return damage. Until he learns his ultimate he has no movement skill at all, so while the enemy jungler is out of sight, stay close to your tower.
strategy.midGame: Once Tremble, Mortals is learned, where Lu Bu lands decides the shape of every skirmish. It ignores crowd control until he lands, so he can wait for the enemy to commit and still go in on top of them. Landing creates the ring of slaughter, and inside it his physical and magical defense rise. Enemies touching the edge are slowed, so anyone trying to escape loses speed on the way out. Once he has landed he has no movement left, so landing at the edge of a fight means walking back in. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, hold the leap until the enemy bunches up and stops moving. Even when opponents start buying defense, the true damage from the enchanted halberd keeps getting through.
strategy.teamfight: Preparation starts before the fight with Souleater. Capture the souls of nearby enemies to stack shields, then leap in with Tremble, Mortals once the enemy formation settles. Land Impaling Thrust on someone while they are launched to enchant the halberd, and from there Basic Attacks keep healing him. Landing toward the enemy's escape route means fleeing enemies cross the edge of the ring and get slowed. If the brawl wears him down, recast Souleater into several enemies to rebuild the shield.

combos.title: Shield Up, Then Drop
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Souleater: a shield per captured soul) → Skill 3 (Tremble, Mortals: crowd control immunity until landing, launch) → Skill 1 (Impaling Thrust) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Stacking shields with Souleater first lets him survive being focused right after he lands. Once down, stay inside the ring of slaughter while landing Impaling Thrust and Basic Attacks.

combos.title: Keep the Halberd Enchanted
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Impaling Thrust: hit an enemy hero) → Basic Attack (true damage and healing) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Souleater: slow and shield)
combos.description: When Impaling Thrust hits an enemy hero, the halberd is enchanted and each Basic Attack restores Health. Missing heroes with it while enchanted strips the enhanced state, so close the distance until it will reach a hero before you swing. Finishing with Souleater slows the target, and with the shield up you can choose to back off or keep hitting.

strengths: While enchanted, Basic Attacks and skills add true damage that gets through high defense
Tremble, Mortals ignores crowd control until he lands and launches every enemy in the area
Souleater's shield grows with each captured soul, and the rest turns into Health
While enchanted, every Basic Attack restores Health, so he can keep brawling
weaknesses: Missing enemy heroes with Impaling Thrust while enchanted strips the enhanced state
Tremble, Mortals is his only movement, so once it is used he has to walk
Without his ultimate, slows are his only way to hold anyone, so kiting enemies are hard to catch
The defense from the ring of slaughter disappears once he steps outside it

playstyle.style: A fighter whose Crescent Halberd becomes enchanted after his skills strike an enemy hero, adding true damage to his Basic Attacks and skills. His only movement skill is his ultimate, Tremble, Mortals: he leaps in, creates a ring of slaughter where he lands, and fights inside it with extra physical and magical defense.
playstyle.suited: How often you land Impaling Thrust on enemy heroes changes both his damage and his healing. While enchanted, a slash that only hits minions strips the enhanced state, so you need the patience to pick what you swing at. Deciding where to land Tremble, Mortals by watching how the enemy bunches up is the most rewarding call he makes.

synergy.reason: Kui drags enemies to him and stuns them nonstop, holding them inside Zhou Yu's fire domain the whole time.
Liu Bang teleports in with Staggering Charge fully charged, and its stun pins enemies right on top of Zhou Yu's flames.

counters.reason: Han Xin shrugs off crowd control during The Unrivaled Spear, so Zhou Yu's stun cannot interrupt the flurry.
Mozi stacks a fresh shield with every skill, absorbing the small ticks Zhou Yu's fire domains chip away.

passive.description:
Zhou Yu's Basic Attacks and skills place fire marks on enemies (including structures) for 4s. At 4 stacks, the marks ignite, dealing 125 (125 + 17% magical attack) magical damage per second for 4s and reducing the target's Movement Speed by 15% for 1s.
Targets cannot gain more marks while burning.
passive.name: Blaze

skill1.description:
Zhou Yu invokes a wind domain. Teammates within the domain gain 5% Movement Speed (up to 5 heroes; effect doubled for Zhou Yu), while enemy heroes' Movement Speed are reduced by 10% for 3s. When the wind is invoked, enemies within range are knocked back in the target direction and take 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage.
If the wind domain overlaps with a fire domain for 1s, a new fire domain spreads in the target direction, dealing 100 (100 + 25% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s. This damage stacks with any existing fire domains.
skill1.name: Wildfire

skill2.description:
Zhou Yu calls down a volley of flaming arrows at the target location, dealing 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and leaving behind a fire domain that lasts for 6.5s. The fire domain deals 100 (100 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s. There can be up to 6 fire domains present at any time, after which creating a new fire domain will extinguish the first one. Zhou Yu stocks 1 volley every 9s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), and up to 3 can be stocked.
Passive: While inside a fire domain, he recovers 35 (35 + 7% magical attack + 2% extra Health) Health every 0.5s.
skill2.name: Scorching Bolt

skill3.description: Zhou Yu unleashes a burst of flames in the target area, dealing 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage. If the flames travel through a fire domain, a firestorm is created, dealing an extra 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and stunning them for 1s.
skill3.name: Flames of War

strategy.earlyGame: Zhou Yu's lane is a placement puzzle for Skill 2's fire arrows. They restock every 9 seconds up to three, and each burn zone lasts 6.5 seconds, so budget one for the wave and one for pressure. The core habit is placing flames where the enemy wants to retreat, shrinking their playable space. You heal while standing in your own fire thanks to the Passive, so trading on top of your flames is a fight you're happy to take. Your Ultimate only stuns when it passes through a burn zone, so even past level 4, everything starts with Skill 2.
strategy.midGame: The 4-minute Tyrant kicks off Zhou Yu's setup game. Thirty seconds before it spawns, push mid and reach the pit first, laying two arrows across the entrance. The enemy detouring around your flames is zoning working exactly as intended. When the fight starts, spread the burn with Skill 1's wind field, knock their formation loose, then send the Ultimate through the widened flames for a multi-man stun. The Passive's 4-stack ignition ticks hard too — in tight corridors, enemies sometimes sit at half HP off placement alone.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Zhou Yu wins fights before they start. Carpet the approach to Overlord or Shadow Tyrant with burn zones: your team gets the wind field's speed while the enemy is forced through flames and slows. With items done, overlapped flames in a narrow path melt even tanks off pure damage over time. The weakness is self-defense — no dash means a read on your position is a death sentence. Stay behind your team, always within reach of your own fire, and keep shooting.
strategy.teamfight: Run the same teamfight script until it's muscle memory. Open with two Skill 2 arrows layered between the teams, push the flames enemy-ward with Skill 1's wind and knockback, then fire the Ultimate through the extended flame line for a clustered 1-second AoE stun. From there, keep feeding restocked arrows onto their escape paths and backline — the enemy is forever choosing between burning and backing off. New and old burn zones stack their damage, so deliberately doubling them on one spot builds a genuinely lethal firepit — a veteran's move.

combos.title: Lay the Fire Line
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (fire domain) → Skill 2 (stacked) → Skill 1 (knockback, spreads the fire) → Skill 3 (firestorm, 1s stun)
combos.description: Skill 3 only stuns when its flames travel through a fire domain, so the fire has to be down first. Once the wind domain covers a fire domain for 1s, a new one spreads in the direction you chose, and old and new domains stack their damage. You stock one volley every 9s up to 3, so spending two on the opener still leaves one in hand.

combos.title: Keep the Marks Alive
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (fire arrows + fire domain) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (knockback) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Marks expire after 4s, so chain a Basic Attack and Skill 1 straight after the arrows. Reach four stacks and the target ignites, taking 125 (Lvl 1) magical damage per second for 4s. A burning target gains no new marks, so hold the follow-up until the fire runs out.

strengths: Overlapped burn zones melt even tanks with sustained damage in narrow terrain
Ultimate through flames becomes an AoE 1-second stun — real CC on a zone mage
Heals while standing in his own fire, making him stubborn on claimed ground
Skill 1's knockback doubles as self-peel and engage-breaking
weaknesses: Setup takes steps, so he reacts poorly to sudden skirmishes and flanks
The Ultimate only stuns through a burn zone — on its own it stops no one
No mobility skill; once his position is read and dived, there's no answer

playstyle.style: An area-denial mage who pre-burns the ground enemies want to stand on, stacking ignition marks until they catch fire. He wins not by aiming at enemies but by removing their real estate.
playstyle.suited: players who shape the ground before the fight reaches it — burn the lanes enemies need, heal while standing in your own fire, and take the corridors early, since only a burn-fed ultimate stuns.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's wind knocks enemies back and pins them in place, so Yango's strings and paper birds all connect.

counters.reason: Diaochan's area damage never stops, so Yango's fragile puppet dies and leaves him stunned.
Gao Changgong stuns and heals off his marked target, undoing whatever Health Yango chips away.

passive.name: Occult Arts - Manipulation
passive.description:
When Yango and the puppet's Basic Attacks hit an enemy hero, they have a 30% chance of granting a Hero Shard and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health.
Yango's Recovery skill is replaced with Hero Shards. He can stock up to 150 Hero Shards, which can be used to turn his puppet into a copy of an enemy hero. He automatically stocks 1 Hero Shard every 10-5s, depending on his level.
Hero Puppet: Consumes 50 Hero Shards to transform the puppet into a copy of the selected hero for 10s. The hero puppet possesses all of the copied hero's skills, but only deals 50% damage and takes an extra 100% damage compared to them. The hero puppet becomes stronger with Yango, dealing 1% more damage for every 15 extra Physical Attack and taking 2% less damage for every 80 extra Health.

skill1.name: Occult Arts - Umbra / Occult Arts - Return

forms.description:
Yango throws the puppet, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. He then starts controlling the puppet. The puppet's Basic Attacks deal 100% physical attack physical damage. When recalled, the puppet purifies crowd control effects from Yango and grants him 40% Movement Speed for 1s, as well as a shield that negates 420 (420 + 6% extra Health) damage.
When the puppet is destroyed, Yango is revealed and stunned for 2s. He is then unable to summon the puppet for 20-16s. If the puppet remains beyond a range of 2,500 from Yango for 5s, it is automatically destroyed.
Normal Puppet: Inherits all of Yango's equipment effects (excluding Revive, Blood Fury, Dark Curtain, and Mana Shield), inherits certain buff effects, and shares Gold and EXP with him.
Retrieves the puppet immediately, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path and launching them for 0.5s.

skill1.description:

skill2.name: Occult Arts - Zhi Chu Luan / Occult Arts - Substitution

The puppet swaps locations with Yango if it is within a range of 900 from him; otherwise, it will move to a location that is 900 from him, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.

skill3.name: Occult Arts - Shadow Crucifixion / Occult Arts - Binding

forms.description: Yango releases two strings then pulls them back, each string dealing 180 (180 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. Enemies hit by both strings take extra physical damage equal to 13% of lost Health and are slowed by 30% for 2s.

The puppet deals 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and slows them by 250 for 2s.
If the skill is used again within 3s, it will enter its 2nd phase. After a brief delay, the puppet will stun enemies continuously, with each strike dealing 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) magical damage.

skill3.skill_name: Occult Arts - Shadow Crucifixion / Occult Arts - Binding
skill3.description: Yango releases two strings then pulls them back, each string dealing 180 (180 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. Enemies hit by both strings take extra physical damage equal to 13% of lost Health and are slowed by 30% for 2s.

skill4.name: Occult Arts - Dispersal / Occult Arts - Breakout

forms.description:
Yango instantly vanishes, cleansing all crowd control effects from himself, then reappears in the target location after a short delay.
Does not cleanse the stun effect from the puppet being destroyed.

The puppet charges in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.
If the puppet's movements have been restricted, then control is passed back to its master.

skill4.skill_name: Occult Arts - Dispersal / Occult Arts - Breakout
skill4.description:
Yango instantly vanishes, cleansing all crowd control effects from himself, then reappears in the target location after a short delay.
Does not cleanse the stun effect from the puppet being destroyed.

strategy.earlyGame: Yango's opening minutes are about collecting shards and getting comfortable on the puppet. Shards accrue passively over time, but basic attacks on enemy heroes have a chance to grant extras, so roam between lanes and harass from safe range. Skill 1's puppet doubles as a bush scout, but if it's destroyed, your real body is stunned for 2 seconds and locked out of resummoning for roughly 20 — don't toss it carelessly at enemies with skills still up. Without his puppet, Yango is just a squishy melee hero.
strategy.midGame: Once you bank 50 shards, the Passive's hero transformation widens your playbook. The copy matches the original's kit exactly, so the standard play is borrowing an enemy with CC or a dash as your engage tool. Ganks start with Skill 1's puppet launch: the 0.5-second knock-up on hit, whittling through puppet control, then the recall — its purify and shield transfer to your body as you finish with Skill 2's hidden weapons. Keep the real body behind walls and bushes, showing the enemy only the puppet. That habit separates Yango players.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, the puppet is the perfect decoy. Walk it into the enemy's path before the fight; when they burn skills on it, that's your cue. It takes 100% extra damage and breaks easily, so recall early when threatened and convert the purify and shield into your own engage. For the finish, chain Skill 2's four paper birds into Skill 3's strings, which pull you back out as they land. The 13% of lost Health only applies to a target hit by both strings — land one and it's chip damage, nothing more. Line up the angle before you fire, especially on a target already low. Once your real body is caught, the fight is basically lost, so check your exit before anything else.
strategy.teamfight: The rule is simple: the real Yango doesn't fight. Send the puppet in from a flank to pressure their backline, and only move your body once you've confirmed their CC and big cooldowns have gone into the doll. The moment they spend a major skill on the puppet is the only window where you're allowed forward. Start with Skill 1's knock-up, and once a target is pinched between puppet and body — with 50 shards turning that puppet into a copy of an enemy hero — you are effectively more than two attackers. Skill 3's strings can cap a combo or buy your spacing back. When a collapse actually lands on you, the answer is Skill 4: it cleanses every crowd control effect and drops you somewhere else. Hold it for that, and remember it cannot clear the 2-second stun from a destroyed puppet.

combos.title: Bind With the Puppet, Finish in Person
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (launch the puppet, 0.5s launch) → Skill 3 in puppet form (250 slow) → recast within 3s (continuous stun) → Skill 1 in puppet form (recall) → Skill 2
combos.description: A clean launch buys 0.5s of hang time. Follow with puppet-form Skill 3, then recast inside 3 seconds to reach the second phase, which stuns continuously after a brief delay. Recalling purifies crowd control from Yango and hands him 40% Movement Speed for 1s plus a 420 (Lvl 1) shield to walk in behind. If the puppet is about to die, recall early — losing it stuns him for 2s.

combos.title: Swap Into Their Backline
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (launch the puppet) → Skill 4 in puppet form (charge deeper) → Skill 2 in puppet form (swap places) → Skill 1 in puppet form (recall) → Skill 3
combos.description: Within 900 units, puppet-form Skill 2 trades the puppet's position with Yango's outright. Charge the puppet past the enemy first and the swap plants him behind them. The recall itself launches anyone in its path for 0.5s, which is the window for the strings. Land both strings and the target takes an extra 13% of their lost Health.

strengths: The puppet leads, soaking enemy skills and attention while his body stays hidden
50 shards turn the puppet into a copy of an enemy hero, borrowing their ace card for 10 seconds
Skill 1's knock-up plus the recall's purify and shield cover offense and defense
Skill 3 adds 13% of lost Health when both strings connect, and creates distance as it lands
weaknesses: The puppet takes double damage, and its destruction stuns the real body for 2 seconds
Controlling the puppet leaves the real body exposed to a pincer
Extremely demanding to pilot — below mastery, you get half the hero

playstyle.style: A one-of-a-kind puppeteer who fights through his puppet while keeping his real body safe. You manage two positions at once, trading mind games with the enemy's vision.
playstyle.suited: players who enjoy complexity for its own sake — piloting two positions at once, where losing the puppet stuns your real body for two seconds and knowing when to recall is what practice buys.

synergy.reason: Li Bai can dash in on Dun's stun, build Sword Energy, and then return to where he started.
Arli can spend her parasol-less speed window attacking rather than escaping, since Dun dives in ahead of her.

counters.reason: Lu Bu brings true damage or Physical Pierce either way, so Dun's Health and defense stop neither.
Diaochan stacks floral marks from outside Dun's reach, and their true damage detonation ignores his defense.

passive.description: If Dun takes damage while his Health is below 50%, he becomes enhanced for 8s. While enhanced, whenever he hits an enemy with a Basic Attack or skill, he recovers 220 (220 +6% extra Health) Health. This passive effect can only be triggered once every 25s. (Decreases with hero level.)
passive.name: Unyielding Might

skill1.description:
Dun swings his blade, creating a gust of wind in the target direction, dealing 350 (350 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25% for 2s.
If the wind hits any enemy, he can use the skill again within 5s in the target direction, dealing 350 (350 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 1s.
skill1.name: Wind Slash

skill2.description: Dun deals 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and gains a shield that negates damage equal to 500 (500 + 12% extra Health) for 5s. His next 3 Basic Attacks are enhanced for 8s, dealing an extra 150 (150 + 45% extra physical attack) true damage each. Hitting enemies reduces the cooldown of his Ultimate by 1s.
skill2.name: Gale's Benediction

skill3.description:
Dun throws his chained blade in the target direction, which stops upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range.
The blade stuns the first enemy it hits for 1s. Dun deals 360 (360 + 10% extra Health) physical damage to enemies near the blade and pulls himself to its location. Upon reaching the blade's location, he deals 360 (360 + 10% extra Health) physical damage to nearby enemies again.
Dun gains immunity to crowd control while using this skill.
skill3.name: Unruly Blade

strategy.earlyGame: Dun's Clash Lane game starts with landing the first Wind Slash. If it hits, the second cast follows with a launch, so clearing the wave and chipping the opponent take the same motion. Once he is below half Health, taking damage triggers Unyielding Might and every hit restores Health, so he can keep fighting through a slightly losing brawl. It only triggers at intervals, so right after it has been used, step back and avoid the follow-up.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Unruly Blade, Dun can take the role of the one who catches. The blade stops on the first enemy it hits, stuns that enemy and pulls him to its location. If someone else stands between him and the target, the blade hits them instead, so wait for a clear line or a chance to take the target's flank from a bush. He is immune to crowd control while using it, so enemy CC cannot stop him on the way in. Once the fight starts, cycle Gale's Benediction and the enhanced Basic Attacks; landing them shortens Unruly Blade's cooldown and brings the next throw sooner. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, the moment an enemy back-liner steps forward is the time to throw.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Dun's work starts once Unruly Blade has carried him into the enemy team. On a hit, the pull puts him right next to the target; land both Wind Slash casts for the launch, then put up the shield from Gale's Benediction. Gale's Benediction hits the enemies around him, so casting it after getting inside their team catches more of them. Below half Health, Unyielding Might triggers and every enhanced Basic Attack or skill hit restores Health. Whether he can stay inside the enemy team at that point decides how much he contributes. Stand in the enemy back line's escape path and stick to them until your team catches up.

combos.title: Chain and Launch
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wind Slash: slow) → Skill 3 (Unruly Blade: stun and pull himself in) → Skill 1 (second Wind Slash: launch) → Skill 2 (Gale's Benediction: shield and enhanced Basic Attacks)
combos.description: The second Wind Slash is only available for a short time after the first one hits, so close the gap with Unruly Blade right after landing it. Launching the target with the second cast as the stun wears off keeps them locked down longer. Finish with Gale's Benediction for the shield and stay put, swinging the enhanced Basic Attacks.

combos.title: Fight Back From Low Health
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Gale's Benediction: shield and enhanced Basic Attacks) → Basic Attack (swing the enhanced attacks) → Skill 1 (Wind Slash) → Skill 1 (second Wind Slash)
combos.description: While Unyielding Might is active, every skill or Basic Attack that connects restores Health. More hits mean more healing, so pack the enhanced Basic Attacks from Gale's Benediction and both Wind Slash casts into that window. Hits from Gale's Benediction also shorten Unruly Blade's cooldown, so his next catch comes sooner.

strengths: After dropping below half Health and taking damage, every hit he lands restores Health
One cast of Gale's Benediction gives both a shield and true damage on his next Basic Attacks
He is immune to crowd control while using Unruly Blade
If the first Wind Slash lands, the second follows up with a launch
weaknesses: Unyielding Might only triggers at intervals, so he cannot count on it in back-to-back fights
Unruly Blade stops on the first enemy it hits and will not reach a target behind someone else
The second Wind Slash is only available after the first one hits an enemy
Gale's Benediction only hits enemies right around him

playstyle.style: Once his Health is below half and he takes damage, Dun enters a state where every hit he lands wins Health back. He layers the shield from Gale's Benediction on top of Unyielding Might and fights back from low Health. His ultimate, Unruly Blade, stuns the first enemy it hits and pulls him to the blade, so he can also be the one who catches targets.
playstyle.suited: Unyielding Might only triggers at intervals, so you have to keep fighting until he drops below half and judge whether he can win from there. If you can plan a brawl around the time spent losing Health, his staying power at low Health will pay off. Unruly Blade stops on the first enemy it hits, so you also need the patience to wait when someone else stands in front of your target.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's gust knocks enemies back and stuns them, giving Lady Zhen a still target to stack skills on.
Sun Bin's field only pays off if enemies stay inside, and Lady Zhen's icicles wall off their escape.

counters.reason: Li Bai goes untargetable and cleanses every debuff during Stroke of Genius and Flickering Flurry, so Lady Zhen's control never sticks.
Sima Yi heals off magical damage, and Lady Zhen's entire kit is magical, so she cannot out-trade him.

passive.description: Every time Lady Zhen's skills deal damage, she places a frozen mark on the enemy for 7s, up to 3 stacks. At max stacks, the target takes 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and is frozen for 0.75s. The duration of repeated freeze effects is reduced to 0.5s.
passive.name: Frozen Touch

skill1.description: Lady Zhen conjures icicles at the target location, blocking heroes and dealing 500 (500 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s. The icicles last 8s and continuously inflict 10% slow on nearby enemies. If Lady Zhen is within range when the icicles are conjured, she will be frozen in an invincible state for 3s. The icicles shatter violently when the skill ends or is canceled, dealing 150 (150 + 35% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and inflicting 10% slow for 3s. Damage is doubled at the center.
skill1.name: Ocean of Tears

skill2.description:
Lady Zhen fires a water orb at the target which bounces between nearby enemy units up to 5-7 times (max number increases when skill level reaches 3 and 5). Each bounce deals 230 (230 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies.
Icicles are considered targets. Once the orb is unable to continue bouncing, it will disappear at its current target's location after a 3s delay.
skill2.name: Flowing Sigh

skill3.description:
Lady Zhen unleashes a water spirit in the target direction, knocking back non-hero units. Upon hitting an enemy hero or reaching its maximum range, the water spirit forms a pool, dealing 300 (300 + 65% magical attack) magical damage to the first hero hit and reducing their Movement Speed by 90% for 1s.
The pool lasts for 5s, dealing 150 (150 + 32% magical attack) magical damage every second to enemies in its range and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1.5s.
skill3.name: Destructive Deluge

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Lady Zhen starts by clearing the wave with Flowing Sigh. The orb bounces between minions, so casting it as the opponent steps close to the wave clears and spreads marks at once. Adding Ocean of Tears to a target already marked by the bounces can reach a freeze even early on. On its own the icicle cast is easy to walk away from, so use it as a placed skill for the moment the opponent steps forward. Until she has her ultimate, don't overextend; focus on wearing the opponent's Health down.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Destructive Deluge, catching enemies with her jungler's ganks gets much easier. The first hero hit can barely move, so firing it as your jungler arrives cuts off the escape. Before Tyrant or Overlord, lay Destructive Deluge's pool across a narrow river path; enemies who step in take damage and slow down, so they have to choose between going around or forcing through. She stays fragile, so always stand behind your front line.
strategy.teamfight: Before a teamfight, fire Destructive Deluge into a narrow approach and break up the enemy formation with the pool. Pour Flowing Sigh into the stalled group and the bouncing orb spreads marks among them, sometimes freezing several at once. If she is targeted, raise Ocean of Tears at her feet to become invincible and wait for her team to come back. She cannot move while invincible, so use it when teammates can follow up as it ends. If Destructive Deluge misses, she has nothing to start a lockdown with until it returns, so be ready to back off.

combos.title: Stop Them, Then Complete the Marks
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Destructive Deluge: heavily slows the first hero hit) → Skill 1 (Ocean of Tears: launch) → Skill 2 (Flowing Sigh)
combos.description: Land the hard-to-hit Ocean of Tears on the target held by Destructive Deluge, then follow up with Flowing Sigh. Each skill hit adds one mark, so three hits are enough to reach the freeze.

combos.title: Spread Marks in Lane
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Flowing Sigh) → Skill 1 (Ocean of Tears: launch and icicles)
combos.description: Even without a freeze, the launch and the slow from the lingering icicles make the trade worth it.

combos.title: Freeze Herself in Her Own Icicles
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (raise icicles with herself inside to become invincible) → end the freeze (the icicles shatter on nearby enemies) → Skill 2 (Flowing Sigh)
combos.description: When someone dives her, raise the icicles where she is inside the area. If she is within range when they form, she freezes herself and becomes invincible for a while, making the enemy's attacks whiff. Ending the freeze shatters the icicles, and enemies at the center of the blast take the most damage.

strengths: Skill damage stacks frozen marks, and three of them freeze the target
Ocean of Tears' icicles cannot be crossed by heroes, so she can close off paths
Flowing Sigh bounces between enemies and spreads marks across a group
Raising icicles with herself inside makes her invincible for a while
weaknesses: Ocean of Tears is easy to walk out of unless the target is already stopped
A missed Destructive Deluge leaves her without a way to start a lockdown until it is back
No movement skill, so positioning mistakes are hard to undo
She cannot move while invincible and is exposed when it ends

playstyle.style: Lady Zhen is a mage who stacks frozen marks with every skill hit and freezes any target that reaches three. Ocean of Tears creates icicles that heroes cannot pass, and Flowing Sigh bounces between enemies to spread marks. Her ultimate, Destructive Deluge, nearly stops the first hero it hits in place and is where her chain into a freeze begins.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who would rather measure their work in how long they held enemies than in kills. Where she raises icicles changes which paths are open, so players who like thinking about placement will enjoy her. With no movement skill, she has few ways to recover from a positioning mistake on her own.

synergy.reason: Donghuang's suppression freezes a target completely, so Fatih can land every slash of The King's Blade on it.
Guiguzi's pull bunches enemy heroes together, so Sacred Tree Blessing grants Fatih more max Health for each one nearby.

counters.reason: Lu Bu's ring of Tremble, Mortals hands him heavy defenses, so Fatih's purely physical damage cannot break him.
Mulan's Balance stacks detonate into a silence, and Fatih cannot answer with Sacred Tree Blessing.

passive.description: After using a skill, Fatih gains 1 enhanced Basic Attack (up to a maximum of 5) as well as 35% Attack Speed. Enhanced Basic Attacks become consecutive long range slashes that recover 100 (100 + 1.6% extra Health) Health (halved when hitting non-hero units).
passive.name: Only the Strong

skill1.description:
Fatih charges forward and slashes, dealing 300 (300 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. This skill can be used up to 3 times. The third slash launches the enemy for 0.5s.
Every unused slash reduces Cooldown by 35%.
skill1.name: The King's Blade

skill2.description:
Fatih unleashes sword energy, dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and slowing them by 25% for 2s.
Recovers 200 (200 + 3% extra Health) Health for each hero hit (halved for non-hero units).
Hitting enemies with Basic Attacks reduces this skill's Cooldown by 5%.
While Sacred Tree Blessing is active, this skill unleashes 1 additional blast of sword energy.
skill2.name: The King's Return

skill3.description:
Fatih calls upon divine power to remove all crowd control effects on himself, dealing 230 (230 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies, as well as gaining 450 (450 + 7% extra Health) max Health (increases by 20% for every 1 enemy hero nearby) and 10% Resistance for 8s.
While this skill is active, Skill 2 and enhanced Basic Attacks unleash an extra wave of sword energy (50% damage) and continuously grant enhanced Basic Attacks.
Tap again to end the skill.
skill3.name: Sacred Tree Blessing

strategy.earlyGame: Fatih's Clash Lane edge is a healing trade: land Skill 2 on the enemy laner and 200 HP comes right back. Until level 4, the loop is simple — tag your opponent with the sword wave, win the sustain war, and reset with your Passive's empowered basic attacks whenever you get chipped. Skill 1 stores three casts, but burning all three every time is a mistake: stop at one or two and each unspent cast refunds 35% of the cooldown, letting you out-tempo your opponent on rotations. Bank the third cast's knock-up as self-defense for when the enemy jungler shows up — it visibly cuts down on early deaths.
strategy.midGame: The moment you learn your Ultimate at level 4 is your first real power spike. It grants crowd control immunity, raises your max HP, and — crucially — the HP bonus grows another 20% per nearby enemy hero, so you can win skirmishes even against two opponents. While it's active, Skill 2 and your empowered basics each fire an extra sword wave, and your effective damage jumps to roughly 1.5 times normal. Be the first one into the Tyrant-fight scrum and brawl while you heal. Basic attacks also shave Skill 2's cooldown on hit, so never stop swinging — that's the secret to his staying power.
strategy.lateGame: Late game you're a dual threat: side-lane pushing and teamfighting. Almost nobody stops a five-item Fatih head-on, so welcome anyone foolish enough to duel you. One catch: your healing only pays full value against heroes — it's halved on minions — so recovering HP by farming a lane takes longer than you'd think. Before a big fight, don't get greedy; recall and reset. You are at your absolute strongest during the Ultimate's 8-second window and noticeably softer once it drops, so commit to finishing fights inside it.
strategy.teamfight: The advanced play is holding your Ultimate instead of opening with it — pop it the instant enemy CC is aimed your way, and the immunity lets you walk straight through their lockdown into the middle of their team. From there, spray long-range empowered basics and bonus sword waves; there are stretches where your healing genuinely outpaces their damage. Any nearby squishy target is a fine focus, but don't chase deep — the second your Ultimate expires, focus fire melts you. When in doubt, just stand next to your frontline and keep swinging. The enemy formation cracks on its own.

combos.title: Sword-Wave Sustain Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (2s slow, heals on hero hit) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 1 (stop after one slash)
combos.description: Skill 2 pays full healing only when it connects with a hero; against minions it is halved. Every skill cast banks an enhanced basic that heals as well, so wave-then-basic refills whatever the trade cost you. Stopping Skill 1 after a single slash leaves two unused casts, cutting its cooldown by 70%.

combos.title: Blessing All-In
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (removes crowd control on himself, raises max Health and Resistance) → Skill 2 (extra wave of sword energy) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 1 x3 (third slash launches for 0.5s)
combos.description: Hold Skill 3 until enemies have surrounded you rather than opening with it. The max Health bonus grows by 20% for every enemy hero nearby, so a two-on-one makes Fatih tougher instead of weaker. Inside the 8s window Skill 2 and enhanced basics each add one more wave of sword energy, and all three Skill 1 slashes go out last so the 0.5s launch cuts off the escape.

strengths: Every skill cast banks an empowered basic and 35% bonus attack speed
The Ultimate's HP bonus scales per nearby enemy — tankier when outnumbered
Outstanding sustain from Skill 2's on-hit healing plus empowered basics
Smart Skill 1 charge management massively compresses his cooldowns
weaknesses: Healing requires hitting heroes, so he slowly bleeds out in poke wars
Noticeably squishier whenever the Ultimate is down
Lacks a gap closer and has no answer to enemies who keep their distance

playstyle.style: A berserker who stacks empowered attacks by cycling skills, healing as he swings. His crowd-control-immune ultimate plants him in the center of the fight, out-sustaining the damage aimed at him.
playstyle.suited: players who want to be the last one standing in the middle — casts bank empowered attacks, the hits heal you back, and the ultimate grows with every enemy nearby, so never plan an exit.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's Time Flux speeds up teammates too, letting Dian Wei close his opening gap in one go.
Zhuangzi's marks raise teammates' Movement Speed, so Dian Wei can stay glued to whoever he jumps on.

counters.reason: Mi Yue's Ravenous Tether keeps draining Dian Wei's physical attack until he can no longer win a trade.
Liang's Power Word - Control pins Dian Wei in place and burns him down with magical damage before he can swing back.

passive.description:
All of Dian Wei's skills can cleanse crowd controls. Each successful cleanse grants Mounting Rage for up to 6 stacks, each stack increasing his Physical Attack and Attack Range for 6s.
Mounting Rage: Each stack increases 15-29 physical attack and 35 Attack Range.
Cleansing hard crowd controls and soft crowd controls grants 2 and 1 stack(s) of Mounting Rage respectively.
passive.name: Mounting Rage

skill1.description: Dian Wei gains 60% Movement Speed, which diminishes over 3s. His next Basic Attack is enhanced, granting an Attack Range equivalent to his max passive stacks, and dealing 220 (220 + 50% extra physical attack) extra physical damage to nearby enemies. When using the enhanced Basic Attack, he will charge toward a target that is beyond his normal Basic Attack range.
skill1.name: Holding On to Sanity

skill2.description:
Dian Wei tramples the ground, dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range while slowing them by 25% for 2s. Whenever his Skill 2 hits an enemy, it enhances him for 3s, during which he gains 200% Attack Speed and 20% Basic Attack Lifesteal. For 3s, each Basic Attack hit also restores 30 Health to him.
If he misses, he only gains half of the Attack Speed, Lifesteal, and extra Health recovery effects.
skill2.name: Outburst

skill3.description: Dian Wei launches a leaping slash at the target enemy, dealing 320 (320 + 90% extra physical attack) true damage while slowing them by 30% for 3s. Grants 1 stack of Mounting Rage for each enemy hero hit. If this skill lands a hit, he becomes enhanced for 5s, during which he deals extra true damage to enemies equal to 2% of their Health.
skill3.name: Leap of Fury

strategy.earlyGame: In the jungle, Dian Wei clears camps by landing Outburst on monsters for its attack speed boost. Until he has Leap of Fury, focus on clearing safely rather than forcing plays. Gank only where Holding On to Sanity's speed gets him there comfortably. When contesting monsters with the enemy jungler, a landed Outburst gives him the attack speed and lifesteal to win the brawl.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Leap of Fury, his ganks gain real threat. The true damage that follows Leap of Fury gets through even defensive items. The key move is to watch for the enemy's stun, cleanse it with a skill and hit straight back. His only gap closers are Holding On to Sanity's enhanced attack and Leap of Fury, so avoid being kited from range after both are used. Diving alongside your team's crowd control is safest.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, go in second after your team starts the fight. Leap onto a squishy enemy or a damaged frontliner with Leap of Fury, then land Outburst for its attack speed and lifesteal. Whether Outburst lands decides much of the brawl that follows. Cleanse the enemy's lockdown calmly with a skill and turn it into bonus attack. The real danger is the moment he runs out of ways to cleanse, so never stay in the middle of the enemy team with every skill spent.

combos.title: Gank With Leap of Fury
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Leap of Fury: leap for true damage and a slow) → Skill 2 (Outburst: attack speed and lifesteal) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Holding On to Sanity: charging enhanced attack)
combos.description: The point is to fit as many hits as possible into the window after Leap of Fury lands, so the Outburst that follows needs to land. A miss halves the attack speed and lifesteal and changes how the brawl goes.

combos.title: Turn Their Crowd Control Into a Counterattack
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Outburst: cleanse and gain attack speed) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Holding On to Sanity: charging enhanced attack) → Skill 3 (Leap of Fury)
combos.description: Cleansing hard crowd control raises his Physical Attack and Attack Range more. Cleansing with Outburst also grants its attack speed boost, so the moment right after being stopped is the time to hit back.

strengths: Any of his skills cleanses crowd control, and each cleanse raises his Physical Attack and Attack Range
A landed Outburst sharply raises his Attack Speed and lifesteal
After Leap of Fury, each hit adds true damage based on max Health, which gets through tough targets
Holding On to Sanity's speed and its enhanced attack, which reaches beyond normal range, close the gap
weaknesses: A missed Outburst grants only half the Attack Speed and lifesteal
His gap closers are Holding On to Sanity and Leap of Fury; once both are used, distant enemies are out of reach
Opponents who use no crowd control give him no cleanse bonus
Once his skills are spent, he also has no way to cleanse

playstyle.style: Dian Wei is a jungler who can cleanse crowd control with any of his skills, gaining Physical Attack and Attack Range each time he does. When Outburst lands, his Attack Speed and lifesteal jump, and he becomes far stronger in a brawl. His ultimate, Leap of Fury, leaps onto a target for true damage, and for a while afterward each hit adds true damage based on the target's max Health.
playstyle.suited: His basic pattern is taking the enemy's crowd control, cleansing it and hitting back, so he suits players who stay calm when stopped and answer with a skill. Whether Outburst lands changes the outcome of a brawl, so judging when to get close enough matters too. He has few ways to reach enemies who keep their distance, so choosing when to dive is part of playing him.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one spot, so Musashi's ultimate catches several of them as he lands.
Zhang Fei slows nearby enemies with every skill once he transforms, so Musashi's duel target has nowhere to run.

counters.reason: Diaochan cycles her skills far faster inside Flowery Potential, so Musashi dives in and she simply blinks away.
Liang's suppression lands the moment Musashi's super armor ends and the trade begins.

passive.description:
Musashi receives 1 Vigor upon using skills, for up to 2 stacks. While he has Vigor, he gains enhanced Basic Attacks that consume 1 Vigor, are not affected by Attack Speed, and reduce the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2 by 1s upon hitting an enemy.
While he has 1 Vigor:
If the target's Health is above 50%, his next Basic Attack is enhanced to a dual-blade slash, dealing 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
If the target's Health is below 50%, his next Basic Attack is enhanced to a forward slash, dealing 45 (45 + 15% extra physical attack) (+ 6% of target's lost Health) extra physical damage.
While he has 2 Vigor:
His next Basic Attack lets him dash to the target, dealing 187 (20 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and slowing them by 25% for 1s.
passive.name: Niten Ichiryuu

skill1.description:
Musashi unleashes a wave of sword energy forward that knocks down enemy projectiles, deals 390 (390 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path, and slows the enemies by 25% for 1s.
He gains crowd control immunity when using this skill.
skill1.name: Illuminating Slash

skill2.description: Musashi dashes forward, dealing 210 (210 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. If he hits an enemy, he gains a shield that negates 330 (330 + 6% extra Health) damage and reduces this skill's Cooldown by 50%.
skill2.name: Extreme Speed

skill3.description:
Musashi locks onto an enemy hero and dashes toward them. Upon arrival, deals 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launches them for 1s. The target is then marked by Musashi for a duel to the death for 5s. All of the target's recovery effects are delayed until after the duel.
Musashi has crowd control immunity and takes 50% less damage during the dash.
skill3.name: Duel to the Death

strategy.earlyGame: In the jungle, Musashi clears by hitting monsters with Extreme Speed; its cooldown shortens when it hits, which speeds up his route. From the very first clear, get used to putting one basic attack after every skill. Each enhanced attack that lands shortens the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2, so this habit shows up directly in how fast he clears and how many skills he has for ganks. Until he has his ultimate, there is no need to walk into the enemy jungle; take river vision and look for the first target to duel.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Duel to the Death, start one-on-ones with enemies left alone in the side lanes. The target's healing is delayed during the duel, which makes fighters who rely on sustain easier to beat. Before Tyrant or Overlord, Illuminating Slash knocks down enemy projectiles, so he can stand in front of his team during river trades. Against targets below half Health his enhanced attacks deal damage based on their lost Health, so his finishing damage rises as the trade goes on. Before you dash in, ask whether the target can be finished during the duel, and hold off when in doubt.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, don't start in the middle; hold Illuminating Slash ready to knock down the enemy's projectiles. Once their crowd control has been used, flank in with Extreme Speed. Go for a marksman or mage who has stepped too far forward, and after the launch from Duel to the Death, alternate skills and enhanced attacks to keep the cooldowns turning. Avoid staying where several enemies can hit him, and don't waste enhanced attacks; then even inside a teamfight he can create his one-on-one.

combos.title: Finish Them Within the Duel
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Duel to the Death: dash and launch) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 2 (Extreme Speed: shield) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 1 (Illuminating Slash: slow) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Duel to the Death dashes at the chosen target and reduces the damage he takes during the dash. After landing, alternate skills and basic attacks so each enhanced attack keeps shortening the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2. If the target is not finished while their healing is delayed, they get a chance to recover.

combos.title: Flank With Two Vigor
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Extreme Speed: dash and shield) → Skill 1 (Illuminating Slash: slow) → Basic Attack (two Vigor turns it into a dash) → Skill 2 (Extreme Speed)
combos.description: Using Extreme Speed and Illuminating Slash back to back without a basic attack in between builds two Vigor. With two Vigor, the enhanced attack becomes a dash to the target that also slows. Extreme Speed's cooldown shortens when it hits an enemy, so he can chase again even if the first round does not finish them.

strengths: Illuminating Slash knocks down enemy projectiles in its path
Duel to the Death dashes at a target he chooses and delays their recovery
Each enhanced basic attack that lands shortens the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2
Against targets below half Health, his attacks deal damage based on their lost Health
weaknesses: If the skill-then-attack rhythm breaks, his damage drops sharply
Head-on brawls where several enemies surround him are hard
If he cannot finish the target during the duel, their delayed healing comes back
He fights up close, so enemies who keep their distance are out of reach

playstyle.style: Musashi is a jungler who builds Vigor every time he uses a skill and spends it on enhanced basic attacks. What the enhanced attack does depends on whether the target is above or below half Health and how much Vigor he has, and each hit shortens the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2. Illuminating Slash knocks down enemy projectiles in its path, and his ultimate, Duel to the Death, dashes at a chosen target and delays their recovery.
playstyle.suited: Keeping up the rhythm of one basic attack after every skill makes a big difference to his damage and pace. If you enjoy judging whether a chosen target can be worn down within five seconds, deciding when to start a duel is where he gets interesting. Long head-on brawls surrounded by several enemies are not his strength.

synergy.reason: Lian Po's Tremor Smash launches everyone in range, opening the exact window Li Bai needs for Flickering Flurry.
Dun's Wind Slash chains a slow into a launch, holding targets still long enough for Li Bai to close in.

counters.reason: Mozi's barrier stuns anything touching it, so Li Bai, who can only close by dashing, gets locked down on entry.
Donghuang's Forsaken Contract suppresses Li Bai when he dives in alone, forcing him to share all damage taken.

passive.description: Whenever Li Bai hits a non-structure enemy unit with his Basic Attack, he gains 1 Sword Energy, for up to 4 stacks. Stacks last for 3s and their duration is reset for each enemy hit. At 4 stacks, he enters Way of the Sword, an enhanced state where he gains an extra 30 physical attack and unlocks his Ultimate.
passive.name: Way of the Sword

skill1.description:
Li Bai can dash twice in the target direction with Drunken Sword Style, dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and stunning them for 0.5s while gaining 1 Sword Energy. He returns to his original location after using the skill a third time.
The interval between skill uses cannot exceed 5s.
skill1.name: Stupor Slash

skill2.description:
Li Bai conjures a Green Lotus Sword Formation around himself, dealing 200 (200 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
The sword formation deals 325 (325 + 115% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies touching its edge, while inflicting extreme slow for 1s and reducing their defense by 150 for 3s.
While creating the formation, Li Bai removes all debuffs from himself and becomes untargetable.
When he is inside the sword formation, he has a 10% chance to dodge Basic Attacks from enemies inside the formation (doubled for Basic Attacks dealt from outside the formation).
skill2.name: Stroke of Genius

skill3.description:
Li Bai transforms into sword energy and slashes 5 times at the target area, each slash dealing 240 (240 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. When hitting multiple enemy heroes, the damage is reduced by 15% for each subsequent hero hit, for a max reduction of 30%.
He removes all debuffs from himself and becomes untargetable for the duration of this skill.
skill3.name: Flickering Flurry

strategy.earlyGame: In the jungle, Li Bai needs Sword Energy to use Flickering Flurry, so his ways to engage are limited until he learns his ultimate. Leave early buff contests to his team and keep clearing along a safe route. Making a habit of weaving basic attacks into his clear to keep Sword Energy up prevents moments where his ultimate is not ready when needed. If the enemy jungler invades, don't force a fight; use the third Stupor Slash to return to his starting point and leave.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Flickering Flurry, hit nearby minions or monsters before a gank and go in at full Sword Energy. The flow is stunning with Stupor Slash's dash, lowering defense with Stroke of Genius's edge, then slashing with Flickering Flurry unlocked by the enhanced state. After the kill, return with the third Stupor Slash and leave before the counterattack. He is untargetable during Stroke of Genius and Flickering Flurry, so he can slash while dodging enemy skills. Even with his items complete, avoid diving at the start of a teamfight. If enemy crowd control is still available when his untargetable window ends, he is easily caught and killed. Wait in a side bush until the enemy's lockdown skills are used on his team, then go in with Stupor Slash the moment their formation breaks. Flickering Flurry deals less damage when it hits multiple enemy heroes, so aim for one isolated target rather than a group.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Li Bai spends a long time waiting. Hold back the urge to go in as soon as the fight starts, and only move after confirming that the enemy's stuns and pulls have been used on his team. When he goes in, follow Stupor Slash's dash by making enemies step on Stroke of Genius's edge, then slash the key back-liner with Flickering Flurry. After the slashes, use the third Stupor Slash to return out of the fight, then hit nearby minions to rebuild Sword Energy before his next turn.

combos.title: Build Sword Energy, Then Strike
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (build Sword Energy on minions or monsters) → Skill 1 (Stupor Slash: dash twice and stun) → Skill 2 (Stroke of Genius: edge lowers defense and applies extreme slow) → Skill 3 (Flickering Flurry) → Skill 1 (third cast to return)
combos.description: Flickering Flurry can only be used in the enhanced state at full Sword Energy, so hit minions or monsters to build it before going in. Only enemies touching Stroke of Genius's edge get the defense reduction and extreme slow, so place it where they will step on the edge. The third Stupor Slash cannot be used if too much time passes, so press it right after the slashes end to return.

combos.title: Build Sword Energy With Three Dashes
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Stupor Slash: dash, stun and gain Sword Energy) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (second cast) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (third cast to return)
combos.description: Each Stupor Slash dash grants 1 Sword Energy, and basic attacks add 1 each as well. A round trip alone reaches the enhanced state, so he can go in on his real target with Flickering Flurry ready. Waiting too long between casts loses the third-cast return, so keep pressing without stopping.

strengths: He is untargetable and sheds debuffs during Stroke of Genius and Flickering Flurry
The third Stupor Slash returns him to his starting point, making it easy to leave after an engage
Lowering defense with Stroke of Genius's edge before Flickering Flurry concentrates heavy damage on one target
weaknesses: He cannot use Flickering Flurry without full Sword Energy, so engages need preparation
Flickering Flurry's damage drops when it hits multiple enemy heroes, so it works poorly on grouped enemies
Waiting too long between Stupor Slash casts leaves him unable to return and stranded among enemies

playstyle.style: Li Bai is a jungler who builds Sword Energy with basic attacks before unleashing his ultimate, Flickering Flurry. At full Sword Energy he enters an enhanced state, gaining physical attack and unlocking Flickering Flurry. He dashes in twice with Stupor Slash and returns to his original location on the third cast, so he sets his own path in and out.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who can decide on their way back before going in. Stupor Slash returns him on the third cast, but if too much time passes between casts he cannot return, so the routine of pressing through without hesitation needs to be drilled in practice. He cannot use his ultimate without Sword Energy, so not minding the preparation before a fight is another requirement.

synergy.reason: Yaria attaches to Marco Polo with a true-damage shield, letting him close in and keep firing.

counters.reason: Consort Yu turns immune to physical attacks under Protecting Winds, and Marco Polo's bullets are all physical.
Zhang Fei's knockback shoves Marco Polo out of the close range where Roaming Gun pays its damage bonus.

passive.description:
Every time Marco Polo deals damage with his Basic Attacks or skills, he places 1 stack of Destruction on his target (5 stacks on minions). At 10 stacks, they are converted into the Destroyed Defense effect for 5s, and he recovers 30 Energy.
His Basic Attacks and skills deal an extra 100 (100 + 35% extra physical attack) true damage to enemies with Destroyed Defense.
passive.name: Chain Reaction

skill1.description:
Marco Polo fires 5 bullets in the target direction (firing speed scales with Attack Speed) and gains 10% Movement Speed while firing. Each bullet deals 151 (120 + 18% physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hit and grants Marco Polo 10 Energy.
Every 3 bullets fired counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill1.name: Resplendent Revolver

skill2.description:
Marco Polo blinks in the target direction.
Passive: When there are enemy heroes nearby, he gains 15% Movement Speed and deals 20% extra damage.
skill2.name: Roaming Gun

skill3.description:
Marco Polo blinks in the target direction, then moves slowly in the same direction while firing barrages of bullets at nearby enemies for 3s (Firing Speed is affected by Attack Speed). Every barrage deals 213 (170 + 25% physical attack) physical damage.
Every 3 barrages counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill3.name: Fevered Barrage

strategy.earlyGame: Keeping the farm going without running out of Energy is the first goal early on. Resplendent Revolver restores Energy with every bullet that hits, and triggering Destroyed Defense restores more. Minions take several stacks per hit, so Destroyed Defense triggers often while clearing the wave, which keeps his Energy up. Roaming Gun's blink lets him reset the distance when someone engages. Right after using it to attack, he has no exit until it returns.
strategy.midGame: Marco Polo's damage starts with stacking Destruction until Destroyed Defense triggers. Against a target with Destroyed Defense, every Basic Attack and skill hit adds true damage, so he can trade even with frontliners who stack defense. Roaming Gun also raises his damage and Movement Speed while enemy heroes are nearby. In the middle of a trade, don't back off too far; staying close to the enemy while firing is what makes that effect count. Before Tyrant or Overlord, decide which of the two blinks you are saving for escape before you step forward.
