strategy.teamfight: Don't step forward when the fight opens; build Destruction on the enemy frontline from the edge of Resplendent Revolver's reach. Fevered Barrage sprays at enemies around him, so blinking to the side of a clumped group and firing hits many of them. Since he moves slowly during the barrage, it is safer to go in after the enemy's crowd control heroes have used their skills.

combos.title: Stack, Then Barrage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Resplendent Revolver: bullet spray that builds Destruction) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (Fevered Barrage: blink, then barrage)
combos.description: Each Resplendent Revolver bullet adds a Destruction stack, so weave in basic attacks to reach Destroyed Defense before starting the barrage.

combos.title: Slip Out and Fire Again
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Roaming Gun: blink in the target direction) → Skill 1 (Resplendent Revolver: speed up while firing)
combos.description: When someone dives you, slip out with Roaming Gun and fire Resplendent Revolver as you back away. He moves faster while firing, so he can rebuild Destruction stacks while keeping his distance. Fevered Barrage also starts with a blink, but the barrage slows him down, so if you use it to escape, pick the direction before you cast.

strengths: True damage from Destroyed Defense gets through even high-defense frontliners
Roaming Gun and Fevered Barrage give him two blinks
He moves faster while firing Resplendent Revolver, so he can reposition as he shoots
weaknesses: During Fevered Barrage he can only move slowly
Until Destroyed Defense triggers, there is no true damage
Using a blink to attack leaves him without an escape until it returns

playstyle.style: Once Marco Polo has stacked Destruction all the way on a target, his attacks against it start dealing extra true damage. He is a marksman built around that Destroyed Defense effect, getting damage through even high-defense frontliners. With two blinks, Roaming Gun and Fevered Barrage, he fights by constantly shifting where he shoots from.
playstyle.suited: He doesn't kill with single heavy hits; his output depends on how long he can keep firing. Every fight asks which of his two blinks you will keep for escaping. Whether he fits you comes down to whether you mind constantly looking for the next spot to shoot from without stopping.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei leaps in and shields every teammate in range, so Di Renjie can hold his ground and keep throwing tokens.
Dolia's Celestial Melody resets whichever skill has the longest cooldown left, so Di Renjie can fire Imperial Order again.

counters.reason: Gao Changgong's dagger mark lets him stun Di Renjie and heal himself while cutting him down.
Han Xin is crowd control immune during The Unrivaled Spear, so Imperial Order's stun cannot stop the flurry.

passive.description:
Di Renjie gains 1 stack of Swift Justice for each Basic Attack used. Each stack increases his Attack Speed by 3.5%–7% and his Movement Speed by 5%, for up to 5 stacks.
On every third Basic Attack, Di Renjie attacks with a red or blue token at random.
passive.name: Swift Justice

skill1.description:
Di Renjie tosses a random assortment of 6 red or blue tokens at the target area, dealing 150 (120 + 18% physical attack) physical damage.
Enemies hit by multiple tokens will only take 30% of the initial damage from subsequent tokens.
Red token: Explodes on hit and deals an extra 90 (90 + 18% extra physical attack) magical damage.
Blue token: Deals an extra 45 (45 + 9% extra physical attack) magical damage while slowing the enemy by 15% for 1s.
Six Tokens count as 1 Basic Attack. Damage dealt to the same target diminishes to 30%. Skill casting speed increases with Attack Speed.
skill1.name: Respect the Law

skill2.description:
Di Renjie tosses 8 tokens in a circle around him, gaining brief immunity to damage and crowd control, removing all debuffs from himself, and gaining 25% Movement Speed for 1s.
The damage and effects of these tokens are the same as those of Respect the Law.
skill2.name: Legal Immunity

skill3.description: Di Renjie tosses a secret golden token, dealing 300 (300 + 60% physical attack + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and 300 (300 + 60% physical attack + 120% extra physical attack) magical damage to the first enemy hero hit and stunning them for 1s. This skill also reduces the target's physical defense and magical defense by 50%, while exposing their location for 5s. During this period, teammates moving toward the target enemy gain 10% Movement Speed.
skill3.name: Imperial Order

strategy.earlyGame: In the farm lane, keeping his basic attacks going is what makes Di Renjie strong. Each attack stacks Attack Speed and Movement Speed, and his third attack throws a token, so he can chip his opponent while taking last hits. Respect the Law handles both clearing and poking, but it costs mana, so pick your moments. Legal Immunity is his key escape, so do not spend it on small early trades.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Imperial Order, he gains a way to stop a target and lower their defenses. The target is stunned, loses physical and magical defense, and teammates move faster toward them, which sets up kills with your jungler. A landed Imperial Order also reveals the target, so it can tell your team where an enemy hiding in a bush is. His lack of a movement skill never changes, so step forward only after checking where your team is. Pressing Legal Immunity after an assassin's lockdown lands removes it and lets him reset; pressing it on reflex leaves him with no answer to the next one.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, stand at the very back and keep attacking to hold his Attack Speed and Movement Speed. Landing Imperial Order on an enemy diving toward you stops their advance and lets your team pile onto the lowered defenses. If it misses, keep attacking and scattering tokens from behind your front line. When someone dives you, take the crowd control first, remove it with Legal Immunity, then hit back. He cannot cross walls, so avoid positions where a wall blocks your way out.

combos.title: Lower Their Defenses, Then Push Through
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Imperial Order: stun and lower defenses) → Skill 1 (Respect the Law: scatter tokens) → Basic Attack
combos.description: A landed Imperial Order stuns the target and lowers their physical and magical defense for a while. Teammates also move faster toward that target, so pairing it with your jungler's approach leaves them nowhere to go. Tokens deal less from the second hit on the same target, so finish with uninterrupted basic attacks.

combos.title: Take It, Then Hit Back
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Legal Immunity: immune to damage and crowd control) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (Imperial Order)
combos.description: Pressing Legal Immunity before their real lockdown means taking it with nothing left to remove it. Once you have reset, answer the diver with Imperial Order for the stun and defense reduction.

strengths: Legal Immunity makes him briefly immune to damage and crowd control and removes debuffs
A landed Imperial Order stuns the target and lowers their physical and magical defense
The longer he keeps attacking, the higher his Attack Speed and Movement Speed
Imperial Order reveals its target and speeds up teammates moving toward them
weaknesses: No movement skill; after Legal Immunity he can only walk away
A missed Imperial Order means no stun and no defense reduction
Respect the Law's token colors are random, so he cannot choose when the slow lands
Tokens deal less damage from the second hit on the same target

playstyle.style: Di Renjie is a marksman whose Attack Speed and Movement Speed rise the longer he keeps attacking. His third basic attack and Respect the Law scatter tokens that wear enemies down, and his ultimate, Imperial Order, stuns the enemy hero it hits and lowers their defenses. Legal Immunity makes him briefly immune to damage and crowd control and removes his debuffs.
playstyle.suited: His damage builds by attacking without pause, so he suits players who can keep basic attacks going. Legal Immunity is most effective when pressed after the enemy's crowd control lands, and being able to wait for that moment decides how often he survives. Imperial Order is about the only skill he has to aim, so you can focus on positioning and keeping up your attacks.

synergy.reason: Zilong's Skysplitter shocks enemies, and Dharma's dash launches those at the center, making a wall slam easier to land.
Daji's point-and-click stun is hard to miss, so Dharma can land his punch flurry on a target who cannot move.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi cleanses crowd control and blocks it for his whole team, so Dharma's wall slams never connect.
Di Renjie's Legal Immunity shrugs off crowd control and clears debuffs, so even a wall stun cannot hold him.

passive.description: Every time Dharma uses a skill, he receives a stack of Mantra which grants 32 physical defense and 32 magical defense for 5s, for up to 3 stacks. Using Skill 1 or his Ultimate grants 1 enhanced Basic Attack (and another 1 enhanced Basic Attack if he hits an enemy). Enhanced Basic Attacks deal an extra 28 (28 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage and slow enemies by 15% for 2s.
passive.name: Heart Meridian Mantra

skill1.description: Dharma dashes and punches, dealing 180 (180 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and launching them for 0.5s. He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 9s, for up to 2 charges. If he successfully knocks an enemy back into terrain with his Ultimate, the next use of this skill within 8s becomes a flying kick in the target direction. This kick deals extra physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health.
skill1.name: Formlessness Mantra

skill2.description: Dharma unleashes a flurry of 5 punches every second for 4s for a total of 20 punches. Each punch deals 65 physical damage (50% extra damage to non-hero units), as well as physical damage equal to 0.35% of the target's max Health (increases by 0.25% for every extra 100 physical attack), and restores 85 (85 + 2.5% extra Health) Health. He can control the skill's direction while punching. While using the skill, he will automatically use enhanced Basic Attacks with the same effects as those of his Passive on nearby enemies. The recovery effect is halved for hits on non-hero units. Cancelling the skill will return 50% to 100% of its cooldown, depending on how long he used it for.
skill2.name: Enlightenment Mantra

skill3.description: Dharma throws a powerful punch forward, dealing 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking them back. If enemies are knocked into a wall, they take an extra 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and are stunned for 1s.
skill3.name: Truth Mantra

strategy.earlyGame: In the Clash Lane, your first teammate is the terrain — the walls — and the early game tests how well you use them. Level 1-3 trades lean on Skill 1's dash and the Passive's defense buff, and since Skill 1 holds two charges, the standing rule is one for offense, one banked for the exit. The only green light is the moment your opponent stands near a wall; otherwise, just soak the wave. Your empowered basic also slows on hit, so stack small hit-and-run chips to open an HP gap while you wait for level 4 to unlock the wall-slam game.
strategy.midGame: Once you have the Ultimate, every wall on the map becomes a Dharma kill zone. The recipe is simple: knock the target into a wall, the collision stuns for a second with bonus damage, and within eight seconds Skill 1 converts into a flying kick that adds 15% of their missing HP. Land the full string and most victims don't walk away. Riverbanks and jungle corridors are nothing but walls, so your presence at Tyrant fights is actually stronger than your laning. Skill 2's punch flurry doubles as healing and percent-HP damage, giving you surprising staying power in monster tug-of-wars.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, Dharma's grade depends entirely on forcing fights into tight terrain. Start a fight in the corridor outside Overlord or around a jungle corner and you get the dream play — wall-stunning the enemy carry right in front of your team. In the wide-open river center, though, your knockback is just a shove and half your threat disappears. Claiming the strong bush early to control where the fight happens is your hidden late-game job. Keep three Passive stacks rolling and you hold your own in frontline slugfests too.
strategy.teamfight: You have exactly one objective: put an enemy backliner into a wall. Enter with Skill 1's dash, set your angle, then fire the Ultimate — and take the half-second before casting to confirm a wall actually sits behind them, because that pause is the difference between a kill and a whiff. Once the stun lands, finish with the flying kick and Skill 2's punch flurry. Skill 2 lets you steer mid-channel, but your movement is still restricted, so swinging it out in front of an enemy holding burst is asking to die. Canceling early is always on the table — take the kills that are actually there.

combos.title: Slam Them Into the Wall
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dash, 0.5s launch) → Skill 3 (knockback; a wall impact adds damage and a 1s stun) → Skill 1 (flying kick, 15% of lost Health) → Skill 2 (punch flurry)
combos.description: Confirm there is terrain behind the target before the punch goes out. A wall impact adds a one-second stun, and any Skill 1 used within the next 8s becomes a flying kick worth 15% of the target's lost Health. Skill 1 stocks one charge every 9s up to two, so entering with both keeps the dash-to-kick chain unbroken.

combos.title: Stack Mantra and Stay In
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.5s launch) → enhanced Basic Attack (2s slow) → Skill 2 (20 punches over 4s, healing on every hit)
combos.description: Every skill cast adds a Mantra stack, layering physical and magical defense up to three times. Landing Skill 1 grants a second enhanced basic, so a connected dash means more swings and more slow. Skill 2 chips 0.35% of the target's max Health per punch while healing Dharma, and cancelling it early returns part of its cooldown.

strengths: Huge burst from the wall stun into the flying kick conversion
Strong brawling stats via the Passive's defense buff and Skill 2 healing
Percent-HP damage on Skill 2 chews through high-health targets
Two Skill 1 charges give him flexibility on offense and escape
weaknesses: Loses half his threat in open terrain with no walls
Restricted movement during Skill 2 makes him a target for big skills
A misjudged knockback angle shoves the enemy to safety instead

playstyle.style: A boxer whose knockback punches deal bonus damage when enemies hit walls. Terrain is half his weapon — the same skill is trivial in the open and lethal in a corridor.
playstyle.suited: players who track wall positions on instinct — a knockback into a wall stuns and opens the flying kick, while in open ground neither happens, so check the geometry before you punch.

synergy.reason: Luban No.7 has no escape, so the longer Xiang Yu pins enemies in place, the more of his scattershot lands.
Nakoruru's dive weakens enemy damage just as No Retreat does, hitting the dive target as well as the front line.

counters.reason: Lam brands low-Health enemies and piles on true damage, turning the very window Xiang Yu fights in into Lam's hunting ground.
Di Renjie speeds up with every Basic Attack and shakes off crowd control with Legal Immunity, so Xiang Yu never catches him.

passive.description:
When Xiang Yu's Health drops below 30%, he gains 40% damage reduction for 6s. This effect can only be triggered once every 90s.
After using Righteous Fervor and No Retreat, Xiang Yu gains different enhanced Basic Attacks. Stocks up to 2 charges.
passive.name: Resolute Will

skill1.description:
Xiang Yu charges in the target direction, knocking back enemies and launching them for 0.75s with a slash. The charge and slash each deal 225 (225 + 5% extra Health) physical damage.
His next Basic Attack is enhanced into a vertical chop that deals 445 (250 + 100% physical attack + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and is guaranteed to be a critical hit with a base critical damage of 150%.
skill1.name: Righteous Fervor

skill2.description: Xiang Yu roars, slowing nearby enemies by 15% for 2s, dealing 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) magical damage, and reducing their damage output by 30% for 3.5s. He then gains an enhanced Basic Attack and a 25% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s. The enhanced Basic Attack is a horizontal sweep that restores 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) Health (effect is reduced to 50% against non-hero units; the lower his Health, the higher the recovery, up to a maximum of 50%) and deals 235 (40 + 100% physical attack) physical damage.
skill2.name: No Retreat

skill3.description:
Xiang Yu charges up and unleashes an energy wave with his sword while gaining crowd control immunity and Undying, dealing 900 (900 + 260% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path. Enemies in the inner zone take 50% extra damage and are stunned for 0.75s. The lower Xiang Yu's Health is, the more damage he deals, up to 50% extra damage. 20% of damage dealt is converted into Health.
Undying: Xiang Yu cannot be defeated and his Health will not drop below 1.
skill3.name: Hegemon's Slash

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Xiang Yu starts as the one who steps up and takes the hits. No Retreat lowers the damage output of nearby enemies for a while, so casting it just as the opponent commits keeps him from losing trades. The enhanced basic attack that follows heals him, so he can stay in lane after taking damage. Righteous Fervor is his only movement skill and doubles as his escape, so after using it to attack, keep an eye on the enemy jungler.
strategy.midGame: When your jungler makes a play, use Righteous Fervor's charge to push fleeing enemies back toward your team; the slash at the end launches them, and your team's damage lands while they are in the air. Before Tyrant or Overlord, take the front row and do not fear losing Health. Once his Health drops below a threshold, his passive reduces the damage he takes, so enemies who step in thinking they can finish him can be weakened with No Retreat and turned on. Hegemon's Slash keeps him alive while charging and grows stronger the lower his Health, which makes it the right answer after soaking the enemy's skills.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, take the hits at the front and strike back once you are worn down. Open by charging with Righteous Fervor to shove the enemy front line toward your team, or by knocking away an enemy closing in on your back line. Cast No Retreat as the enemy bunches up to lower everyone's damage output at once. Charge Hegemon's Slash after stepping into the enemy at low Health, and swing it before the threat passes. Some of the enemies it hits are stunned and the damage dealt heals him, so a nearly beaten Xiang Yu striking back becomes the start of your counterattack.

combos.title: Push Them Out and Launch Them
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Righteous Fervor: charge, knock back, launch at the end) → Basic Attack (vertical chop) → Skill 2 (No Retreat: lower damage output) → Basic Attack (horizontal sweep heals)
combos.description: Righteous Fervor pushes enemies as he charges, so aim it to knock them toward your team. Once the slash at the end launches them, follow with the vertical chop, which always crits. Enhanced basic attacks can be stocked twice, so you can also cast No Retreat first and then swing both.

combos.title: Swing Through After Taking Damage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (No Retreat: lower damage output) → Skill 3 (Hegemon's Slash: charge and release) → Basic Attack (horizontal sweep heals)
combos.description: Lowering the enemy's damage output with No Retreat first reduces what he takes while charging Hegemon's Slash. He cannot die while charging it, and it hits harder and heals more the lower his Health, so it is worth the most when he has already taken a beating.

strengths: Low Health triggers his passive damage reduction, and he cannot die during Hegemon's Slash
No Retreat's roar lowers the damage output of nearby enemies
Righteous Fervor's knockback and launch push enemies away from his allies
Hegemon's Slash deals more damage and healing the lower his Health
weaknesses: Righteous Fervor's charge is his only movement skill, so he struggles to chase enemies who keep their distance
Hegemon's Slash charges before it fires, so enemies who read it can avoid it
At full Health his damage and pressure are modest
His passive damage reduction does not come back for a long time once used

playstyle.style: Xiang Yu grows tougher and hits harder as his Health drops. Below a Health threshold his passive cuts the damage he takes, and his ultimate, Hegemon's Slash, keeps him from dying while it is active and deals more damage and healing the lower his Health. Righteous Fervor's knockback and No Retreat's roar, which lowers enemy damage output, blunt the enemy's attack while he stands in front.
playstyle.suited: What decides whether he suits you is staying calm as your Health drops and waiting for the moment to swing Hegemon's Slash. If you like taking the first hits and striking back from there, he holds on in a way few others can. At full Health his damage is modest, so players who want to go hunting from the start may find him lacking.

synergy.reason: Kongming's Spirit Bomb scales with Health already lost, so Sima Yi's burst makes it hit much harder.
Guiguzi pulls enemies into one clump with The Animist and stuns them, so Sima Yi's area skills hit everyone.

counters.reason: Han Xin is crowd control immune through The Unrivaled Spear, so Sima Yi cannot interrupt the flurry.
Zhang Fei soaks Sima Yi's burst behind a huge shield and an invincible roar that ignores crowd control.

passive.description:
Sima Yi gains vision of enemies casting skills within a range of 2,000 and gains 10 Shadow Force (up to 50).
After using the skill, Sima Yi condenses Shadow Force into a scythe, gaining an enhanced Basic Attack and 20 Movement Speed for 5s. Using the enhanced Basic Attack consumes all Shadow Force.
Each scythe strike deals 230 (230 + 46% magical attack) magical damage and true damage equal to Shadow Force. The first attack allows Sima Yi to dash behind the target and deals 300 (300 + 60% magical attack) magical damage (true damage is doubled).
For every 20 Shadow Force consumed, the enhanced Basic Attack's range increases by 3%.
passive.name: Quiet Whispers

skill1.description:
Sima Yi gains crowd control immunity and begins controlling a spirit with high Movement Speed that lasts 2.5s.
The spirit deals 115 (115 + 23% magical attack) magical damage to enemies it passes through. When Sima Yi uses a Basic Attack or when the spirit's duration ends, Sima Yi moves to the spirit's location, dealing 115 (115 + 23% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1s.
skill1.name: Shadow Stings

skill2.description:
Sima Yi releases spiritual energy and suppresses enemies in the surrounding area, dealing 275 (275 + 55% magical attack) magical damage and silencing them for 0.75s. Inside the suppression zone, Sima Yi gains 10% increased recovery.
Passive: When Sima Yi takes magical damage, 25% is converted into Health recovery for 3s (halved for physical damage).
skill2.name: Barren Lands

skill3.description:
Sima Yi steps back and charges up briefly, then dashes to the target location, where he deals 530 (530 + 110% magical attack) magical damage (damage halved to enemies along his path).
If this skill is interrupted, 90% cooldown is returned.
skill3.name: Death Descends

strategy.earlyGame: In the jungle, Sima Yi gains Shadow Force and vision whenever an enemy hero nearby uses a skill. Watching where enemies in nearby lanes use their skills while clearing helps him find openings for ganks. With Shadow Force stored, the first enhanced strike dashes behind the target, so even opponents who retreat behind their minions are within reach. Barren Lands' passive turns part of the magical damage he takes into Health, so he can hold up in trades against mages.
strategy.midGame: As he spends more time ganking and ambushing, send the spirit ahead with Shadow Stings to scout. While controlling it he is immune to crowd control, so he can check the flank route as he approaches. Pressing a basic attack or letting the spirit expire moves him to it, so his approach is faster than it looks. Chip with the enhanced strike from behind, then shut down the target's movement and counterattack skills with Barren Lands' silence before finishing them. Enemies giving away their position by readying a skill in a bush also helps his ambushes. Leave the opening of teamfights to his team and move once enemies have used skills and his Shadow Force has built up.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, he goes in second. Shadow Force builds as enemies use skills, so entering from the side right after absorbing their engage gives him more damage and more safety than diving first. Go for an isolated mage or marksman; silencing them with Barren Lands as the enhanced strike carries him behind them leaves them unable to press their escape. Shadow Stings also works as a way to move to the spirit, so keep one use as a way out instead of spending it all on offense.

combos.title: Get Behind Them With the Enhanced Attack
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Shadow Stings: control the spirit) → Basic Attack (move to the spirit and strike from behind) → Skill 2 (Barren Lands: silence)
combos.description: Pressing a basic attack during Shadow Stings moves Sima Yi to the spirit, and that strike dashes behind the target. The true damage grows with stored Shadow Force and is even larger on the first strike from behind. It lands hardest right after the enemy has used a skill, so wait for them to move first.

combos.title: Charge In, Then Silence
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Death Descends: step back, charge, dash) → Skill 2 (Barren Lands: silence) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Death Descends deals reduced damage to enemies along the path, so aim it to land directly on your target. Once there, silence them with Barren Lands to stop their counterattack and hit with the scythe that his skills summoned again. Most of the cooldown returns if the charge is interrupted, so he can show the windup to bait out escape skills.

combos.title: Use the Spirit as an Escape
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Shadow Stings: send the spirit along your escape route) → Skill 2 (Barren Lands: silence) → Basic Attack (move to the spirit)
combos.description: The spirit is fast, and Sima Yi himself is immune to crowd control while controlling it. Silence the chaser with Barren Lands, then press a basic attack to move straight to the spirit. The same move happens when the spirit's time runs out, so even if you forget, he is not left behind.

strengths: He gains vision of enemies casting skills nearby and knows where they are first
The first enhanced strike dashes behind the target and deals true damage
Barren Lands' silence stops the target's escape or counterattack skills
Death Descends returns most of its cooldown if interrupted
weaknesses: Barren Lands' passive healing is halved against physical damage
His damage depends on Shadow Force, which grows slowly if enemies hold their skills
After spending his enhanced attack, his damage dips until Shadow Force builds again
He is fragile, and failing to finish a target invites a counterattack

playstyle.style: Sima Yi is a jungler who gains vision of enemy heroes casting skills nearby and turns the Shadow Force he collects into a scythe. Using a skill enhances his next basic attack; the first strike dashes behind the target and adds true damage based on his Shadow Force. Barren Lands silences nearby enemies, and its passive converts part of the magical damage he takes into Health.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who would rather win by reading what the enemy did than by reflexes. You choose where to strike based on where enemies used their skills and how much Shadow Force has built up. He is fragile, so picking targets he can finish ties directly to how often he survives.

synergy.reason: Wang Zhaojun's Frigid Prison freezes enemies in place, so they cannot dodge the Misty Mountain Wang Wei conjures at the target location.
Guiguzi's The Animist pulls enemies to him and stuns them, so Wang Wei's Misty Mountain hits the whole group at once.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect grants teammates crowd control immunity, so Wang Wei's Endless River cannot pull them into the mountain.
Sima Yi heals from magical damage taken, and every Wang Wei skill is magical, so the poke struggles to finish him.

passive.description: Mist Sage gains 1 mark every 5–4s. At 5 marks, he dodges the next instance of damage. Each dodge consumes marks based on damage taken, up to 250 (250 + 50% extra magical attack) damage.
passive.name: Shifting Mists

skill1.description:
Mist Sage conjures a Misty Mountain at the target location, dealing 400 (400 + 80% magical attack) magical damage and slowing enemies by 20% for 0.75s, then dealing 45 (45 + 9% magical attack) magical damage once every 0.4s for 1.5s. The mountain then explodes, dealing 180 (180 + 36% magical attack) magical damage.
While Mist Sage is within the area, he enters the Misty Mountain state, recovering passive marks more quickly.
skill1.name: Misty Mountain

skill2.description:
Mist Sage releases a river that flows in the target direction, dealing 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and knocking back enemies for 0.75s.
Up to 2 streams will split off from the river to chase enemies, dealing 50% damage and slowing them by 15% for 0.5s.
If the river runs into the mountain conjured by Skill 1, it will circle the mountain once, pulling nearby enemies into the mountain before detonating it and breaking away at increased speed.
skill2.name: Endless River

skill3.description:
Mist Sage unleashes a mist hairpin and controls it for 9s, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path (1/3 damage for repeat hits).
When the hairpin stops, he emerges at its location, dealing 400 (400 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. He then locks on to a random enemy in range and deals 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage once every 1/3s for 3s. Repeated hits deal less damage, down to 1/3 of the initial damage. He enters the Misty Mountain state from when he lands until the skill ends.
While controlling the hairpin:
Skill 1 is replaced with Mist Rider: Mist Sage calls upon the speed of the mountain mists, granting the pin a brief Movement Speed boost.
Skill 2 is replaced with Churning Mists: Mist Sage causes the mountain mists to swirl, slowing the hairpin so he can change direction more quickly.
skill3.name: One With All

strategy.earlyGame: Misty Mountain is cheap, and its damage and slow on landing are followed by continued damage and a final detonation. In mid lane, placing it where the enemy and the minions overlap clears the wave and pokes the opponent in one cast. His passive marks build over time and let him dodge the next instance of damage once complete. Standing inside the mountain's area makes the marks build faster, so check whether a dodge is ready before stepping up.
strategy.midGame: Once he leaves lane, his main tool is the Misty Mountain and Endless River combination. Place the mountain first and hit it with the river before it detonates; the river circles the mountain, pulls enemies to the center and sets it off. Endless River has a longer cooldown than Misty Mountain, so he cannot link them every time; when the river is not available, use the mountain just to poke. When the river hits an enemy, streams split off to chase nearby enemies and slow them. One With All's attacks after he emerges lock onto a random enemy in range, so if only frontliners are nearby, that is where they go. Carry the mist close to their back line before emerging.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfights start with Misty Mountain the moment the enemy bunches up. Run Endless River through it to pull them in and stack everything up to the detonation. One With All's hairpin damages enemies in its path, but repeat hits on the same enemy deal less, so steer it over different enemies where you can. While he controls the hairpin, Skills 1 and 2 are replaced by other skills, so decide in advance whether to cast the mountain and river before entering the mist or after emerging. After emerging he enters the Misty Mountain state and builds marks faster.

combos.title: Run the River Into the Mountain
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Misty Mountain: place the mountain) → Skill 2 (Endless River: send the river into it)
combos.description: Place the mountain at the enemy's feet and hit it with the river while the slow is still on them. Even if the river is late, the mountain detonates on its own after damaging for a while.

combos.title: Sweep Through the Mist, Then Emerge
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (One With All: control the hairpin) → Skill 1 (Mist Rider: speed up) → Skill 2 (Churning Mists: turn) → Skill 3 (emerge)
combos.description: Speed into the enemy line with Mist Rider, slow down and turn back with Churning Mists, and steer so it passes over different enemies. Finally emerge near their back line and land the arrival damage.

combos.title: Push Them Back, Then Slow Them
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Endless River: knock back) → Skill 1 (Misty Mountain: slow)
combos.description: Knock back an enemy closing in with Endless River, then place the mountain where they land to slow them. If you reverse the order and the river touches the mountain, it pulls enemies to the center instead. When you want distance, fire the river first.

strengths: Misty Mountain is cheap, keeps damaging and slowing where it lands, then detonates
Running Endless River into the mountain pulls enemies to its center before it detonates
One With All lets him control the mist and emerge far away to attack
Once his marks have built up, he dodges the next instance of damage
weaknesses: No stuns or launches; his only ways to hinder enemies are slows and Endless River's knockback and pull
One With All's attacks after he emerges lock onto a random enemy in range, so he cannot choose the target
One With All is his only movement skill, and Endless River's knockback is his only way to push away someone closing in
Marks build over time, so after a dodge there is a gap before he can dodge again

playstyle.style: Wang Wei is an area-damage mage who runs Endless River through the mountain he places with Misty Mountain, pulling enemies to its center before it detonates. His ultimate, One With All, lets him control a mist hairpin across the map, damaging enemies in its path before he emerges somewhere else. His passive also lets him dodge one instance of damage once enough marks have built up.
playstyle.suited: What decides how he plays is whether you can place the mountain and get the river into it before it detonates. If you can keep that order, his area combo comes together quickly. Skills 1 and 2 change roles while he controls the hairpin, so the mist itself also takes practice.

synergy.reason: Da Qiao's whirlpool warps the team onto the hero Fuzi has pinned, turning his solo dive into a fight.
Li Bai needs a target that stays put to hold Sword Energy, and Fuzi's bind keeps one there.

counters.reason: Charlotte's final enhanced strike scales with Fuzi's missing Health, so the longer he holds the harder it hits.
Guan Yu's Charge Stance attack knocks Fuzi back, denying the melee range Fuzi needs.

passive.description: Whenever Fuzi lands a Basic Attack, he gains 1 stack of Admonition for 5s, up to 5 stacks. At full stacks, he becomes enhanced for 5s. While enhanced, he gains 60 Movement Speed and 30% Attack Speed, while each Basic Attack deals an extra 65 (65 + 23% extra physical attack) true damage and reduces his Skill 1 and Skill 2's Cooldown by 1s.
passive.name: Ancient Wisdom

skill1.description: Fuzi swings his ferule in the target direction, pulling enemies within range toward him and dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage while slowing them by 25% for 1.5−2.5s (duration scales with skill level).
skill1.name: Corporal Punishment

skill2.description:
Fuzi enhances himself for 2s, during which he gains 25% Movement Speed and 45% damage reduction.
While enhanced, he reflects 50% of the damage taken after being hit by the first Basic Attack and slows his attackers by 15% for 2s. This reflected damage carries his Basic Attack's on-hit effects.
Passive: His Basic Attack has a 25% chance of being followed up with another Basic Attack that inflicts 50% damage and on-hit effects.
skill2.name: Intuition

skill3.description: Fuzi charges in the target direction, dealing 500 (500 + 185% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hero hit and binding them to his lamppost. While bound, the enemy hero will be confined for 5s within the area where his Ultimate hit, and deal 20% less damage.
skill3.name: Sage's Might

strategy.earlyGame: Take Skill 2 first in the clash lane — the damage reduction and bonus-attack procs let you clear the opening wave and trade at the same time. Fuzi's lifeline is his Passive: whether you have five stacks banked from hitting minions before you commit changes the fight entirely. The empowered state adds true damage and shaves the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2, so at even HP you win most slugfests on math alone. Don't chase before level 4, and any time the enemy jungler disappears from the map, assume the river brush and back off.
strategy.midGame: At the 4-minute Tyrant fight, your job is to open by binding the enemy fighter or jungler with your Ultimate. Five seconds of restricted movement plus 20% reduced damage output means they fight the whole skirmish at a disadvantage. In lane, lean on your 1v1 strength to push the side, and drag anyone who collapses on you into melee with Skill 1. Skill 2 reflects 50% of the first basic attack you take while it's active — read the tell on an enemy's empowered attack and pop it in response, and you win the trade on that alone.
strategy.lateGame: True to his late-game label, Fuzi peaks once Doomsday and Blood Rage come online after 15 minutes. Five-stack true damage all but ignores armor, so almost nobody wins a straight brawl against you. But games are decided at Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, not in a side lane. Leave the 1v1 thirty seconds before the objective spawns, regroup with your team, and claim the position that lets you land your Ultimate as the fight's opening move.
strategy.teamfight: The dream scenario: bind the enemy carry right before the brawl starts and turn it into a 5v4. The dash latches onto the first hero it touches, so when their frontline is walling you out, look for a flank angle. Once the bind lands, activate Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and never stop swinging — as long as your basics connect, the stacks and cooldown refunds keep cycling, and Fuzi only gets stronger the longer the fight runs. Standing around without a target is the one thing that kills you.

combos.title: Opening Bind
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (dash, 5s movement confinement) → Skill 2 (damage reduction) → Basic Attacks → Skill 1 (pull back)
combos.description: The dash only catches the first enemy hero it touches, so find an angle past their frontline instead of driving through it. A bound target deals 20% less damage. Hold the 45% reduction (Lvl 1), keep swinging, and drag them back with Skill 1 when they drift to the edge of the zone.

combos.title: Stack Up Before You Commit
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×5 (5 Admonition stacks → enhanced) → Skill 1 (pull + slow) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: Each landed Basic Attack adds a stack, and five of them open a 5-second enhanced window. While enhanced, every hit adds true damage and shaves 1s off Skill 1 and Skill 2. Five seconds is short, so stack on minions and close the distance immediately after.

combos.title: Reflect Counter
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (2s enhance, damage reduction) → Skill 1 (pull + slow) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: The enhanced state runs for only 2s, so press it just as the enemy winds up a Basic Attack. That first hit is reduced, 50% of it bounces back, and the attacker is slowed by 15% for 2s (Lvl 1). Pull them in with Skill 1 and take the trade.

strengths: Five-stack true damage makes him one of the game's best 1v1 brawlers
Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and reflect turn enemy aggression against them
The Ultimate's 5-second bind and 20% damage cut shuts down the enemy ace
A late-game power curve that keeps climbing as items complete
weaknesses: Needs uninterrupted basic attacks to function — kiting shuts him down hard
His only real gap-closer is the Ultimate; missing it leaves a long window
Skill 1's pull radius is small and whiffs against high-mobility targets
Without stacks, both his damage and durability are merely average

playstyle.style: A brawler who powers up through repeated basic attacks, pulls enemies in with his ruler, and reflects the first attack that hits his stance. He is built to win while being hit.
playstyle.suited: patient brawlers happy to win while taking hits. Stacking five basic attacks takes discipline; the payoff is turning the enemy's opening blow back on them.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's speed buff builds Guan Yu's charge faster, so he reaches the fight already in Charge Stance.
Yaria's shield scales with the target's extra Health, so Guan Yu keeps charging forward instead of pulling back.

counters.reason: Fuzi's slow drags Guan Yu's Movement Speed down, which strips him of Charge Stance.
Daji's stun freezes Guan Yu in place, and her burst lands on him while he cannot move.

passive.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu gains 2% Movement Speed for every 200 units of distance he moves, entering Charge Stance upon moving 2,000 units. When Movement Speed drops below 375, exits Charge Stance, and the accumulated distance is reset after 0.7s.
When standing stationary near brush, recovers 30 Health and Energy every 0.5s.
Charge Stance: Enhances next Basic Attack, charging forward to deal an extra 500 (500 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and knocking them back. Gains 20% Movement Speed when moving toward enemy heroes.
When in Normal Stance, he can use Basic Attacks while moving.
passive.name: Rider of Triumph

skill1.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu swings his blade, dealing 500 (500 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
Charge Stance: He charges forward, dealing 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and knocking them back. He then attacks again, dealing 500 (500 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Heroic Charge

skill2.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu removes all crowd control effects from himself and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
Charge Stance: He removes all crowd control effects from himself and leaps forward, dealing 650 (650 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies near his landing point and knocking them back. He also gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
skill2.name: Soaring Green Dragon

skill3.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu enhances himself for 10s. While enhanced, the distance required to enter Charge Stance is reduced by 75%.
Charge Stance: Guan Yu summons heavy cavalry on either side of himself that charge forward with him, dealing 620 (620 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their path and knocking them back. He then enhances himself for 10s. While enhanced, the distance required to enter Charge Stance is reduced by 75%.
skill3.name: Razor Cavalry

strategy.earlyGame: Guan Yu starts in the clash lane, but after the first two waves your top priority is simple: never stop moving. His Passive enters the charge state after 2000 units of travel, so every second spent standing in a lane staring at your opponent is a second spent being weak. Loop through the river and your own jungle to build a runway, then knock enemies flying with the charged basic attack, disengage, and repeat. Until level 4, resist every urge to chase — hit, knock them back, and leave. That alone wins you lane priority.
strategy.midGame: The game becomes Guan Yu's around the 4-minute Tyrant. Objective standoffs hand you runways for free, and a single blindside knockback into their backline can decide the fight before it starts. Cast Skill 3 in Normal Stance and you are enhanced for 10s, with the distance required to enter Charge Stance reduced by 75% — 2,000 units becomes 500, so re-engages come around far faster. When ganking, angle your approach so enemies get knocked toward your tower or your teammates — punting them to safety in their own territory is the classic first mistake every new Guan Yu makes.
strategy.lateGame: With two or three defense items like Overlord's Platemail and Blazing Cape done by 15 minutes, Charge Stance Skill 1 becomes your main tool. It charges forward, knocking enemies back for 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage, and the slash at the end of the charge adds 500 (500 + 160% extra physical attack) on top. Your enhanced basic attack is flat, not percentage — an extra 500 (1,000 at level 15) plus 125% extra physical attack — so items are what scale it. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, your job is to crash sideways into the brush they're holding, wedge yourself between the boss pit and their team, and split their formation. You lack solo kill power, so leave knocked-back targets to your teammates and immediately start building the next runway. While an enemy with strong slows is alive, take the long way around and come from behind — never the front.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight prep starts 30 seconds early: run the perimeter and keep the charge state alive. The ideal entry clips their marksman and mage in a single line, and once you've run someone over, do not stop — Skill 2 cleanses crowd control and re-accelerates you for a second and third pass. Planting your feet in the middle of the scrum is the worst thing you can do. Keep making passes back and forth through their team, and the enemy never reforms their line while your own backline shoots for free.

combos.title: Ride Through With the Cavalry
combos.sequence: Build 2,000 distance (Charge Stance) → Skill 3 (charge alongside heavy cavalry, knockback) → run it back (required distance cut by 75%) → Empowered Basic Attack (charge + knockback)
combos.description: Only the Charge Stance version summons cavalry on either side and knocks back everything in the path. Press it in Normal Stance and no dash comes out — you just get the 10s buff. That buff cuts the distance needed to enter Charge Stance by 75%, so a short run-up is enough to set up another empowered Basic Attack.

combos.title: Cleanse and Rebuild the Run-Up
combos.sequence: Skill 2, Normal Stance (removes all crowd control, +30% Movement Speed for 2s) → run to rebuild distance → Empowered Basic Attack (charge + knockback)
combos.description: Charge Stance breaks the instant Movement Speed drops under 375, and the stored distance resets 0.7s later. When you get caught, leave instead of trading — Skill 2 strips every crowd control effect off him even in Normal Stance. At Lvl 1 it adds 2s of 30% Movement Speed, which doubles as the opening of your next run-up.

combos.title: Heal in the Brush, Then Charge
combos.sequence: Stand still near brush (30 Health and Energy every 0.5s) → run 2,000 distance → Empowered Basic Attack (charge + knockback)
combos.description: Even at Lvl 1 that regen returns 30 Health and Energy every half second, so top up at the edge of a brush instead of walking home. Standing still puts Movement Speed under 375, which clears Charge Stance and the stored distance alike. Heal first, then start the run and angle the charge so they land on your side of the lane.

strengths: Charge Stance Skill 1 lands twice — the charge itself and the slash at the end — so even tanky lines break
Skill 2 self-cleanses CC, making him extremely hard to pin down
Elite formation-breaking; he creates teamfight openings single-handedly
Gets stronger just by running, so his farm dependency is low
weaknesses: Standing still drops the charge state, leaving him weak in tight scrums
Stacked slows or chained CC stop his feet and get him focused down
Demands runway knowledge and heavy mechanics — a genuinely hard hero
Lacks solo kill power; his knockbacks need teammates to convert

playstyle.style: A cavalry hero whose power is his run-up: 2,000 units of movement puts him in charge state, where his skills split formations with knockbacks. A stationary Guan Yu is barely a hero at all.
playstyle.suited: anyone happy never to stand still. Keep the run-up alive and choose the angle that splits the enemy formation; stop moving and the hero stops working.

synergy.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect clears and blocks crowd control, so Diaochan can dive without being stopped.
Bai Qi's pull and taunt hold enemies still, letting Diaochan stack her floral marks to detonation.

counters.reason: Liang's suppression locks Diaochan in place, so even her blink cannot break her out of it.
Mulan's Balance stacks detonate into a silence, cutting off Diaochan's skills and her blink escape.

passive.description: Every time one of Diaochan's skills deals damage, it places a floral mark on the target for 8s. At the maximum of 4 stacks, the marks will be activated, restoring 140 (140 + 1.5% extra Health) Health to her while dealing 140 (140 + 40% magical attack) true damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 25%-50% for 1s.
passive.name: Explosion of Fragrance

skill1.description: Diaochan sends out a lotus in the target direction, dealing 260 (260 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and again on its way back.
skill1.name: Returning Lotus

skill2.description: Diaochan blinks to the target location and launches 3 lotus petals at nearby enemies. Each petal deals 140 (140 + 28% magical attack) magical damage and reduces Skill 2's Cooldown for up to 3s based on the locations of her and the target hit.
skill2.name: Petals in the Wind

skill3.description:
Diaochan conjures a lotus circle that deals 210 (210 + 50% magical attack) magical damage upon its appearance and disappearance. When she is in the circle, the cooldowns of her Skill 1 and 2 are further reduced.
Tapping the skill again will close the lotus circle.
skill3.name: Flowery Potential

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Diaochan holds back until she has her ultimate. Returning Lotus travels out and back, so hitting both passes adds two marks in one cast. It handles both wave clearing and poking, while Petals in the Wind is her only emergency escape, so don't spend it on offense in case of ganks. Mana is a concern, so completing Holy Grail early to avoid running dry is her first goal.
strategy.midGame: As her cooldown reduction items come together, her strength in close-range fights rises. When roaming away from lane, Petals in the Wind closes distance quickly. In skirmishes before Tyrant, lay Flowery Potential's circle first, then cycle Returning Lotus and Petals in the Wind to push back with the true damage and healing from mark bursts. Diving in while the enemy still has stuns or silences ready gets her stopped and taken down, so count who has used their crowd control first. Mark bursts hit armored frontliners just as hard, so her damage holds up as games go long.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, she goes into the middle the moment the enemy's crowd control is used. With her circle down, a grouped enemy is her source of damage and healing; the more enemies her skills hit, the more mark bursts chain, until her healing outpaces the damage she takes. Ideally she catches two or three enemies in the circle and keeps moving, changing direction with Petals in the Wind's blinks. A single stun can break her, so before the fight, check which enemies have crowd control and what they still have left. When a high-burst enemy is ahead, save your spell and let a teammate be the first to dive.

combos.title: Keep Cycling Inside the Circle
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Flowery Potential: open the circle) → Skill 2 (Petals in the Wind: blink and launch petals) → Skill 1 (Returning Lotus: out and back) → Skill 2 (Petals in the Wind)
combos.description: Returning Lotus and Petals in the Wind only cycle faster while she stays inside the circle. So place the circle where she can stay, not at the enemy's feet. Petals in the Wind's cooldown shrinks depending on how the petals hit, so keep close and land them.

combos.title: Stack Four Marks and Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Returning Lotus: hit going and returning) → Skill 2 (Petals in the Wind: land the petals) → marks burst
combos.description: Each skill hit adds one mark, and four make them burst. The lotus hits both on the way out and on the way back, so landing both passes advances the marks quickly.

combos.title: Blink Out
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Petals in the Wind: blink toward allies or a wall) → Skill 1 (Returning Lotus: lotus into the chaser's path)
combos.description: Petals in the Wind is her only movement skill, so right after spending it on offense is when she is most vulnerable. Even after blinking away, the petals fly at nearby enemies, and hits shorten the cooldown. The lotus comes back to her, so firing it while retreating can still catch chasers on the return.

strengths: Mark bursts repeat true damage and healing, so she holds on in brawls
Petals in the Wind's cooldown shrinks depending on how its petals hit, so her movement rarely stops
Inside Flowery Potential's circle her skills return faster, wearing down several enemies at once
Mark bursts deal true damage, so they get through enemies with defensive items
weaknesses: A silence or stun stops her sequence and she collapses quickly
She is fragile and weak to burst damage before her marks burst
She fights close to enemies, so she cannot reach opponents who keep poking from range
Petals in the Wind is her only movement skill, so she is vulnerable right after using it to attack

playstyle.style: Diaochan is a mage who fights close to enemies, repeatedly blinking with Petals in the Wind. Her skill damage stacks floral marks, and at four marks they burst, dealing true damage to nearby enemies and restoring her Health. Inside the circle from her ultimate, Flowery Potential, the cooldowns of her Skills 1 and 2 shorten, so she stacks marks faster.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who want to break the idea that mages stand at the back and instead keep moving near enemies. What decides how she plays is learning the distance at which she can stack four marks and survive on the burst's healing. Silences and stuns break her sequence, so she also needs the caution to count which crowd control has been used before going in.

synergy.reason: Zhuangzi's slow keeps enemies from escaping, so Angela's Chaos Cinder vortex keeps ticking on them.
Zhang Fei's shield covers Angela as she steps up, letting her keep firing instead of retreating.

counters.reason: Han Xin leaps in and launches Angela before she can even start firing, pinning her down.
Daji stuns Angela, shreds her Magical Defense while she is held, and wins the trade outright.

passive.description:
Every time Angela deals damage with one of her active skills, she places 1 stack of Burning on the target while gaining 1 stack of increased Movement Speed herself. Both max out at 10 stacks and last for 3s.
Stacks on enemies cause the target to take an extra 10 (10 + 2% magical attack) magical damage from her active skills, while stacks on Angela increase her Movement Speed by 2%.
passive.name: Flame Incantation

skill1.description:
Angela unleashes 5 fireballs in the target direction. When a fireball hits an enemy hero, it disappears and deals 280 (280 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. Fireballs deal an equal amount of damage to non-hero units in their path.
When multiple fireballs hit the same target, subsequent fireballs only deal 30% damage.
skill1.name: Scorching Barrage

skill2.description:
Angela unleashes a fireball in the target direction, which forms a flame vortex upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, stunning the first enemy hit for 1s.
The vortex deals 125 (125 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s and slows them by 30% for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Chaos Cinder

skill3.description:
Angela channels a blazing beam in the target direction, dealing up to 12 strikes of 150 (150 + 21% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its way. Angela can adjust the direction of the beam while channeling.
While channeling the beam, Angela gains a shield that grants crowd control immunity and negates 850 (850 + 88% magical attack) damage.
Use the skill again after 0.5s to cancel the channeling.
skill3.name: Blazing Brilliance

strategy.earlyGame: Where you fire Scorching Barrage shapes the early lane. Each fireball vanishes when it hits an enemy hero, but minions in its path take the same damage, so one cast can work on the wave and the opponent together. Extra fireballs on the same hero deal reduced damage, so firing through the minion line wastes less than aiming at the opponent alone. Every skill that lands adds Burning and Movement Speed stacks, so the more often you hit, the harder your poke becomes. Aim Chaos Cinder for when the opponent stops to clear minions.
strategy.midGame: Once the wave is pushed, you will spend more time showing up where your jungler is about to fight. Chaos Cinder stuns the first enemy it hits, so landing it with allies close enough to strike sets up a kill. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, firing Chaos Cinder into the path enemies will take works too: the vortex still forms at max range, chipping at nearby enemies and slowing them. Blazing Brilliance can be steered while it fires, and crowd control cannot stop it while the shield holds. When the shield breaks, though, the immunity goes with it, so choose where to start the beam based on whether the enemy divers are visible. Without a blink, Angela stays alive by reaching the enemy from behind her own frontline.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Chaos Cinder is worth more saved for whoever dives you than spent on the frontline at the start. Once it is gone, she has nothing left to stop someone who reaches her. When the stun lands, layer Scorching Barrage and Blazing Brilliance on the target while the Burning stacks build. The shield means crowd control will not stop the beam, so you can start it even with enemies nearby. When the target drops, recast to end the beam and move to where you can reach the next one.

combos.title: Stun, Then Chase With the Beam
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Chaos Cinder: stuns the first enemy hit) → Skill 3 (Blazing Brilliance: steer while firing) → Skill 1 (Scorching Barrage: finisher)
combos.description: Start Blazing Brilliance while Chaos Cinder holds them, and you can turn the beam to follow once they start moving. Extra fireballs on the same hero deal reduced damage, so treat Scorching Barrage as the last push.

combos.title: Meet the Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Blazing Brilliance: shield and crowd control immunity) → Skill 2 (Chaos Cinder: hold them in place) → Skill 1 (Scorching Barrage)
combos.description: Start the beam the moment someone reaches you. If the kill is not there, recast to end the beam, stop them with Chaos Cinder, then make distance.

combos.title: Block the Path With the Vortex
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Chaos Cinder: fired into the enemy's path in advance) → Skill 1 (Scorching Barrage: follow-up)
combos.description: Chaos Cinder turns into a vortex at max range even if it hits nothing. Place it where enemies have to walk and the slow drags them down without a direct hit, which gives Scorching Barrage an easy target.

strengths: Scorching Barrage also deals the same damage to minions in its path, so the wave and the opponent go down together
While Blazing Brilliance's shield holds, crowd control cannot stop the beam
Each skill that lands adds Burning to the target and Movement Speed to Angela
Chaos Cinder leaves a vortex even on a miss, slowing enemies who come near it
weaknesses: Every skill is a skillshot, so targets that keep strafing are hard to hit
No blink; once Chaos Cinder is used, she has little defense against divers
Fireballs after the first deal reduced damage to the same hero
When the shield breaks, the crowd control immunity goes with it and the beam can be stopped

playstyle.style: Angela is a mage who burns the minion wave and her lane opponent with the same volley of fireballs, stacking Burning with every skill that lands. Her damage grows heavier the longer she keeps hitting. Her ultimate, Blazing Brilliance, can be steered while it fires, so she can chase a fleeing target with the beam.
playstyle.suited: Every skill is aimed in a direction, so she rewards players who lead a moving target rather than react to it. With no blink, how long she survives depends on deciding where to fire from before the fight starts. There are no tricky mechanics in her kit; what you learn is where to stand and which order to cast in.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi drags enemies into one clump, so a single Crescent Slice marks them all and New Moon keeps resetting.
Zhuangzi's ultimate hands out crowd control immunity and a shield, so Luna can dive in without being stopped.

counters.reason: Liang's ultimate simply suppresses Luna, so she cannot dash, mark, or fight back at all.
Heino heals more the more enemy heroes stand near him, so Luna's own melee pressure feeds his sustain.

passive.description:
Luna's Basic Attack has two forms. When the target is out of melee range, it automatically switches to the ranged form.
While in melee form, the 1st of every 3 of her Basic Attacks causes her to charge toward the enemy.
Every 3rd Basic Attack deals an extra 150 (150 + 35% magical attack) magical damage and marks the enemy for 5s. Structures cannot be marked.
For every 1 Magical Attack, she gains 0.03% Attack Speed.
passive.name: Moonlight Dance

skill1.description: Luna unleashes a moon wave, dealing 400 (400 +65% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and marking them.
skill1.name: Crescent Slice

skill2.description:
Luna pulls in nearby enemies, dealing 160 (160 + 32% magical attack) magical damage. The attack stuns them for 0.5s and slows them by 25% for 2s. Luna also gains a shield that negates 450 (450 + 80% magical attack) damage for 2s.
Pulled enemies will also be marked.
skill2.name: Searing Stab

skill3.description:
Luna dashes to the target location, dealing 350 (350 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits a marked enemy, this skill's cooldown is reset and the mark is consumed.
skill3.name: New Moon

strategy.earlyGame: Luna is a jungler first. Open on both buffs and the camps between them and race to level 4, drilling the Skill 1 → Ultimate → third basic attack order into muscle memory as you clear. Everything Luna does rests on one rule: hitting a marked enemy with the Ultimate resets its cooldown. On your first ganks after level 4, resist the urge to show off a long chain — landing Skill 2's pull and stun to hold the target for your laner succeeds far more often than a greedy solo play.
strategy.midGame: From around 8 minutes, with one or two magic attack items done, Luna headlines every skirmish. The base pattern at Tyrant and mid: tag from range with Skill 1, enter with the Ultimate, refresh the mark with your third basic and Skill 2, and keep weaving in and out. Marks stick to minions too, so learn to chain Ultimates through waves and camps as transportation — it puts your chases and escapes in a different dimension. As long as you don't die, nobody out-farms you.
strategy.lateGame: Teamfights after 15 minutes are won before you enter. A Luna walking in the front door is just a squishy melee, so always start from a flank or the rear with a mark already on a perimeter enemy. Touch once and leave before their stuns and silences turn your way, then start the real dance once their CC is down. Skill 2's shield and 0.5-second stun erase hundreds of damage in a scrum — when you feel surrounded, restart from the pull rather than the attack and your survival rate climbs.
strategy.teamfight: A dropped chain is death, full stop. Throughout the fight, keep the next marked Ultimate target decided two steps ahead, and the instant one dies, switch to another enemy or a minion. While a mark lives, you enter and exit the fight at will — from the enemy's seat, an uncatchable nightmare. But one missed reset deletes your escape plan, so build the habit of confirming your exit mark one step before every overextension. Luna returns exactly what you put into her, and she demands commitment.

combos.title: Keep Skill 3 Rolling
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (apply the mark) → Skill 3 (dash; hitting a marked enemy resets its cooldown) → 3rd Basic Attack (re-apply the mark) → Skill 3
combos.description: Landing Skill 3 on a marked enemy resets its cooldown. Both Skill 1 and every 3rd Basic Attack apply that mark, so after each dash you bank three hits to set up the next reset. In melee form the 1st of every 3 attacks charges her at the enemy, which closes a small gap on its own.

combos.title: Pull First, Then Restart
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pull + 0.5s stun + 450 shield + mark) → Skill 3 (hitting the mark resets the cooldown) → 3rd Basic Attack → Skill 3
combos.description: When they surround her, press Skill 2 before you press attack. Everything it pulls gets marked, and the 0.5s stun plus a 450 shield (Lvl 1) buys the beat she needs. They also lose 25% Movement Speed for 2s, which is enough to put Skill 3 back into that mark and restart the loop.

combos.title: Hop Through Minions
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (mark a minion) → Skill 3 (dash to it; the cooldown resets) → Skill 3 again to the next marked target
combos.description: Towers and crystals cannot be marked, but minions and jungle camps can. Use them as waypoints and Skill 3 chains far past its own range. Miss the marked target and no reset comes, which strands her exactly where she stopped.

strengths: Endless Ultimate resets grant mobility no one else in the game matches
Skill 2's pull, stun, and shield keep her alive in the center of brawls
Free entry and exit lets her bait enemy CC before the real engage
At full mastery, she can win a teamfight single-handedly
weaknesses: The instant the reset chain breaks, her escape disappears with it
A stun or silence mid-loop reduces her to a squishy melee
One of the hardest heroes in the game — low mastery means zero output
Tunnel vision mid-combo makes her slow to react to counter-ganks

playstyle.style: The moonlight duelist with a theoretically infinite combo: her ultimate resets whenever it hits a marked enemy. Maintain the mark-dash-mark loop and she never stops; drop it once and she's mortal again.
playstyle.suited: combo drillers. Mark, dash, reset, repeat — break the chain once and you are just squishy melee again, so hundreds of practice reps are the entry fee.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's shields and slows let Ziya hold a forward spot and keep firing his skills.
Erin finishes off the lowest-Health enemies, so Ziya's Sanctification turns his chip damage into EXP orbs.

counters.reason: Gao Changgong picks his moment from stealth, and the mark's stun leaves Ziya no way out.
Gan & Mo strip Ziya's Magical Defense with Guard Her Grave, then stack flying swords until he falls first.

passive.description:
When Ziya deals damage to a target and they are defeated within 3s, he gains 1-3 EXP orbs.
When he reaches level 15, Sanctification Power is restored, granting the one-time skill Sanctify and increasing his level cap to level 25. Each level gained grants 20 Magical Attack.
Sanctify grants 1,200 EXP to a teammate, allowing them to break through their level cap, and potentially gain EXP orbs.
If Ziya acts as a support in the match, he grants additional Sanctification effects based on the teammate's class.
passive.name: Sanctification

skill1.description: Ziya places a divine seal on enemies in the target area, dealing 70 (70 + 14% magical attack) magical damage, followed by 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage every 0.4s for a total of 7 hits. Sealed enemies will gradually lose up to 30% of their Movement Speed and 10% of their physical defense and 10% of their magical defense. If the skill hits any enemy, he gains a 30% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 1s.
skill1.name: Divine Seal

skill2.description: Ziya unleashes divine retribution on wrongdoers, conjuring a magic circle that deals 3 strikes of damage to enemies in the target area. Each strike deals 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage. After a short delay, the magic circle explodes, dealing 300 (300 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and launching them for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Divine Punishment

skill3.description:
Ziya channels divine energy in the target direction, unleashing 3 shockwaves. The first 2 shockwaves each deal 120 (120 + 20% magical attack) magical damage, while the last deals 560 (560 + 80% magical attack) magical damage.
Upon reaching level 15, Ziya's Sanctification Power is restored, and there is a 20% chance of entering the Sanctifier state, allowing him to launch a shockwave while moving. Each subsequent level gained increases the chance of entering the Sanctifier state by 20%.
The charging lasts up to 2s, and moving or using the Ultimate again will immediately unleash the shockwaves. Charge time affects the attack range of the shockwaves, up to a distance of 1,800. Shockwaves deal 10% damage to structures in their path.
skill3.name: Universal Law

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Ziya's main job is to keep levelling until 15 without dying. Place Divine Seal where the wave and the opponent overlap and a single cast both clears minions and chips the enemy. Enemies he damaged drop EXP orbs when they die, so pick them all up to build a level lead. With no blink, stay close to your tower while the enemy jungler is out of sight. Divine Punishment's knock-up is also how he protects himself, so after using it to attack, don't push forward until it is ready again.
strategy.midGame: Reaching level 15 raises Ziya's own level cap, and from then on each level also adds magical attack. At the same time he gains Sanctify, a skill he can use only once. Sanctify is aimed at one ally, who receives EXP and can keep levelling past their cap. When Ziya is playing the roam position, that ally also gets an extra effect based on their role. Who receives it shapes the rest of the match, so the usual choice is an ally whose next level changes how they fight. Around the same time, Universal Law can start entering the Sanctifier state. Whether it does is a matter of chance, and the chance rises as he levels. In that state he can fire the shockwave while moving and it reaches further the longer he charges, so when it shows up, use it to wear enemies down in standoffs before Shadow Tyrant or Overlord. When it doesn't, settle for the regular three-shockwave cast and wait.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Ziya puts his effort into the setup. Lay Divine Seal on the path enemies will take to strip their speed and defenses, and place Divine Punishment where the enemy diver is likely to land. The blast takes a moment to go off, so placing it after they have already jumped usually comes too late. Once the fight starts, fire Universal Law from the very back and push out the most wounded enemies one by one. While the enemy assassin is out of sight, hold off on charging and secure a spot where you can fire without being touched.

combos.title: Seal, Then Launch
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Divine Seal: slow and shred defense) → Skill 2 (Divine Punishment: delayed blast and knock-up) → Skill 3 (Universal Law: three shockwaves)
combos.description: Enemies inside Divine Seal steadily lose speed and defense, which makes it easier to judge where the delayed Divine Punishment will land. Firing Universal Law while they are in the air makes it easier to reach the heavy third shockwave.

combos.title: Charge and Fire From Range
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (charge it in the Sanctifier state) → Skill 1 (follow-up)
combos.description: In the Sanctifier state, the shockwave reaches further the longer you charge it. Firing from a distance enemies cannot close makes it a good way to wear their HP down first in a standoff before an objective. It also hits towers and crystals in its path, but the damage that gets through is small, so leave tower-breaking to your team.

combos.title: Use the Speed to Get Away
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (land it to gain speed) → back off → Skill 2 (knock up the chaser)
combos.description: Ziya has no blink; his way to open distance is the speed he gains when Divine Seal lands. The boost fades quickly, so the first step after the cast is where you gain the most ground. Place Divine Punishment on the path of whoever follows and the knock-up ends the chase.

strengths: Sanctify lets one ally break through their level cap
In the Sanctifier state, his shockwave reaches further the longer he charges it
Divine Seal's slow and defense shred win the standoffs before objectives
EXP orbs from enemies he helped kill make an early level lead easier
weaknesses: No blink; when someone reaches him, his defense depends on where he places Divine Punishment
Moving while charging releases the shockwave, so a full charge means standing still
His real strength starts at level 15, so a bad early game is hard to recover
Using Sanctify on the wrong ally or at the wrong time wastes much of his late game

playstyle.style: Ziya is a mage who takes on a bigger role from level 15. Until then he wears down enemies' speed and defenses with Divine Seal, launches them with Divine Punishment, then follows up from range with the shockwaves of Universal Law. Reaching level 15 raises his own level cap and gives him Sanctify, a skill he can use once per match to raise one ally's level cap as well.
playstyle.suited: His power only starts to climb visibly at level 15, so you need the patience to get through lane without dying. When and on whom to use Sanctify is a choice he gets once per match, which rewards players who like reading how a game is going. If you want to take over early by killing opponents, the wait until his turn will feel long.

synergy.reason: Di Renjie exposes the target's location, so Liu Bang can land his fully charged Staggering Charge after teleporting.
Butterfly only halves Basic Attack damage after diving in, and Liu Bang's ultimate shield covers the skill damage she still takes.

counters.reason: Marco Polo's Destruction stacks strip defense and add true damage that Liu Bang's armor cannot reduce.
Lu Bu is immune to crowd control while diving, and his landing knock-up breaks Liu Bang's ultimate channel.

passive.description: Liu Bang gains 1 mark every second, for up to 4 marks. Basic Attacks expend all marks, dealing an additional 80 (80 + 10% magical attack) magical damage per mark. At maximum marks, the next Basic Attack is enhanced into a ranged attack that deals 474 (294 + 100% physical attack + 42% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Royal Ambition

skill1.description:
Liu Bang gains a shield that negates 650 (650 + 20% extra Health) damage for 5s. Upon expiry, the shield detonates and deals 650 (650 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
After 1.5s, using the skill again will detonate the shield immediately. If the shield is broken, it will only deal 50% damage.
skill1.name: Dominator's Shield

skill2.description:
Liu Bang dashes a distance of 275−550 in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 40% magical attack)−600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and stunning them for 0.75s.
This skill can be charged for up to 1s, and its effects depend on charging time. If the charge is interrupted or canceled, the cooldown will be reduced by 40%.
skill2.name: Staggering Charge

skill3.description:
Liu Bang selects a teammate and starts channeling in place, granting the teammate a shield that negates (480 + 12% target's extra Health)−(960 + 24% target's extra Health) damage. After 2.2s, he teleports to the teammate.
Upon arriving, Liu Bang gains 30% Movement Speed and restores 300 (300 + 8% extra Health) Health to himself and nearby teammates. He also fully charges Staggering Charge, keeping it charged for 10s.
After channeling for 0.4s, this skill can be used again to immediately teleport to the teammate, remove their shield, and deal 200 (200 + 40% magical attack)−400 (400 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. However, he will not gain the recovery effect.
The longer he channels, the stronger the shield becomes and the more damage he deals upon ending the channeling early.
skill3.name: Battlefield Command

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Bang's default home is the clash lane. Until level 4, Skill 1's shield and delayed blast handle the waves, while the Passive's four-stack ranged empowered basic lets you chip melee opponents without ever being touched. Skill 2's charged dash is your only stun and it's precious — through the early game, hold it as the counter-punch for enemy jungler ganks. Liu Bang's real value unlocks with his Ultimate and its map-wide reach, so through this window, simply banking experience without dying earns a passing grade.
strategy.midGame: After the 4-minute Tyrant, your two-front war begins. Shove side waves, and the moment a teammate gets touched anywhere on the map, channel your Ultimate and warp to them. You arrive delivering shields, and for 10 seconds after warping, Skill 2 sits at max charge — meaning an immediate full-range stun dash the second you land. The 2.2-second channel is a complete opening, so always cast from brush or behind a tower. Your goal is planting one thought in every enemy's head: if Liu Bang is off the map, this could be a 5v6.
strategy.lateGame: With three or more defense items after 15 minutes, split push and make two defenders deal with you. A detail worth banking: your Ultimate's shield scales with the target's bonus HP, so it lands biggest on your beefiest tank or fighter. The gold-standard pattern is pushing a side lane until seconds before Overlord, then warping in as it spawns. And if five enemies start collapsing on you, the warp to a distant ally is itself your escape hatch.
strategy.teamfight: Fighting with your team from the start, the job is catching the enemy carry with Skill 2's stun and layering Skill 1's blast on top. The shield can be manually detonated 1.5 seconds after casting, so when enemies glue themselves to you, pop it yourself and waste nothing. Arriving from a side lane instead, drop onto their backline mid-fight and let the max-charge Skill 2 flip the board. Engage together or arrive late — read the enemy comp and pick your policy in the first half, and the hesitation disappears.

combos.title: Drop Into the Fight
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (2.2s channel → teleport to the ally) → Skill 2 (max-charge dash stun) → Skill 1 (shield) → Basic Attack
