Divine Glow - Annihilation only hits enemies in its path, so targets moving sideways can avoid it

playstyle.style: Nuwa is a mage who uses her passive's extra range and vision to wear enemies down from afar. The matrices she places with Divine Glow - Coalescence are walls that only she can move through quickly and that enemy heroes cannot cross, and they explode when her other skills hit them. Placing walls first and firing second is what drives both her damage and her safety.
playstyle.suited: Every exchange starts with deciding where to put a wall. If you like taking time to set up and opening fights on your own terms, you will enjoy how a well-placed wall turns straight into damage. Players who are at their best reacting in sudden scrambles may find the setup time frustrating.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's Time Flux gives the diving Nezha the speed to stay on a target and then get out.
Zhang Fei's Leaping Savior shields teammates around his landing spot, so a Nezha diving in with him holds the line longer.

counters.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract makes the two share damage, so Nezha's own team ends up hitting him.
Diaochan heals each time her floral marks trigger and burns Nezha with true damage for staying close.

passive.description:
Nezha receives a shield that negates 75 (75 + 1.5% extra Health) true damage for every enemy hero he damages with a skill, for up to 800 (800 + 20% extra Health) true damage in total. This also triggers Wind-Fire Wheels 1 time, increasing Movement Speed by 5% for 3s, for up to 5 stacks.
The true damage shield can be recovered at the spawn point.
When he deals damage using Basic Attacks or Scorching Ember, or deals damage to a non-hero unit, he only gets a shield negating 20 (20 + 0.5% extra Health) true damage.
Each target can trigger Wind-Fire Wheels up to 1 time.
passive.name: Scorching Ember

skill1.description:
Nezha deals 330 (330 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and places Scorching Ember on them, dealing 42 (42 + 17% extra physical attack) true damage to the enemy every second for 5s, for up to 3 stacks. Damage increases by 50% with each stack. Scorching Ember also reduces the target's Health recovery by 15%.
The duration of Scorching Ember is refreshed when Nezha deals damage to the target.
skill1.name: Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep

skill2.description:
Flips behind the target to deal 150 (150 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage. He also gains a shield that negates 24 (24 + 0.5% extra Health) true damage, halved for non-hero units.
This skill cannot be used on the same target again for 3s.
skill2.name: Red Armillary Sash - Bind

skill3.description:
Nezha selects an enemy hero and flies to their location, dealing 450 (450 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking them back.
After landing, Nezha gains 10% damage reduction and 20% Resistance for 4s.
This skill enters a 50%-100% Cooldown based on flight distance. If the target is untargetable upon arrival, Nezha waits until the untargetable state ends and then immediately knocks the target back (can wait up to 0.5s).
skill3.name: Universe Ring - Skyfall

skill4.description:
Nezha unleashes the universe ring, dealing 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage to all enemy heroes across the entire map and gaining vision. Enhances the range of Universe Ring - Skyfall to cover the entire map for 5s.
Heroes revealed by this effect cannot use recall.
skill4.name: Universe Ring

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Nezha doesn't force a win before learning his Ultimate; he chips with Scorching Ember from Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep. Trades suit many short contacts. Flipping behind the opponent with Red Armillary Sash - Bind lets him keep hitting from outside their front.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Universe Ring - Skyfall, how he plays the map changes. When the minimap shows a wounded enemy or an isolated back-liner, fly to them, break their position with the landing knockback and sandwich them with your team. Skyfall's cooldown depends on flight distance, so the closer the target, the sooner it comes back. When the fight over Tyrant stalls, pressuring the opposite lane without showing himself makes it easier to force the enemy to split up. Limit your targets to enemies your team can reach right away. Flying in the moment the enemy marksman steps forward lets the knockback pull them out of formation, and Scorching Ember follows straight after. Scorching Ember's healing reduction also slows the support's attempts to restore them. The November 5 update lowered the damage of Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep and Skyfall.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, decide in advance whether Nezha flies first or last. If your team has another engager, flying onto the remaining damage dealer after the enemy has used their crowd control is the steadier option. After landing, stack Scorching Ember with Fire-tipped Spear and keep flipping behind the target with Red Armillary Sash to burn them down with true damage. He struggles when the enemy spreads out and fires from range, so aim to start fights in tight terrain.

combos.title: Ambush From Map-Wide Vision
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Universe Ring: damage and vision on every enemy hero) → Skill 3 (Universe Ring - Skyfall: fly in and knock back) → Skill 1 (Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep: Scorching Ember) → Skill 2 (Red Armillary Sash - Bind: flip behind)
combos.description: Pick a target whose recall is blocked by Universe Ring's vision and fly to them with Skyfall. Landing grants damage reduction and Resistance, so keep chipping with Fire-tipped Spear and Red Armillary Sash and hold on until your team arrives.

combos.title: Keep Scorching Ember Burning
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep: apply Scorching Ember) → Skill 2 (Red Armillary Sash - Bind: flip behind and gain a shield) → Skill 1 (Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep: add stacks)
combos.description: Scorching Ember keeps dealing true damage for a while and grows with each stack. Dealing damage also refreshes its duration, so weave in Red Armillary Sash flips and keep it burning. Red Armillary Sash cannot be used on the same target again right away, so fill the gaps with Fire-tipped Spear and Basic Attacks.

strengths: Skyfall flies him to a distant enemy hero, and Universe Ring extends it to the whole map
Scorching Ember's true damage and healing reduction get through enemies who rely on healing
His shield stacks every time a skill lands, so he is hard to kill in brawls
After Skyfall lands, he takes less damage and gains Resistance
weaknesses: Skyfall only flies him to the target, so he is easily isolated if his team does not follow
His burst is modest, so targets sometimes escape before he finishes them
His shield only stacks when skills land, so a string of misses leaves him unprotected
Until he learns his Ultimate, Red Armillary Sash - Bind's flip is his only way to close in

playstyle.style: Nezha is a fighter who stacks a shield against true damage every time his skills hit an enemy hero, and drops from the sky onto a chosen enemy hero with Universe Ring - Skyfall. Casting Universe Ring briefly lets Skyfall reach every enemy hero on the map, and enemies it reveals cannot recall. Scorching Ember, applied by Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep, keeps dealing true damage and reduces the target's Health recovery.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who want to go catch a chosen target themselves. Skyfall leaves him isolated if his team does not follow, so he needs the composure to check the minimap for teammates before flying. Whether you can hold Universe Ring until the turning point of the match also decides how he plays.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's pull bunches enemies into one spot and stuns them, so every flying sword lands at once.
Dolia's Celestial Melody refunds Freshly Forged, so Gan & Mo get another full set of flying sword charges.

counters.reason: Mai Shiranui strips magical defense, then dashes in and launches Gan & Mo, who cannot answer while airborne.
Sun Ce keeps super armor while piloting his ship, so the knockback on Guard Her Grave cannot stop him.

passive.description:
Whenever Gan uses a flying sword skill at a target location, Mo unleashes an equal number of swords to the same location at the same time to deal equal damage. Flying sword skills share usage caps.
Flying swords place 1 stack of Sword Energy on enemies hit. If a flying sword hits a marked target, each stack deals 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage.
If multiple flying swords hit a marked target at the same time, subsequent hits only deal 50% of this damage.
Gan & Mo's Basic Attacks deal 300 (300 + 25% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Forever Entwined

skill1.description:
Gan unleashes Splitting Swords in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage twice to enemies within range and knocking them back, while also retreating in the opposite direction. Reduces hit enemies' Magical Defense by 150 for 3s.
Passive: Each defeat or assist grants Gan & Mo 1 Splitting Sword, increasing their magical attack by 15, for up to 20 stacks.
skill1.name: Guard Her Grave

skill2.description:
Unleash flying swords in the target direction, dealing 325 (325 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in their path, and an extra 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies with Sword Energy.
Flying sword skills share a usage cap, with one charge restored every 5-6s (cooldown reduces with skill level). When the same Sword Energy is triggered multiple times, the second time onwards only deals 50% damage.
skill2.name: Coupled Blades - Short

skill3.description:
Unleash flying swords in the target direction, dealing 325 (325 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in their path, and an extra 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies with Sword Energy.
Flying sword skills share a usage cap, with one charge restored every 5-6s (cooldown reduces with skill level). When the same Sword Energy is triggered multiple times, the second time onwards only deals 50% damage.
skill3.name: Coupled Blades - Long

skill4.description:
Immediately gains 2 uses of flying sword skills and enhances the next flying sword skill to unleash more swords.
Passive: Increases field of vision by 15% and increases the usage cap of flying sword skills by 1. Each time a flying sword hits an enemy, this skill's cooldown is reduced by 1s.
skill4.name: Freshly Forged

strategy.earlyGame: Gan & Mo outrange the entire mid lane from level 1. Everything about the duo's damage flows from crossing Skill 2's short-range blades with Skill 3's long-range blades at a single point, so the second volley detonates the Sword Energy the first one left behind — spend the opening waves calibrating that intersection distance on stationary minions. Blade skills draw from a shared usage cap that only restores one charge every five to six seconds, which means never stepping forward right after emptying it. If someone jumps you, Skill 1's knockback-and-hop-back buys exactly one reset. That is the only insurance policy you own; price it accordingly.
strategy.midGame: From about 7-8 minutes, with your first core item finished, one clean intersection removes close to half of an enemy mage's HP. Before the 4:00 Tyrant or the 10:00 Shadow Tyrant, simply raining blades from maximum range onto anyone entering the pit forces the enemy to open the fight pre-chipped — that is Gan & Mo's brand of pressure. Skill 1 banks bonus magic attack on every kill and assist, so involvement snowballs the damage curve on its own. Skip the roams. Push mid, step back, carve sword qi into whoever contests, repeat.
strategy.lateGame: With Skill 1 grown to 15-20 stacks, a single intersection deletes a marksman outright — which is precisely why the enemy will spend everything to reach you. Two non-negotiables: stand behind every teammate, and never fight with a wall at your back. Do not hunt with Skill 1 either; hold it as the reaction card you play the instant someone commits to the jump. During Overlord fights, dropping blades from outside the pit's perimeter slowly bends the enemy formation out of shape until someone makes the mistake you have been waiting for.
strategy.teamfight: Gan & Mo never need to walk forward in a teamfight. From the deepest backline, punish any enemy frontliner who stops moving by crossing the short and long blades on their feet — that alone is a full shift's work. Priority targets: pre-fight clumps and anyone locked down by your team's CC. Chasing sprinting targets with blades is wasted ammunition. Skill 1's 150 magic defense shred also boosts your allied mage, so land it on the focus target first. Empty the charges, take one step back, wait for the refill. Guard that rhythm and you survive.

combos.title: Crossing the Blades
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (short-range flying swords, applies Sword Energy) → Skill 3 (long-range flying swords into the same spot, +75 per Sword Energy stack) → Basic Attack (300 magical damage)
combos.description: When Gan sends flying swords, Mo mirrors the same number into the same spot, so every cast lands doubled. Get Sword Energy on the target first and the follow-up volley adds 75 magical damage per stack. Charges only refill one every 5-6s, so pick your retreat before you empty them.

combos.title: Reloading With Skill 4
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (instantly stock 2 flying sword uses, enhance the next one) → Skill 3 → Skill 2
combos.description: Skill 4 is ammunition, not damage. It hands back two charges at once and makes the next flying sword summon more blades. Every flying sword that connects shaves 1s off Skill 4's cooldown, so accuracy shortens the wait for the next reload.

combos.title: Answer to a Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (knock back while retreating in the opposite direction, -150 Magical Defense) → Skill 3 → Skill 2
combos.description: Skill 1 is the only way Gan & Mo create space on their own. Bounce the diver, back off, and pour both blade skills into the 3s window where their Magical Defense sits 150 lower. Spend it on offense and there is nothing left the next time someone jumps you.

strengths: Crossed blade intersections burst enemies from beyond retaliation range
Skill 1 banks up to 20 stacks of magic attack off kills and assists
Knockback plus hop-back on Skill 1 is genuine anti-assassin insurance
The 150 magic defense shred amplifies every magic dealer on the team
weaknesses: Damage tracks intersection accuracy one-to-one; the skill floor is steep
No mobility skill, so a closed gap almost always means death
Blade charges are finite and the pressure vanishes once they are spent
No hard CC of their own, so they cannot lock anyone down solo

playstyle.style: An extreme-range artillery mage whose paired blades both strike wherever he aims — one act of aim, double the payload. Accuracy converts directly into multiplied damage.
playstyle.suited: snipers who trust their aim — one cast sends two blades, and landing them where they cross is how accuracy turns into damage from outside anyone's reach.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's Unbridled Outburst stuns whoever it flings to the far end, right as Athena's Immovable Aegis counterattacks.
Dharma pins enemies against a wall and stuns them, so Athena's enhanced Unstoppable Spear attack lands cleanly.

counters.reason: Sun Bin's Time Lapse interrupts and silences Athena, so her engage stops dead on the spot.
Guan Yu in Charge Stance keeps knocking Athena back, so her combo never gets to land.

passive.description:
Able to move freely in her Divine form after dying, gaining 30 Movement Speed and a new Divine skill to aid teammates.
When resurrected, flies toward the nearest allied tower, dealing 600 (600 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies within takeoff range for 0.75s.
passive.name: Divine Awakening

skill1.name: Holy Advance / Victory Call
skill1.description: Dashes ahead while raising her Aegis, gaining a shield that negates 500 (500 + 7.5% extra Health) damage and grants 1s of crowd control immunity while dealing 400 (400 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies and knocking them back.

forms.description: Dashes ahead while raising her Aegis, gaining a shield that negates 500 (500 + 7.5% extra Health) damage and grants 1s of crowd control immunity while dealing 400 (400 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies and knocking them back.
Athena dashes in the target direction.

skill2.name: Unstoppable Spear / Victory Call
skill2.description:
Leaps in the target direction and enhances the next Basic Attack. When using this enhanced Basic Attack, charges at the enemy, dealing 180 (180 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage, plus extra physical damage to non-structures equal to 6% of the target's lost Health (damage capped at 300 against monsters).
Hitting enemies with Holy Advance and Immovable Aegis resets Unstoppable Spear's cooldown.
Enhanced Basic Attacks deal an extra 40% damage to non-hero units.

forms.description:
Leaps in the target direction and enhances the next Basic Attack. When using this enhanced Basic Attack, charges at the enemy, dealing 180 (180 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage, plus extra physical damage to non-structures equal to 6% of the target's lost Health (damage capped at 300 against monsters).
Hitting enemies with Holy Advance and Immovable Aegis resets Unstoppable Spear's cooldown.
Enhanced Basic Attacks deal an extra 40% damage to non-hero units.
Athena spreads her wings, granting a nearby teammate a shield that negates 250 (250 + 80% physical attack + 5% extra Health) damage for 2s.

skill3.name: Immovable Aegis / Victory Call
skill3.description: Athena raises her Aegis, gaining a shield that negates 1,200 (1,200 + 16% extra Health) damage and grants crowd control immunity. After 1.5s, she uses her Aegis to perform a counterattack, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in range. Each time she is attacked by an enemy hero while her Aegis is raised, her counterattack damage increases by 10% and her Aegis's casting time is reduced by 10%, for up to 5 stacks.

forms.description: Athena raises her Aegis, gaining a shield that negates 1,200 (1,200 + 16% extra Health) damage and grants crowd control immunity. After 1.5s, she uses her Aegis to perform a counterattack, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in range. Each time she is attacked by an enemy hero while her Aegis is raised, her counterattack damage increases by 10% and her Aegis's casting time is reduced by 10%, for up to 5 stacks.

Athena flies toward the nearest allied tower. During takeoff, she deals 600 (600 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range (scales with hero level) and launches them for 0.75s. She also protects nearby teammates and causes them to retreat with her.
This active skill cannot be used when the respawn timer is below 10s.
If Athena uses her Ultimate while dead, she cannot grant protection or follow-up effects to teammates after resurrecting.

strategy.earlyGame: Athena's laning is a level-2 trade loop: jump in with Skill 2, land the empowered basic attack, dash out with Skill 1 — and because a connected Skill 1 refunds Skill 2's cooldown, you immediately get another round trip. Run that cycle and only your opponent's health bar moves. The empowered hit adds 6% of the target's missing HP, so the more chipped they are, the harder it lands. Level 4 unlocks the full all-in: two shields with crowd control immunity layered on top. The only real way to throw it is whiffing, so pick your jump target with care.
strategy.midGame: Around 7-8 minutes, one core item in, Athena's mobility starts cashing checks. Shove your side wave, then use Skill 2's leap to cut through the river and hit the 4:00 Tyrant or any skirmish from the flank. Before diving, count the enemy's key lockdown skills — if one is still up, time Skill 1's one second of crowd control immunity to slide through it and reach the backline safely. Do not rush the Ultimate out either. Its retaliation grows every time enemies strike the braced shield, so the moment they focus you is the moment it starts printing damage.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Athena is a time bomb strapped to the enemy backline. As long as Skill 1 and the Ultimate keep connecting, Skill 2 keeps refreshing, and no amount of running rescues a marksman you have decided to keep. Do not overlook the Passive: on death she respawns at the nearest allied tower with a knock-up burst, so in defensive scenarios even a death converts into a play. That insurance barely functions when you are the one diving deep, so measure your entry. At Shadow Tyrant, slide in from behind after both sides have traded skills — that is where she cuts deepest.
strategy.teamfight: Decide one thing before every teamfight: whose face are you living in. Athena's damage is stacked empowered basics, so swapping targets mid-fight means killing no one. The ideal is single-minded pursuit of the enemy marksman. Slip the first lockdown with Skill 1's crowd control immunity, raise the Ultimate against their counterattack so every hit feeds the retaliation, then dump it back on them. One detail everyone forgets in practice: you can walk while the shield is braced. Drifting toward your escape route during those seconds is often the difference between a reset and a respawn.

combos.title: Riding the Resets
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (leap) → Empowered Basic Attack (+180, plus 6% of the target's lost Health) → Skill 1 (dash, knock back; a hit resets Skill 2) → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: A Skill 1 that connects refunds Skill 2's cooldown on the spot. The empowered attack adds 6% of the target's lost Health, so it bites harder the longer the fight runs. Miss Skill 1 and the loop stops dead, leaving you parked in their team with nothing.

combos.title: Brace, Then Answer
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (1,200 shield, crowd control immunity) → Absorb their attacks to grow the counter → Counterattack after 1.5s (450 magical damage; a hit resets Skill 2) → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Every hit an enemy hero lands on the raised Aegis adds 10% counterattack damage and cuts 10% off its casting time, up to 5 stacks. Raising it after they commit is what makes the answer heavy. The counterattack also refunds Skill 2, so the follow-up leap is waiting the moment it lands.

strengths: Skill 1 and Ultimate hits refund Skill 2, so her mobility never runs dry
Shields with crowd control immunity slip enemy lockdown on demand
Missing-HP empowered basics give her a real answer to tanks
Tower respawn passive turns defensive deaths into tempo, not losses
weaknesses: A whiffed Skill 1 or Ultimate stalls the reset engine mid-combo
No burst, so disciplined enemies can recover before she finishes them
Respawn is fixed to the nearest allied tower — weak while sieging
Reset bookkeeping is expert-level; sloppy play accomplishes nothing

playstyle.style: A shield-and-dash fighter who doesn't stop at death — she remains on the field as a divine spirit, supporting her team, and her respawn descent hits like a skill. Dying is part of her kit.
playstyle.suited: players who want to dive deeper than anyone else — landing Skill 1 or Skill 3 refunds the leap, and being killed leaves you on the field as a spirit rather than out of the fight.

synergy.reason: Hou Yi keeps attacking with no way to disengage, so Tune of Tranquility's heal and defense are what keep him alive.
Gao keeps performing deep in the enemy team, so Tune of Tranquility's heal and defense cover his whole song.

counters.reason: Musashi's Duel to the Death delays all recovery on his target, so Cai Yan's healing arrives only after the duel ends.
Lady Zhen's Destructive Deluge pool denies Cai Yan a place to heal from, and its slow keeps her from leaving.

passive.description:
When taking damage, Cai Yan gains 35% Movement Speed that diminishes over 2s. She also recovers 250 (250 +50% magical attack) Health per second for 2s.
The passive can only be triggered once every 10s.
passive.name: Can't Touch This

skill1.description: Cai Yan plays a tune, increasing her Movement Speed by 40% and restoring 60 (60 + 20% magical attack) Health to teammates every 0.5s for 3s. Restores 50% less Health to non-hero units.
skill1.name: Healing Hymn

skill2.description:
Cai Yan launches a sound wave that bounces between enemies. Each hit deals 270 (270 + 48% magical attack) magical damage and stuns the enemy for 0.75s.
Each sound wave bounces up to 6 times, and the same target can only be hit by 2 bounces. The second bounce inflicts only 25% of the initial damage and stun duration.
skill2.name: Earworm

skill3.description: Cai Yan plays her harp, restoring 90 (90 + 45% magical attack) Health to the teammate with the lowest Health within range every 0.5s for 5s while increasing their physical defense and magical defense by 200 (200 + 30% magical attack).
skill3.name: Tune of Tranquility

strategy.earlyGame: In lane, staying next to your laner is the core of Cai Yan's early job. When the enemy goes in, answer with Earworm and let your ally hit back while the stun holds. Walking with Healing Hymn after a trade restores your ally's Health, which helps them stay in lane longer. Taking damage triggers Can't Touch This, speeding her up and restoring Health, but it only triggers at intervals, so avoid standing where she can be focused again and again.
strategy.midGame: Once she learns Tune of Tranquility, she can rescue one ally in a skirmish. Who it goes to depends on how much Health each ally has left, so casting it when the ally you want to save is the most wounded puts it where you mean it. While your team takes down Tyrant or Overlord, hold Earworm on the path enemies would use to come in from the side, and stun whoever enters. Its cooldown drops as the skill levels up, so leveling it when you can helps it come back in time for the next fight.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfights come down to two choices: spend Earworm on the enemy's entry or save it to stop a chase, and decide near whom to open Tune of Tranquility. The sound wave bounces between enemies, so releasing it as they dive in a group hits more of them. Get near the ally you want to protect before casting Tune of Tranquility. Rescue, the active on her first item, shields every ally in range at once. If Cai Yan goes down first the healing stops, so she stays behind her own back line.

combos.title: Stop the Dive With Sound
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Earworm: bouncing stun) → Skill 3 (Tune of Tranquility: protect the lowest-Health ally) → Skill 1 (Healing Hymn: heal on the move)
combos.description: The more tightly enemies bunch up, the more targets the sound wave can bounce to. Opening Tune of Tranquility while the stun has them stopped lets the targeted ally recover Health and defense. Finish with Healing Hymn to speed up and fall back with the team while still healing.

combos.title: Stop the Chasers on the Way Out
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Healing Hymn: speed up and heal allies) → Skill 2 (Earworm: stun the chasers)
combos.description: Once you decide to fall back, cast Healing Hymn first to gain speed and restore allies' Health while running. When the chasers get close, Earworm's stun stops the pursuit. The more of them follow, the more targets the wave has to bounce to.

strengths: Tune of Tranquility heals the lowest-Health ally in range and raises their defenses
Earworm bounces between enemies and stuns each one it hits
Taking damage gives her Movement Speed and Health back, buying time to escape
Healing Hymn speeds her up, so she heals allies on the move
weaknesses: Against a lone target, Earworm bounces onto them only twice, and the second bounce is weaker
Can't Touch This only triggers at intervals, so repeated focus can still catch her
Tune of Tranquility covers one ally, chosen by who has the lowest Health
Earworm is her only crowd control, so a miss leaves her nothing to stop divers

playstyle.style: Cai Yan's healing from the roam position comes from two skills. Healing Hymn restores teammates' Health bit by bit, while Tune of Tranquility heals the lowest-Health ally in range and raises their physical and magical defense. When enemies close in, Earworm sends out a sound wave that stuns each enemy it bounces to.
playstyle.suited: Her job leans toward keeping allies alive rather than taking enemies down. Tune of Tranquility goes to the ally with the lowest Health in range, so where she stands has to follow who is taking damage and where. Against a single enemy, Earworm has fewer targets to bounce to and hits fewer times.

synergy.reason: Angela's Blazing Brilliance is a long channel, and Forsaken Contract keeps a target pinned in place while it lands.
Guiguzi's camouflage hides Donghuang's approach, so he reaches Forsaken Contract range before anyone sees him coming.

counters.reason: Shouyue's Wild Wind scales with Donghuang's max Health, so building tanky only makes the snipe hit harder.
Gan & Mo's Guard Her Grave knocks Donghuang back, breaking the close range Forsaken Contract needs.

passive.description:
Whenever a dark orb of Donghuang's hits an enemy, it deals 100 (100 + 50% magical attack) magical damage, plus extra magical damage equal to 3% of the target's Health. At the same time, he recovers 162 (96 + 40% magical attack + 2% Health) Health.
When a dark orb hits a non-hero unit, he recovers 1% Health.
He can have up to 3 dark orbs orbiting him simultaneously.
passive.name: Soul Sacrifice

skill1.description:
Releases a burst of power, dealing 300 (300 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and creating a dark orb that orbits around him. Can have up to 3 dark orbs orbiting simultaneously.
When this skill hits an enemy, its Cooldown and Mana cost are reduced by 50%. If there are already 3 dark orbs present, restores 150 (150 + 60% magical attack) Health instead.
The number of dark orbs will influence the strength of Dark Impact.
skill1.name: Eclipse

skill2.description:
Donghuang consumes all of his dark orbs (there must be at least one) to barrage the target location, with each orb targeting a further area than the last. Orbs deal 500 (500 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range. When he uses this skill, he gains 30% Movement Speed for 1s. He gains 10% Movement Speed for every extra dark orb consumed.
The first orb slows enemies within range by 30% for 1s, the second slows enemies within range immensely for 1s, and the third will stun enemies within range for 1s.
skill2.name: Dark Impact

skill3.description:
Donghuang suppresses an enemy hero for 2s. While the enemy is suppressed by him, both share all damage taken.
He instantly gains 3 dark orbs when his Ultimate is used. During suppression, the orbs orbit 25% faster. Every 50 Magical Attack makes them orbit 5% faster, to a max of 100%.
skill3.name: Forsaken Contract

strategy.earlyGame: As a roamer, Donghuang starts moving once Eclipse has built his orbs. Orbs damage enemies based on their max Health and heal him with each hit, so he is strong in close fights in narrow bushes, and moving with your jungler can open chances to push into the enemy's side. Eclipse comes back quickly when it hits, so keep hitting minions and enemies with it to hold three orbs. Once Forsaken Contract is learned, check that Flash is ready and look for the first catch.
strategy.midGame: The areas around Tyrant and Overlord become his main ground. Get to the bushes on the paths into the pit first, roll Dark Impact down the path to chip and slow, and look for the stun with the third orb. The main threat is Flash into Forsaken Contract. During the suppression the target shares the damage he takes, so catching the enemy's key player while your team piles on lets him take them down with him. He cannot move during the suppression either, so only use it within your team's reach. Always know Flash's cooldown; whether that one spell is ready changes how far the enemy back line can safely walk.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, he either starts the fight or shuts down the enemy's start. On offense, Flash and Forsaken Contract stop the enemy's key player while your team pours in damage. On defense, hold a diving enemy with orbs and Dark Impact's stun. Because the damage is shared, using it on a sturdy frontliner rarely takes them down with him, so marksmen and assassins make better targets. He gets three orbs back the moment he casts it, so the damage keeps coming during the suppression.

combos.title: Catch Them With Flash
combos.sequence: Flash → Skill 3 (Forsaken Contract: suppress and share damage, gain three orbs) → hit with orbs → Skill 1 (Eclipse)
combos.description: Donghuang has no movement skill, so Flash does the work of closing the gap. Forsaken Contract fills him with three orbs at once, and they orbit faster during the suppression, taking Health from the target and healing him with each hit. Damage is shared both ways, so make the catch where your team's damage can land.

combos.title: Build Three Orbs and Win the Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Eclipse: create an orb) → Skill 1 → Skill 1 (three orbs) → hit with orbs → Skill 2 (Dark Impact: the third stuns)
combos.description: Eclipse's cooldown and cost drop when it hits, so he can stack up to three orbs quickly. Win the trade with orb hits, then fire Dark Impact: the first two orbs slow and the third stuns. Each orb lands further than the last, so leave some distance between him and the target you want to stun.

strengths: Forsaken Contract suppresses one enemy hero and shares the damage between them
Each dark orb hit takes a share of the enemy's max Health and heals him
Dark Impact's third orb stuns enemies in the area
Eclipse's cooldown and cost drop when it hits, so he builds orbs quickly
weaknesses: The dark orbs orbit close to him, so enemies who fight from range are hard to reach
He cannot move during the suppression, so using it out of his team's reach gets him killed
Each Dark Impact orb lands further than the last, so hitting with the stunning third one takes judgment of distance
No movement skill, so closing the gap tends to depend on Flash

playstyle.style: Donghuang is a support whose ultimate, Forsaken Contract, suppresses one enemy hero and makes the two of them share all damage taken. The dark orbs orbiting him deal damage based on the target's max Health and heal him each time they hit. He builds orbs with Eclipse and fires them all at once with Dark Impact, where the third orb stuns.
playstyle.suited: His job is to pick a target and offer up his own Health to hold them. He cannot move during the suppression either, so everything depends on using it where your team's damage can reach. Closing the gap often comes down to Flash, so players who track whether it is ready will find him easier.

synergy.reason: Gao grows tankier the more enemies stand near him, so Guiguzi's pull packs them into Rock Out! for him.
Angela's beam only pays out on a target that cannot move, and Guiguzi's pull and stun freeze one for her.

counters.reason: Li Bai clears debuffs and turns untargetable with two skills, so Guiguzi's long channeled pull rarely connects.
Mozi stacks a shield just by casting, so it soaks up Guiguzi's enhanced Basic Attack entirely.

passive.description:
After Guiguzi leaves the enemy's field of vision for 3s, his next Basic Attack will be enhanced, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25%−50% (increases with level) for 1.5s.
If he is not in the enemy's field of vision when using the enhanced Basic Attack, this skill's cooldown will be increased to 10s.
passive.name: The Laws of Nature

skill1.description:
Guiguzi covers himself in spriteflies that camouflage him from enemy sight for 4s. While camouflaged, he gains 40% Movement Speed and deals 450 (450 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to each enemy he touches, while reducing their physical defense and magical defense by 25% for 4s. This effect can only be triggered once on each enemy.
The camouflage disappears when he deals damage to enemies in any other way.
skill1.name: Prophecy - Hidden Hand

skill2.description: Guiguzi summons a large number of spriteflies that surround him, dealing 100 (100 + 15% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 2s to enemies within range, after which he pulls them in and stuns them for 1s, dealing 400 (400 + 60% magical attack) magical damage. If an enemy hero is hit, Guiguzi and teammates within range gain a shield that negates 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) damage.
skill2.name: The Animist

skill3.description:
Guiguzi orders spriteflies to cover himself and teammates within a range of 1,500, camouflaging everyone after 1s. The camouflage lasts for 4s, during which he and his teammates gain 30% Movement Speed and vision of the nearest enemy hero.
While camouflaged, using Basic Attacks, skills, or inflicting debuffs on enemies will immediately remove it.
skill3.name: Prophecy - Out of Sight

strategy.earlyGame: Guiguzi should have walked half the map before his first recall — that is the correct pace. Touch the mid wave for a moment, then slide toward a side lane under Skill 1's camouflage and 40% movement speed. Ghost through the enemy laner's back, and merely brushing them carves 25% off both defenses; your laner collapsing onto that debuff turns into a kill from thin air. One rule above all: attacking anything breaks the camouflage. The touch already did the work, so keep your hands to yourself.
strategy.midGame: Guiguzi's busiest window is the thirty seconds before each Tyrant spawn. Tuck into the pit-side bush with your jungler, and anyone who wanders up eats Skill 2's pull-and-stun — objective and numbers advantage in one motion. The Ultimate's team-wide camouflage can hand your side the opening of an entire teamfight, but spending it casually on travel leaves nothing for the moment that matters; commit it to engages, full stop. The free vision of the nearest enemy hero it grants sharpens every ambush you set.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game a single engage decides everything, which makes Guiguzi's stealth the trump card of trump cards. The script: cloak all five with the Ultimate, spread across the objective approach, and land Skill 2's pull on the enemy's structural piece — usually the carry. But understand that your durability is paper against late-game damage, and the two-second channel can be burned through, shield and all. Always start the play from inside your team's effective range. Solo hero-ball adventures are this hero's number one loss condition.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal sequence never changes: vanish the team with the Ultimate, thread Skill 1 through the enemy line to stamp the 25% defense shred on priority targets, then channel Skill 2 in the thick of their formation. Two seconds later the pull and stun compress them into one tidy package for your team's AoE. The shield on hero contact absorbs some of the opening fire, but the channel is your single point of failure — start it while their attention is fixed on your frontline, in that stolen instant when nobody is looking at you.

combos.title: Cloaked Team Approach
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (camouflages the team after 1s, 30% Movement Speed for 4s) → Skill 1 (contact cuts both defenses by 25%) → Skill 2 (pull and 1s stun after 2s)
combos.description: The camouflage drops the instant he uses a basic attack, a skill, or applies a debuff to an enemy. Touch nothing until the team is in position. Shred both defenses by 25% with Skill 1, then channel Skill 2 in the clump so the pull-stun arrives together with your team's damage.

combos.title: Bush Capture
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (camouflage, 40% Movement Speed, 25% off both defenses on contact) → Skill 2 (pull and 1s stun after 2s, 600 shield to allies on a hero hit) → Empowered Basic Attack (300 damage, 1.5s slow)
combos.description: Skill 2 needs a 2s channel, so starting it at a range they can simply walk out of wastes the cast. Close with Skill 1 first and the pull lands. The empowered attack requires 3s outside enemy vision, which the wait in the bush has already paid for.

strengths: Team-wide camouflage lets him dictate exactly when fights begin
Pull-stun engage plus ally shields makes his openings devastating
Skill 1's 25% dual-defense shred raises the whole team's damage
Stealth and speed give him unmatched roaming range for ambushes
weaknesses: Paper durability — a failed engage usually costs him his life
Skill 2's two-second channel whiffs badly against anyone who reads it
His openings evaporate if teammates do not follow up instantly
Close to zero solo damage or kill threat

playstyle.style: The architect of ambushes: he cloaks his entire team and delivers an invisible squad to the enemy's doorstep, with a mass pull and shields to finish the design.
playstyle.suited: shot-callers who want to design the opening — you cloak the whole team, walk it to the enemy's door, and land the pull before the two-second channel gets read.

synergy.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract locks an enemy hero in place, so Kongming's slow-channeling Spirit Bomb lands without fail.

counters.reason: Wukong's Protective Shroud eats the first skill Kongming throws and turns it into invincibility and a shield.
Allain builds Fury with every hit he lands, growing steadily tankier, so Kongming's chip damage never finishes him.

passive.description:
Kongming gains 1 mark for 10s every time his active skills hit an enemy, for up to 5 stacks. Upon reaching max stacks, he summons 5 prisms, which circle around him for 10s and attack the nearest enemy unit, dealing 135 (135 +25% magical attack) magical damage.
Prisms prioritize enemy heroes. They deal 40% less damage to monsters and 40% extra damage to minions.
passive.name: Time for Tactics

skill1.description:
Kongming fires 3 prisms in the target direction, each dealing 460 (460 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. When multiple prisms hit the same enemy, subsequent hits only deal 20% damage.
Each prism triggers 1 Strategic Mark. He stocks Arcane Assault every 7.5s, for up to 2 charges.
skill1.name: Arcane Assault

skill2.description:
Kongming blinks in the target direction, creating magic fields at the start and the end of the dash that each deal 350 (350 + 52% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. When an enemy takes damage twice from this skill within 5s, they are inflicted with extreme slow. This effect diminishes over 3s.
When an enemy takes damage from multiple fields at the same time, the second magic field only deals 50% damage.
He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 7.5s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.
skill2.name: Time Shift

skill3.description:
Kongming targets an enemy and starts channeling a Spirit Bomb, which deals 450 (450 + 55% magical attack) magical damage. Non-hero enemy units that are targeted or in the Spirit Bomb's path will take extra damage and be launched for 0.5s. Enemies take 2% extra damage from Spirit Bombs for every 1% Health lost.
When a Spirit Bomb hits and defeats an enemy hero, Kongming gains a full stack of marks, and this skill's Cooldown is reduced by 80%.
If the targeted enemy hero is defeated while the Spirit Bomb is being channeled, the Cooldown of this skill will still be reduced by 80%.
skill3.name: Winning Strategy

strategy.earlyGame: In lane, Kongming builds marks by sending Arcane Assault through both the wave and his opponent. Each of its prisms triggers a mark when it hits, so even shots at the wave fill his marks quickly. Once they are full, prisms appear around him and start attacking the nearest enemy on their own. These prisms prioritize enemy heroes and deal extra damage to minions, so while his marks are full he clears the wave and pokes at the same time. Time Shift stores charges; if you spend one going in, keep the other for backing off.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns his Ultimate, finishing enemies with the Spirit Bomb joins his game. The bomb grows with the Health its target has lost, so aim it at someone already worn down rather than at a healthy target. Killing an enemy hero with it refunds much of the cooldown and fills his marks right away. After one kill, look for the next enemy with low Health and fire again. Hitting the same enemy with Time Shift twice in a short window inflicts an extreme slow, so slow a fleeing target first and then chase with the Spirit Bomb. Spending every Time Shift charge on offense leaves him no way out, so keep one in hand while the enemy still has crowd control available.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Kongming enters from outside the spot where the frontlines collide. Arcane Assault stores charges, so keep casting it to hold his marks and let the prisms join the frontline brawl. Meanwhile, watch whose Health is falling and pick the Spirit Bomb's target. A kill refunds the cooldown, so look for the next target right after. Keep one Time Shift charge so he can reposition after firing.

combos.title: Finish the Wounded Target
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Arcane Assault: build marks) → Skill 2 (Time Shift: close the distance) → Skill 3 (Winning Strategy: lock on and fire)
combos.description: The Spirit Bomb gets stronger the more Health the target has lost, so wear them down with Arcane Assault and Time Shift's fields before firing. A kill refunds much of the cooldown and fills his marks at once, so he can head straight for the next target.

combos.title: Poke While Backing Off
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Arcane Assault) → Skill 2 (Time Shift: blink backward) → Prisms attack on their own
combos.description: Time Shift leaves a magic field where he leaves and where he lands, so even a retreat damages whoever is chasing. If his marks are full, the prisms attack the nearest enemy by themselves, keeping his damage going while he makes space.

strengths: Killing an enemy hero with the Spirit Bomb refunds much of its cooldown, so he can go straight for the next target
Time Shift is a blink with stored charges, usable both to engage and to escape
Once his marks are full, prisms attack nearby enemies automatically and prioritize heroes
The Spirit Bomb grows with the target's lost Health, which makes weakened enemies easier to finish
weaknesses: Without full marks there are no prisms, and his damage output drops
Once Time Shift's charges are spent, he has no escape until another one comes back
The Spirit Bomb barely grows against targets with high Health, so he has to choose who to fire at
When several Arcane Assault prisms hit the same enemy, every hit after the first deals far less

playstyle.style: Kongming's finisher is Winning Strategy's Spirit Bomb, which hits harder the more Health its target has lost. The damage that sets it up comes from Arcane Assault, the magic fields of Time Shift, and the prisms that appear once his marks are full. Time Shift is a blink he can stock charges of, so it serves for both going in and getting out.
playstyle.suited: Finishing an enemy hero with the Spirit Bomb refunds much of its cooldown, so he suits players who track whose Health is low and pick their target from that. The bomb does little against targets with plenty of Health left, so if you can't wait for the right moment, his damage goes to waste.

synergy.reason: Di Renjie's Imperial Order halves a target's defenses, so the allies Da Qiao teleports in hit far harder.
Mulan needs time to stack Balance, and Da Qiao's tide explosion slows enemies so they cannot slip away.

counters.reason: Han Xin is immune to crowd control during The Unrivaled Spear, so Da Qiao's koi launches do nothing.
Zhang Fei's Forbidden Domain knocks heroes back, scattering the team Da Qiao just gathered into Eye of the Whirlpool.

passive.description:
Da Qiao boosts her own Movement Speed by 30.
When the koi in Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge leaps past another skill's tide, it triggers a tide explosion, dealing 140 (140 + 25% magical attack) magical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1s.
For every 250 Magical Attack, the skill range of Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge increases by 50, with a maximum increase of 200.
passive.name: Law of Infinity

skill1.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 90 (90 + 13% magical attack) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s. Using skills increases Da Qiao's Movement Speed by 30% for 2.5s.
skill1.name: Leaping Koi Tide

skill2.description:
Da Qiao conjures a magic circle for 4s that grants vision. When it closes, she teleports a teammate to the spawn point, removing all debuffs. They can return via the portal at the Crystal.
If no hero teleports, the magic circle leaves behind a mark a teammate can touch to recall.
Using the skill again clears the mark. If no hero has teleported, 50% of the Cooldown is returned. Da Qiao teleports first. No channeling is required to touch the recall mark.
skill2.name: Sea of Fate

skill3.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps from left to right, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 90 (90 + 13% magical attack) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s.
skill3.name: Severing Surge

skill4.description: Da Qiao summons a whirlpool at the target location, dealing 500 (500 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range. The whirlpool lasts for 8s, during which teammates can teleport to it by tapping the Eye of the Whirlpool button. Da Qiao and teammates gain a shield that negates 350 (350 + 50% magical attack) damage while in the whirlpool. Da Qiao gains an extra shield that negates damage equal to 7% of her extra Health.
skill4.name: Eye of the Whirlpool

strategy.earlyGame: Da Qiao's early job is less about damage and more about learning how to place Sea of Fate. If no one is sent, half the cooldown comes back and the leftover mark lets a teammate recall by touching it. Either way the cost is small, so place it near a hurt ally early. Leaping Koi Tide also gives her a burst of Movement Speed, which helps her move between lanes.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, Eye of the Whirlpool becomes one of her biggest jobs. The whirlpool stays at the spot for a while, and teammates only need to tap its button to teleport there, so even allies far away can make it to the fight. Da Qiao and teammates inside get a shield, and hers grows with her extra Health. Use Sea of Fate on an ally pushing a side lane, and a worn-down ally can step out and come back through the Crystal portal. In skirmishes, send one koi through the tide the other left behind and Law of Infinity's explosion slows enemies down. More Magical Attack widens both koi skills, which gives magical attack items a purpose too.
strategy.teamfight: Da Qiao's place is the very back, watching the entrance to the fight. When an assassin jumps at your carry, launch them with Leaping Koi Tide, then sweep Severing Surge's koi across. The second launch plus the slow from the tide explosion makes it hard for the diver to finish the job. Eye of the Whirlpool deals damage but is not a tool for stopping enemies. It is for bringing teammates in and shielding them, so place it where the fight is about to start. Sea of Fate takes too long to close in the middle of a brawl, so put it in advance where hurt allies will retreat. When both koi are spent, use Law of Infinity's extra Movement Speed to keep your distance.

combos.title: Two Koi, Two Launches
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Leaping Koi Tide: straight koi, launch and tide) → Skill 3 (Severing Surge: sweeping koi, second launch, sets off the tide)
combos.description: Lay a tide with Leaping Koi Tide first, then send Severing Surge's koi across it, and Law of Infinity sets off an explosion that adds damage and a slow. Both launches are short, so the second koi needs to follow without a gap. Once the tide fades there is no explosion, so a late follow-up loses the slow too.

combos.title: Send Home, Call Back
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Sea of Fate: sends one teammate home when the circle closes) → Return through the portal at the Crystal → Skill 4 (Eye of the Whirlpool: a teleport point at the front, plus shields)
combos.description: Sea of Fate takes a while to close, so place it as soon as an ally's Health starts dropping. The ally sent back is also freed of debuffs. With Eye of the Whirlpool already placed at the front, one tap teleports them there, and they pick up a shield inside it.

strengths: Sea of Fate sends a teammate to the spawn point and removes their debuffs
Eye of the Whirlpool pulls teammates to the front and shields those inside it
Two koi knock-ups plus the slowing tide explosion help stop divers
If nobody teleports, Sea of Fate returns half its cooldown and leaves a recall mark
weaknesses: Sea of Fate only sends someone when the circle closes, too late for sudden burst
No skill to start fights; her self-defense is the koi knock-ups
Once both koi are spent, she cannot stop anyone until they come back
Eye of the Whirlpool does not launch anyone, so it cannot stop enemies

playstyle.style: What Da Qiao moves around is not the enemy but her own team. Sea of Fate sends a teammate to the spawn point, and they can come back through the portal at the Crystal. Once Eye of the Whirlpool is down, teammates can teleport to it by tapping its button.
playstyle.suited: Da Qiao's contribution shows up less in kills than in decisions: who to send home, when, and where to call the team. She fights with the two koi from Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge, but she has no skill to start a fight herself. She suits players who can keep watching allies' Health and positions and deciding whether to send someone now or wait.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's shield soaks the damage aimed at Huang Zhong, so he keeps firing while stuck in Turret Mode.
Lian Po's slow and launch pin enemies at the turret's center, where Huang Zhong's shots hit hardest.

counters.reason: Marco Polo adds true damage against targets with Destroyed Defense, slipping past the defenses Turret Mode grants.
Shouyue's snipe scales off max Health, and Huang Zhong cannot dodge it while locked in Turret Mode.

passive.description: Huang Zhong's Basic Attacks increase his physical attack by 6-12 and Critical Rate by 0.75%-1.5% (increases with hero level) for 1.5s, for up to 5 stacks. These buffs are doubled when he is in Turret Mode. When he enters or exits Turret Mode, the buffs' durations are refreshed, and the buff multiplier is replaced with the multiplier of the current mode.
passive.name: Gunner's Spirit

skill1.description:
Huang Zhong unleashes his potential, gaining 70% Movement Speed that diminishes over 2s. If he is in Turret Mode, he can leave it immediately.
Passive: He gains 20 physical attack (doubled while the skill is active).
skill1.name: Unleash Your Potential

skill2.description:
Huang Zhong places a landmine at the target location that grants him vision around it. The landmine deals 360 (360 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies that come into contact with it, while also granting him vision of them for 3s. The landmine slows heroes by 25% and inflicts 10%-20% Sunder for 2s (value scales with skill level). At the same time, he gains a shield that negates 360 (360 + 5.5% extra Health) damage for 3s. While not in Turret Mode, he gains increased skill use speed if there are enemies within range.
Up to 2 landmines can exist at the same time.
skill2.name: Lay the Mines

skill3.description:
Huang Zhong dashes for a certain distance and deploys a turret. For the next 15s, he is immobile and gains 200 physical defense and 200 magical defense. Each of his Basic Attacks deals 350 physical damage to enemies at the center (40% less to enemies on the edge). He returns to his normal mode after 5-9 Basic Attacks (number scales with skill level). Damage to towers is reduced by 50%.
Passive: When he enters Turret Mode, the Cooldown of Unleash Your Potential will be refreshed.
Using the skill again allows him to exit Turret Mode.
skill3.name: Bring out the Artillery

strategy.earlyGame: Huang Zhong is a hyper-late-game marksman who farms up in the farm lane. Until level 4, don't force trades — just collect last hits, because his turret only hits like a truck once crit items come online. Gank protection is entirely Skill 2's job: drop a mine in the river bush and you get 3 seconds of vision, a slow, and a shield all in one cast. Whenever the enemy jungler is missing from the map, hold your mines for defense instead of poke.
strategy.midGame: Start rotating to your team around the 10-minute mark, once two crit cores are finished. The turret deals 50% less damage to towers, so during sieges the right call is shooting the heroes defending it, not the building. Shove the wave in, set up behind your teammates, and the enemy simply can't step forward while the tower chips away. Always place a Skill 2 mine on your escape route before you sit down — deploying while three or more enemies are missing from the map is suicide.
strategy.lateGame: The clumped-up fights around Shadow Tyrant and Overlord in the final minutes are where Huang Zhong takes over. In turret mode his Passive buff doubles and he gains 200 physical and magic defense, so just parking one step behind your frontline and firing melts the enemy line. The catch: you cannot move at all. If an assassin flanks you, don't get greedy — hit Skill 1 to instantly exit turret mode and retreat with the 70% speed boost. Also remember that re-entering turret mode resets Skill 1's cooldown; that detail alone changes your survival rate.
strategy.teamfight: The single most important rule: never set up where you'll be hit first. Wait until the enemy's dive skills have been burned, then deploy behind your frontline. The bombardment deals full damage at the center of its area and 40% less on the edges, so aim at the middle of the enemy clump and your damage jumps dramatically. Put mines at your own feet or in a side bush — enemies who touch them get slowed and armor-shredded while you get a shield, so one mine doubles as assassin insurance and damage support.

combos.title: Mine the Exits, Then Sit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (mines on your escape path and flank) → Skill 3 (deploy the turret; you cannot move) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: Sitting in the turret takes your movement away completely. Only two mines can exist at once, so place one on your escape path and one on your flank before you deploy. An enemy hero who trips one is slowed 25% for 2s and Sundered, and you pick up a 3s shield. Shots deal full damage at the center of the area and 40% less at the edge.

combos.title: Sit Down to Refresh Skill 1
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (70% Movement Speed to reposition) → Skill 3 (deploy the turret — Skill 1's cooldown is refreshed) → Basic Attacks → Skill 1 (instant exit plus the speed boost again)
combos.description: Entering turret mode refreshes Skill 1's cooldown outright. Spend the boost walking to the spot you want, and your exit is already back by the time you sit. If someone flanks you, don't hold the position — Skill 1 drops the turret instantly and you leave on the 70%.

strengths: Turret mode adds 200 to both defenses and doubles his Passive, turning him into a fortress
A single Skill 2 mine covers vision, a shield, armor shred, and a slow
Skill 1's 70% speed boost makes disengaging from turret mode fast
Best-in-class AoE damage among marksmen once crit items are complete
weaknesses: Completely immobile while the turret is deployed, helpless against hard CC and dives
No mobility skill; mines are his only answer to ganks
The turret deals 50% less to towers, so his solo siege power is poor
Mediocre fighting power until two core items are finished forces a patient early game

playstyle.style: A deployable-turret marksman who chooses between mobility and mounted dominance. Once planted, few heroes match his zone control — the real skill is deciding where and when to plant.
playstyle.suited: players who want the siting call to be theirs — planting the turret buys 200 of each defense at the price of every step, and knowing when to pack up is on you.

synergy.reason: Ming's link raises Kaizer's attack, so the bonus damage his passive gives on single-target hits climbs further.
Yaria's shield stacks on top of Kaizer's own Block, so he can keep pushing into the front line.

counters.reason: Mi Yue's Umbral Moon makes her immune to everything, so Kaizer's launch and slow simply do not land.
Donghuang's Forsaken Contract suppresses Kaizer, burning the enhanced window of Invincible Warrior while Kaizer cannot act.

passive.description: Kaizer's Basic Attacks and Skill 2 deal 50% more physical damage when hitting only a single enemy.
passive.name: Demon Soul

skill1.description:
Kaizer throws a blade in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hit and slowing them immensely for 1s.
The blade then ricochets between nearby enemies (hitting each enemy only once), with each hit dealing an equal amount of damage and slowing the target by 15% for 2s.
If the blade hits at least one enemy or finishes ricocheting, it returns to him, and he recovers 350 (350 + 5% extra Health) Health. This skill's Cooldown is also reduced by 30%, and he gains 15% Attack Speed and 15% Movement Speed for 3s.
skill1.name: Vortex Brand

skill2.description:
Kaizer slashes twice in the target direction, with each slash dealing 160 (160 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The second slash launches enemies for 1s. His next Basic Attack is enhanced, causing him to dash toward the target and deal 130 (130 + 35% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
Passive: After leaving combat, he gains 10 Movement Speed and recovers 1% Health and max Mana every second.
skill2.name: Blade Tempest

skill3.description: Kaizer summons his demonic suit of armor. After a 1s delay, he deals 250 (250 + 25% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and enhances himself for 8s. While enhanced, he gains 500 Health, 100 physical attack, 50 Movement Speed, and 60 Block, while also dealing 50 (50 + 16% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s.
skill3.name: Invincible Warrior

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Kaizer's trades are built around Vortex Brand. When the blade returns he heals and the skill comes back sooner, so the more often he lands it, the better each trade goes for him. Basic Attacks and Blade Tempest deal more damage when they hit only one enemy. While your opponent stands inside their minion wave, do not chase; go for them once they step away and are alone. He slowly recovers Health and Mana while out of combat, so after a trade he can often recover without backing all the way off.
strategy.midGame: After leaving lane, Kaizer's job is picking off stray enemies one at a time. Invincible Warrior's armor takes a moment to kick in, so start it in a bush or out of enemy vision before you approach. His catch is the launch on the second slash of Blade Tempest, followed by the enhanced Basic Attack's dash. When the armor runs out, he fights without the enhancement. Let targets go if you cannot finish them inside the armor window, or if their teammates are close by. Before Tyrant or Overlord, join late from a side bush instead of walking in from the front, and go for the one enemy standing alone.
strategy.teamfight: Before the fight, move to a side bush and go in once your team has drawn the enemy's attention. Put on the armor with Invincible Warrior, slow your target with Vortex Brand, then launch them with Blade Tempest and close in. Stick to one target. While the enemy stays grouped, Blade Tempest tends to hit several of them. In that phase, wear them down with Vortex Brand bouncing between them and the armor's damage to nearby enemies, and wait for them to spread out.

combos.title: Armor Up Before the Catch
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Invincible Warrior: put on the armor) → Skill 2 (Blade Tempest: second slash launches) → Basic Attack (enhanced dash) → Skill 1 (Vortex Brand: slow)
combos.description: Invincible Warrior takes a moment to kick in, so start it in a bush or somewhere the enemy cannot see you. Once it lands, launch with Blade Tempest and close in with the enhanced Basic Attack's dash before the target can back off. Vortex Brand slows the first enemy it hits immensely, which buys time to take the rest of their Health.

combos.title: Throw the Blade and Get It Back
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Vortex Brand: land it and let it return) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Blade Tempest: second slash launches) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Vortex Brand heals him and shortens its own cooldown once the blade comes back. The attack speed and Movement Speed that follow help him stack Basic Attacks, then the second slash of Blade Tempest launches the target for the enhanced Basic Attack to follow. A miss gives none of that, so get close enough that the throw is hard to dodge.

strengths: Basic Attacks and Blade Tempest deal more damage when they hit only one enemy
Landing Vortex Brand and getting the blade back gives healing, a cooldown cut and a speed boost at once
Invincible Warrior raises Health, physical attack and Movement Speed while damaging nearby enemies
Out of combat he slowly recovers Health and Mana, which helps him stay in lane
weaknesses: When Blade Tempest hits more than one enemy, his single-target bonus does not apply
When the armor ends, the enhancement goes with it and he takes return fire less well
Invincible Warrior takes a moment after the press before the enhancement lands
His only dash toward a distant target is the enhanced Basic Attack after Blade Tempest

playstyle.style: When his target stands alone, Kaizer's Basic Attacks and Blade Tempest hit harder. His ultimate, Invincible Warrior, puts on his demonic suit of armor, raising his Health and physical attack for a while and dealing magical damage to nearby enemies the whole time. Finding one isolated enemy and finishing them inside that window is what he is built for.
playstyle.suited: When his Basic Attacks or Blade Tempest hit more than one enemy, his bonus damage does not apply. The skill is in waiting for an opponent to end up alone and timing the armor for that moment. The enhancement disappears when the armor ends, so you also need an eye for whether the target can actually be finished before you commit.

synergy.reason: Liang's suppression freezes a target, giving Xuance time to charge Nightmare Hooks and land it cleanly.
Zhuangzi grants crowd control immunity, so Xuance can dive the enemy line and shrug off the stuns that follow.

counters.reason: Liu Bang teleports onto an ally and lands with a stun, cutting in before Xuance can finish the kill.
Sima Yi gains vision of nearby enemies who cast skills, so Xuance is spotted the moment he starts charging.

passive.description: Xuance's chained sickles deal an extra 59 (35% physical attack) physical damage to enemies at long range, reducing their Movement Speed by 15% while increasing his own Movement Speed by 15% for 0.75-1.5s.
passive.name: Crazed Prelude

skill1.description:
Xuance dashes in the target direction, enhancing his next Basic Attack to deal an extra 4% Health physical damage (increases by 0.05% for every 10 extra physical attack). If he has marked an enemy with his sickle, they are pulled a certain distance toward him when the dash ends.
The Movement Speed increase and slow effects of Crazed Prelude are enhanced as Flailing Sickles levels up.
skill1.name: Flailing Sickles

skill2.description:
Xuance wields his sickle, charging up to gain 30% Movement Speed and gradually increasing its range. He then throws it in the target direction, dealing 380 (380 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and immobilizing them briefly. The sickle will mark the first target hit as Hunted, and will return upon reaching its max range. Xuance deals an extra 10% damage to Hunted targets and takes 15% less damage from them.
For the duration of the mark, he can use the skill again to consume the mark and pull the target behind him, dealing 380 (380 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage (deals 50% extra damage to monsters).
Canceling the charge-up reduces the cooldown of Nightmare Hooks by 50%. If the Hunted target dies or is marked by Crimson Blur, 40% of the cooldown will be returned immediately.
skill2.name: Nightmare Hooks

skill3.description:
Xuance dashes behind a target marked by Nightmare Hooks, dealing 420 (420 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. Beyond a certain distance, he'll dash toward them instead.
If he has not marked an enemy, he will instead dash to the target's location and mark them, dealing 280 (280 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage.
He takes 50% less damage during the dash.
Passive: He gains 30% Movement Speed (diminishes over time) and 25% Attack Speed for 5s for each kill or assist, for up to 3 stacks.
He can stock 1 use of Crimson Blur every 6s, for up to 3 uses in total.
skill3.name: Crimson Blur

strategy.earlyGame: You're the jungler. The moment you hit level 2 off your first buff, start planning the opening gank — Xuance's game is decided by whether he moves one beat faster than the enemy and steals first blood. Everything revolves around Skill 2's hook, and its 50% bonus damage to monsters keeps your clear speed respectable too. One detail worth memorizing: canceling the charge partway refunds 50% of the cooldown. If the angle feels wrong, don't throw it — cancel and rotate to the next bush. The discipline to hold the hook is often worth more than a kill.
strategy.midGame: The mid game is about erasing isolated enemies one at a time. Charge Skill 2 from outside their vision (you gain 30% move speed while charging) and release the instant a sightline opens. On hit, reactivate to hurl the target behind you — deliver them straight to your team. While your Ultimate carries you through an enemy you take 50% reduced damage, so diving under towers is safer than it looks. Every kill or assist triggers the Ultimate's passive attack speed and move speed surge, which even speeds up your travel to the next victim.
strategy.lateGame: A head-on 5v5 is your worst-case scenario — even full-build Xuance is made of paper. During the standoff before Shadow Tyrant, keep orbiting the perimeter. Your cue is seeing the enemy's stuns get burned on your teammates. Then hook a chipped backliner out of their formation, throw them, and finish with the Ultimate. Xuance's real terror is the chain reaction: one kill stacks the Ultimate's passive and the snowball starts rolling. Focus entirely on taking the first pick safely and the rest falls into place on its own.
strategy.teamfight: Never, ever take the job of engaging first. Sit on the edge of the fight with Skill 2 charged, waiting for a lane to open toward their marksman or mage. When the hook lands, pull yourself in with Skill 1 and the empowered basic attack, then reactivate Skill 2 to throw them into your team's kill zone. If you miss, back off immediately and wait out the cooldown. Playing hit and miss as two completely separate game plans — that discipline is what decides Xuance's winrate.

combos.title: Hook, Pull, Toss
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (charged throw — snare + Hunted mark) → Skill 1 (dash drags the marked enemy with you + Enhanced Basic Attack) → Skill 2 (recast to spend the mark and throw them behind you) → Skill 3 (dash follow-up)
combos.description: The recast throws them behind you, so face away from your own side before you press it. While the mark holds you deal more damage to that target and take less from them, which makes a few seconds of standing and trading worth it. Spending the mark clears it, so the Skill 3 that follows latches the sickle again instead — and that latch refunds 40% of Skill 2's cooldown.

combos.title: Going In Without the Hook
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (dash to the target and latch the sickle — 50% less damage taken while moving) → Skill 1 (dash drags them along + Enhanced Basic Attack) → Skill 2 (charge)
combos.description: Against enemies you can't reliably hook, close the distance with Skill 3 first. You take half damage for the whole dash, so diving under a tower doesn't automatically end with you melting. With the sickle latched, Skill 1's dash drags them where you're going, and the latch itself returns 40% of Skill 2's cooldown.

strengths: A self-sufficient pick machine: hook, throw, and follow-up all live in one kit
Kill-and-assist stacking passive makes his snowball terrifyingly fast
50% damage reduction while the Ultimate is in motion keeps dives safe
The charge-cancel cooldown refund lets him attempt hooks again and again
weaknesses: Missing Skill 2 silences both his damage and his mobility at once
Paper-thin base durability; a single stun or hard CC deletes him
Cannot play the frontline role in a head-on teamfight
Hook accuracy takes practice, so results swing wildly before mastery

playstyle.style: An assassin built entirely around his chain-sickle: hook one target, bind them, and never let go. When the hook lands the kill is nearly scripted; when it misses he has little else.
playstyle.suited: skillshot players ready to stake a fight on one throw — a landed hook hands you the chase and the kill, a miss takes your damage and your mobility with it.

synergy.reason: Mozi's barrier stuns enemies over and over, so Shouyue can finish his long aim before firing.
Lian Po's Tremor Smash slows and then launches enemies, giving Shouyue time to complete his aim and land Wild Wind.

counters.reason: Consort Yu turns immune to physical damage with Protecting Winds, so Shouyue's snipe and basic attacks do nothing.
Liu Bang's Battlefield Command shields the exact target Shouyue is aiming at, so the snipe lands into a shield.

passive.description:
Shouyue gains 1 stack of Ambush for every 1.5s he is out of combat, for up to 5 stacks. When he has Ambush stacks, he gains 20% Physical Pierce and 70-140 (+ 15% extra physical attack) physical damage. Every Basic Attack hit on enemy heroes consumes 1 stack of Ambush, while every skill hit consumes 5 stacks.
Accuracy: For every 1% Critical Rate, he deals 4 extra damage with Wild Wind and 2 extra damage with Getaway.
passive.name: Accuracy

skill1.description:
Places a scouting device that provides vision within a range of 600-1,000 for 300s. He stocks 1 device every 35s, for up to 3 devices. Devices become ineffective when occupied by enemy heroes, and they become ineffective more quickly when occupied by multiple enemy heroes.
Passive: When out of combat and near natural terrain or a scouting device, he disguises himself, gaining 15% Movement Speed and 15% Attack Speed. After losing his disguise, the Attack Speed boost will remain in effect for 3s.
skill1.name: The Tranquil Eye

skill2.description:
Takes aim and snipes in the target direction, dealing 750 (750 + 250% extra physical attack) physical damage to targets hit, plus extra physical damage equal to 8% of the target's Health while slowing them immensely for 0.5s.
Aiming takes 2s, and bullets fired before the full duration have reduced accuracy. Up to 3 bullets can be stocked at a time. Landing a Basic Attack hit reduces the time taken to aim by 4%.
Wild Wind: When his Attack Speed is increased by 40%/80%/120%/160%, his aim time is reduced by 0.25/0.5/0.75/1s. The time taken for him to exit the aiming state is also reduced.
skill2.name: Wild Wind

skill3.description:
Leaps backward and fires in the target direction, dealing 750 (750 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies in the path by 15% for 2s. Upon landing, gains 15% Movement Speed for 2s. Bullets stocked are shared with Wild Wind, and 1 bullet is used with each skill use.
Using Basic Attacks or skills removes the Movement Speed boost instantly.
Passive: Increases Basic Attack range by 15 with every skill level upgrade.
skill3.name: Getaway

strategy.earlyGame: In the farm lane, Shouyue starts by getting used to standing next to walls and bushes. Near terrain and out of combat he becomes disguised and gains movement and attack speed. Wild Wind is how he wins the lane; each shot is heavy, so catching the opponent as they step up for a last hit can send them back with very few shots. Bullets come back over time, so don't fire them all, and while the enemy jungler is out of sight keep one for Getaway.
strategy.midGame: Once he spends more time away from lane, place The Tranquil Eye devices ahead of time in the bushes and river paths the enemy is likely to use. Devices last a long time, so it is worth refreshing them before your team starts moving. On offense, snipe the enemies defending a tower until they back off, then move on the tower with your team. Ambush builds while he is not attacking and is spent all at once on a skill hit, so taking a breath after each shot makes the next one heavier. As critical items come together, Wild Wind and Getaway hit harder still. He rarely has a reason to step forward at any point in the game; the usual spot is backed against a wall or bush, looking for a line.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights he stands behind his own backline and snipes whoever comes into his line first. He is defenseless while aiming, so while the enemy diver still has skills up, fight with basic attacks and switch to sniping once they have used them. Prioritizing enemies your team has already wounded means more shots that send someone out of the fight.

combos.title: Hide, Build Up, Then Shoot
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (The Tranquil Eye: place a device) → wait without attacking inside its range or near terrain → Skill 2 (Wild Wind: fire once the aim settles)
combos.description: Standing in a device's range or near terrain without attacking disguises him, and his passive Ambush stacks build at the same time. A skill hit on an enemy hero spends the stacks all at once, so the time spent waiting before a snipe becomes the weight of that shot. Firing before the aim settles can send the bullet off line, so once you decide to wait, wait it out.

combos.title: Leap Back and Return Fire
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Getaway: leap back while shooting) → open the gap with the landing speed boost → Skill 2 (snipe with a remaining bullet)
combos.description: When someone dives you, Getaway jumps you backward and fires on the way out, leaving a slow. The speed boost after landing ends the moment you use a basic attack or a skill, so decide before the leap whether you are leaving or trading. The leap shares ammo with Wild Wind, so if you have spent every bullet on snipes, you cannot leap.

strengths: Each Wild Wind snipe adds damage based on the target's max HP
The Tranquil Eye devices let him set up his own vision
Near terrain or inside a device's range he becomes disguised, hiding where he is
The more Critical Rate he builds, the harder Wild Wind and Getaway hit
weaknesses: The aim takes time to settle, leaving a big opening in close-range trades
His only escape is Getaway's backward leap, so repeated dives are hard to survive
A run of missed snipes drops his damage sharply
Long gaps between shots make drawn-out brawls a poor fit

playstyle.style: Shouyue is a marksman who wears enemies down with long-range snipes.
