Ambush stacks build while he holds fire and are spent all at once when a snipe lands, so he wins on the weight of each shot rather than the number of them. The Tranquil Eye devices let him set up his own vision, so he can prepare sightlines from places the enemy cannot see.
playstyle.suited: A snipe fired before the aim settles can stray, so what matters is whether you can wait that extra beat before shooting. If you would rather watch the route enemies take and shoot them as they arrive than scramble to aim once a fight breaks out, he will feel natural. He dislikes close-range brawls, so players who like to step forward will find him frustrating.

synergy.reason: Liu Shan can spin and stun at once, holding enemies still long enough for Yixing's board to close.
Nakoruru flies in over terrain and drops her charge on whoever Yixing's board has locked in.

counters.reason: Han Xin gains crowd control immunity during The Unrivaled Spear, so Yixing's launch simply does not land.
Diaochan's blink shortens its own cooldown, so she slips away from the stones Yixing lays down.

passive.description:
Yixing's Basic Attacks deal magical damage, and skill hits apply 1 stack of Anti-Qi. At 4 stacks, a Weiqi stone is summoned below the enemy, dealing 100 (100 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. This Weiqi stone is then pulled to the center of Skill 2's Weiqi formation, dealing 170 (170 + 11% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. He gains 1 permanent Weiqi stone every time Anti-Qi marks are triggered, as well as 5 Weiqi stones every 60s and whenever he scores a kill or assist. Each permanent Weiqi stone grants 1 magical attack.
When taking fatal damage, he enters the void, summoning a Weiqi stone below his feet while gaining immunity to all damage and 30% Movement Speed for 1s. This effect has a cooldown of 150s.
When Weiqi stones summoned by Anti-Qi marks hit an enemy multiple times within a short duration, subsequent hits deal only 50% damage.
passive.name: Maintaining Initiative

skill1.description:
Places a Weiqi stone at the target location, gaining vision around it for 3s, dealing 100 (100 + 18% magical attack) magical damage, and reducing Taking Liberties' cooldown by 0.5s. The Weiqi stone lasts for 12s, and if a Weiqi formation is created, it will be pulled toward its center, dealing 180 (180 + 36% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path while slowing them by 25% for 1s. Hitting an enemy in this way will enhance his Basic Attack to deal 223 (120 + 60% physical attack + 18% magical attack) magical damage.
At 50/110/181 permanent Weiqi Stones, he gains an extra one-off skill that further improves his enhanced Basic Attack and grants a burst of Movement Speed for 5s. The enhanced Basic Attack improvements are a scattershot effect/17% damage boost/34% damage boost.
He stocks 1 Weiqi stone every 6s, for up to 2 stones. If an enemy is hit by multiple Weiqi stones being pulled to the Weiqi formation within 0.5s, subsequent hits only deal 50% of the initial damage. On-hit effects of enhanced Basic Attacks are reduced to 30%.
skill1.name: Sliding Stones

skill2.description:
Yixing deals 160 (160 + 25% magical attack) magical damage in the target area, which expands into a Weiqi formation. Enemies within the central area take 160 (160 + 25% magical attack) extra magical damage and are pulled toward the center of the formation.
The Weiqi formation lasts 10s. If Yixing passes through the formation's edge, he gains a 50% Movement Speed increase that diminishes over 1s, while enemy heroes that do so gain a stack of Anti-Qi. Each effect can only be triggered once. If Yixing moves too far away from the formation, it disappears.
This skill deals 180% more damage to non-hero units.
skill2.name: Taking Liberties

skill3.description:
Yixing's position becomes the corner of a void Weiqi board. After 1.5s, the board takes shape and launches enemies within it for 0.5s. The Weiqi board lasts for 4s, during which enemy heroes cannot leave it. The board adds 3 Anti-Qi marks to enemy heroes over time and exposes their location. If he successfully traps an enemy hero, he gains 1 charge of Sliding Stones.
The smaller the Weiqi board, the shorter the cooldown, for a maximum reduction of 25%.
When the Weiqi board is fully formed, Yixing gains 30-70% Movement Speed that diminishes over time.
skill3.name: The World is My Board

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Yixing starts by clearing waves with Taking Liberties. It deals much more damage to non-hero units, so laying the formation over minions finishes the wave quickly. Use the spare time to show up at the river, and placing a Sliding Stones stone in a bush on the enemy jungle side gives brief vision. He is fragile, but fatal damage makes him briefly immune to damage and faster, so stay calm and back off when ganked. That immunity has a long cooldown, so he cannot rely on it twice in a row.
strategy.midGame: Until he learns The World is My Board, the order of stones and formation decides his damage. Place a stone with Sliding Stones first, then lay Taking Liberties over it, and the stones in the formation slide to the center and cut through enemies in their path. Every skill hit applies a mark, and triggered marks, kills and assists add Weiqi stones, so the number of hits turns directly into magical attack growth. Once he has his ultimate, fights over Tyrant and Overlord are where he shines. The board takes a moment to form, so drop it while enemies are hitting an objective or right after your team's crowd control lands. Trapped enemy heroes keep gaining marks and have their location exposed.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, stand at the back and place Sliding Stones stones where enemies are likely to walk. When they push in, lay Taking Liberties over them and break their formation with the pull and the stones' path damage. The World is My Board's cooldown is shorter the smaller the board, so cycling small boards that trap just a few enemies is one option. If he wants to catch several enemies with a large board, he waits until they are clumped and cannot back off. When he is dived, drawing a small board with his own position as the corner launches and holds the attacker.

combos.title: Place Stones, Then Lay the Formation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Sliding Stones: place a stone in the enemy's path) → Skill 2 (Taking Liberties: formation pulls enemies and stones to the center) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: Stones inside the formation are pulled to its center, damaging and slowing enemies in their path. A stone hitting an enemy enhances his basic attack, so keep attacking after the pull. Each Sliding Stones cast also shortens Taking Liberties' cooldown.

combos.title: Trap Them on the Board and Pop the Marks
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Taking Liberties: lay the formation) → Skill 3 (The World is My Board: launch and trap) → Skill 1 (Sliding Stones: place a stone inside the formation)
combos.description: The board adds Anti-Qi marks to trapped enemy heroes over time, and once the marks are complete a stone is summoned below them. With a formation already laid, that stone also slides to the center and hits enemies in its path. Trapping an enemy hero gives him a charge of Sliding Stones, so he can add one more stone to finish.

strengths: Enemy heroes trapped on The World is My Board's board cannot leave until it disappears
Magical attack rises as his Weiqi stones accumulate, so his damage grows as the game goes on
Taking Liberties deals heavy damage to non-hero units, clearing waves and monsters quickly
When taking fatal damage he briefly ignores all damage and speeds up, leaving him a way out
weaknesses: Before his stones and formation are set up, his burst is low
The World is My Board takes a moment to form, and enemies who leave the area before then avoid it
No dash or blink skill, so he struggles to escape when assassins target him
Lining up stone placement with the formation takes practice

playstyle.style: Yixing is a mage who places Weiqi stones, pulls them in with his formation, and traps enemies on his ultimate's board. Each skill hit applies an Anti-Qi mark, and four marks summon a Weiqi stone below the enemy that deals damage. His permanent Weiqi stones keep growing from triggered marks, kills and assists, and each one grants magical attack.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who can stick to the order of placing stones first and then laying the formation over them. Stones outside the formation are not pulled in, so what decides it is whether you enjoy thinking about where each stone goes. His ultimate's board takes a moment to form, so players who can wait for a moment when enemies cannot back off will land it more often.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's Time Flux speeds up nearby allies, letting Menki close in before his own shield expires.
Zhang Fei leaps in and shields nearby allies, so Menki can stack that on his own and stay in the fray.

counters.reason: Sima Yi feeds on nearby skill casts, and Menki must keep casting to hold his Mass.
Zhuangzi cycles through crowd control immunity, so Menki's roam-ending launch often does nothing at all.

passive.description:
Menki gains Mass when he uses skills. For every 10 Mass, he gains 6 physical attack, 8 Physical Defense and 8 Magical Defense.
He loses 5 Mass per second while in combat, and 15 Mass per second when out of combat.
passive.name: Dream-eating

skill1.description:
Menki uses Dream Power to gain a shield that negates 431 (175 + 150% physical attack) damage for 4s, while also dealing 371 (260 + 65% physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and increasing his Mass by 30.
This skill's Cooldown is reduced by 0.5s every time he hits an enemy with his Basic Attack.
skill1.name: Lingering Dream

skill2.description:
Menki throws a Dream Bubble in the target direction and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
After reaching its max range, the Dream Bubble returns to him.
Upon catching the Dream Bubble, he throws it again at a nearby enemy, and it returns to him after it reaches its max range.
The Dream Bubble deals 130 (130 + 25% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and places 1 stacks of slow on them for 2s, for up to 4 stacks. The slow effect is dependent on Menki's physical attack.
After retrieving the Dream Bubble a second time, he gains 30 Mass and the bubble turns into a Dream Bubble. He can throw the Dream Bubble in a target direction to deal 100 (100 + 24% magical attack)-550 (550 + 132% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range of its explosion.
The longer the Dream Bubble flies, the higher the damage of the Dream Bubble, with maximum damage dealt at 5.5s of flight time.
skill2.name: Dream Bubble

skill3.description: Menki performs a dream roam, dealing 201 (150 + 30% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path while continuously gaining Mass. He briefly gains crowd control immunity at the start of the dream roam. Using the skill again stops the roam immediately, dealing 201 (150 + 30% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and launching them for 0.75s.
skill3.name: Dream Roam

strategy.earlyGame: Menki is a clash lane fighter who brawls while banking Mass. Every skill cast adds Mass, and each 10 points grants +6 physical attack and +8 to both defenses, so the golden rule is cycling skills to charge up before you commit. It drains 5 per second while in combat, so the longer a brawl drags, the more you fizzle — keep that in mind. Open trades behind Skill 1's shield: every basic attack shaves 0.5 seconds off its cooldown, so as long as you keep swinging, you can keep re-shielding. Lane opponents hate it.
strategy.midGame: Skill 2 carries your mid-game damage. The bubble flies out and returns, then launches at a nearby enemy and returns again — after two retrievals it becomes the Dream Bubble, which at 5.5 seconds of flight time detonates for up to 550 plus 132% magic attack. In a 1v1, stack the bubble's slows while punching, then slam the grown bomb onto their escape path. Push the side lane, and when a river fight breaks out, join with your Ultimate's roam. The crowd control immunity at activation lets you start the rotation straight through enemy CC — quietly one of his best tools.
strategy.lateGame: Your late game changes faces with your build: physical items make you a backline diver, defensive items make you a frontline wrecking ball. Either way, cycle skills on jungle camps and minions to top off your Mass before joining any fight. Entering at zero Mass versus full Mass is a difference of dozens of points of attack and both defenses — literally a different hero. At Overlord standoffs, your job is arriving from an unexpected angle with the Ultimate and splitting their formation with its ending knockup.
strategy.teamfight: Enter deliberately. First, send Skill 2 bubbles through their line to spread slows while the bomb grows. Once your team commits, roam to their backline with the Ultimate and time the reactivation knockup right under their marksman's feet. The instant you land, press Skill 1 — shield plus 30 Mass in one cast — then cycle basic attacks to reset it and squat in their backline through a second and third shield. Overstaying until your Mass runs dry makes you crumble fast, so the moment it starts dropping, back out and recharge.

combos.title: Grow the Bomb, Bank the Mass
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (throw the bubble — it makes both round trips on its own) → Skill 1 (shield + 30 Mass) → the second catch turns it into the Dream Bubble (+30 Mass) → throw the Dream Bubble
combos.description: The bubble flies out and comes back by itself, and the second catch turns it into the Dream Bubble. Skill 2 is a single press. Mass bleeds 15 per second out of combat, so run this right before you engage; slotting Skill 1 into the wait banks 30 Mass on top of the 30 from the catch, and the bomb peaks at 5.5s of flight time.

combos.title: Roam In, Stop on the Carry
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (roam in — brief crowd control immunity at the start) → Skill 3 again (end the roam instantly: damage + a 0.75s launch) → Skill 1 (shield + 30 Mass) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: The crowd control immunity lasts only a moment at the start of the roam, not for the whole trip. Treat it as a way through one piece of enemy crowd control and end the roam standing on their marksman. The closing launch is only 0.75s, so press Skill 1 the instant it connects for the shield and 30 Mass.

strengths: His stats at full Mass rank among the best of any fighter in the game
A fully grown Dream Bubble detonates for up to 550 plus 132% magic attack
Skill 1's shield recycles constantly thanks to basic-attack cooldown reduction
Crowd control immunity on the Ultimate makes rotations and backline dives reliable
weaknesses: Fighting at zero Mass leaves both his damage and durability below average
Mass drains every second in combat, so long fights taper off badly
The bomb needs travel time to grow, so he has no instant burst on demand
The Ultimate's crowd control immunity only covers the start; CC catches him mid-roam

playstyle.style: A fighter who stacks mass through skills, literally growing heavier and tougher. Manage the bubble's round trip and your mass economy, then plant your inflated self in the enemy team.
playstyle.suited: players who would rather prepare than react — every cast adds mass that raises attack and defense, and it drains every second the fight runs, so you arrive already big.

synergy.reason: Da Qiao's Eye of the Whirlpool gives Arli a way home, so she can dive in far deeper.
Sun Bin's slow holds enemies still, letting Arli chain Basic Attacks into a full set of Maple stacks.

counters.reason: Liang's suppression pins Arli in place, and her blink cannot answer it while the hold lasts.
Daji's Strike a Pose is aimed straight at its target, so Arli's Lithe Step cannot dodge the stun.

passive.description:
Arli's Basic Attacks place 1 stack of Maple on enemies for 5s, for up to 4 stacks. At max stacks, she detonates the Maples, dealing 230 (230 + 55% extra physical attack) physical damage to the target and enemies near them, and placing 1 stack of Maple on them.
If she uses an active skill, she can use it again within 4s to teleport to the parasol's location and retrieve it. Otherwise, she will automatically retrieve the parasol after 4s. When she isn't holding her parasol, she gains 30-60 Movement Speed and 10-20% Attack Speed (increases with level).
Every time she uses a skill or retrieves her parasol, her next Basic Attack will be enhanced, launching an extra Basic Attack that deals 53 (20 + 20% physical attack) physical damage. She can stock up to 2 enhanced Basic Attacks.
passive.name: Falling Leaves

skill1.description:
Arli blinks in the target direction.
If she is carrying her parasol, she will leave it behind at the location she blinked from.
skill1.name: Lithe Step

skill2.description:
Arli attacks nearby enemies twice, each attack dealing 300 (300 + 72% extra physical attack) magical damage. Using the skill also knocks down nearby enemy projectiles.
If she is holding her parasol, it will fly in a circle around the location where she used the skill.
skill2.name: Maple Dance

skill3.description:
Arli deals 400 (400 + 90% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in the target direction and knocks them back.
If she is holding her parasol, she will throw it in the same direction. Upon reaching a certain distance, the parasol will continue to fly at a slower pace.
skill3.name: Autumn Storm

strategy.earlyGame: In the farm lane, Arli works on the rhythm of leaving her parasol with a skill and returning to it with a recast from the start. Step in with Lithe Step, mark the opponent with an enhanced attack, and recast to return before they can hit back. Repeating this makes it hard for the opponent to focus on last hits. Her damage is low until her first offensive item, so don't overextend. Marks detonate at four, so aiming for four over two round trips, rather than greedily more, is about right.
strategy.midGame: As her offensive items come together, she starts to shine in river skirmishes. Her trump card is Maple Dance's projectile knockdown; the moment it is cast, it removes nearby enemy projectiles, so she can trade while canceling enemy marksman attacks and mage shots. It only works at the instant of casting, so save it for the enemy's big ability. In Tyrant fights, always leave the parasol on the safe side and keep stacking detonations while moving in and out to chip down even the front line. Her passive detonation was buffed in the November 5 update, so the more offensive items she builds, the harder it hits.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, keep moving and never stand still. Spread marks while changing angles with Lithe Step so the enemy cannot read her next position. When a big enemy projectile skill is coming, knock it down with Maple Dance; when a frontliner dives her, push them off with Autumn Storm and switch to shooting while retreating via the parasol recast. She is fragile and can fall to a single targeted stun, so stay on the outer edge of the fight.

combos.title: Leave the Parasol, Hit, Return
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Lithe Step: blink, leaving the parasol behind) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 1 (recast to return to the parasol)
combos.description: Lithe Step leaves the parasol where she started, and recasting it shortly after takes her back there. Both casting and retrieving the parasol enhance her next basic attack, which fires an extra shot, so marks stack quickly. Once four marks are in place they detonate, damaging the target and enemies nearby.

combos.title: Three Steps to Shake a Diver
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Autumn Storm: knock back) → Skill 1 (Lithe Step: blink at a new angle) → Skill 2 (Maple Dance: knock down incoming projectiles)
combos.description: When someone dives her, push them back with Autumn Storm first. Casting it while holding the parasol throws the parasol in the same direction, so recasting would move her toward the enemy. To escape, change the angle with Lithe Step, and time Maple Dance's projectile knockdown to incoming shots.

strengths: She can return to her parasol after skills, giving her many ways in and out
Maple Dance knocks down enemy projectiles near her
Maple detonations and enhanced basic attacks hit several enemies at once
Autumn Storm's knockback pushes off enemies who dive her
weaknesses: She is fragile and weak to targeted stuns
Misplacing the parasol can send her jumping into the enemy
Including parasol management, her inputs are busy and take time to learn
Her damage is slow to grow until her offensive items come together

playstyle.style: Arli is a marksman who fights by placing her parasol, throwing it, and teleporting back to it. Casting a skill again shortly after using it moves her to the parasol, and she gains movement speed and attack speed while it is out of her hands. Her basic attacks stack Maple marks on enemies, and four marks detonate to damage enemies around the target.
playstyle.suited: The more practice you are willing to put into placing one parasol, the further she can go. A misplaced parasol can send her teleporting into the middle of the enemy team. Simply deciding to always leave the parasol on your team's side cuts down on accidents while learning.

synergy.reason: Garo's Silent Arrow casts faster the more Attack Speed she carries, which is exactly what Time - Carefree hands her.
Arli builds her Maple stacks with Basic Attacks, so the attack boost from Time - Carefree rides into the detonation.

counters.reason: Li Bai strips his own debuffs with two of his skills, so the shred from Mastery - Glide never sticks.
Daji shreds magical defense, so she can finish Ming while he is down on the health Peace - Longevity cost him.

passive.description:
Every 5s, the next Basic Attack deals 238 (70 + 100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) magical damage and steals Health from the hit enemy, restoring 225 (225 + 40% magical attack) Health to the linked teammate and to Ming. Ming additionally recovers 4% extra Health.
Hitting a non-hero enemy unit only restores 50% Health.
passive.name: Good Omens

skill1.description:
Ming throws his instrument. If it hits a teammate, it links to them. If it misses, it automatically links to a teammate within range. The instrument increases the linked teammate's main attack stat by 20 (20 + 10% magical attack) (1 main attack stat = 1 physical attack or 2 magical attack) and their Attack Speed by 10%. If the instrument hits a teammate, increases the main attack stat boost by an extra 25% (rapidly diminishes over 4s).
Enemies who touch the link take 30 (30 + 25% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s.
Passive: Increases his physical attack by 30, magical attack by 65, and Movement Speed by 7.5%.
skill1.name: Time - Carefree

skill2.description:
Ming throws his instrument. If it hits an enemy hero, it links to them. If it misses, it automatically links to an enemy hero within range. The instrument reduces the linked enemy's physical defense and magical defense by 10%. If the instrument hits an enemy hero, it reduces their physical defense and magical defense by an extra 25% (rapidly diminishes over 4s).
Enemies who touch the link take 30 (30 + 25% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s.
Gains vision of the linked enemy.
Passive: Increases his physical defense and magical defense by 15%.
skill2.name: Mastery - Glide

skill3.description:
After channeling for 0.75s, Ming deals true damage to an enemy linked to his instrument and restores Health to a linked teammate.
If the instrument is linked to 1 target, Ming spends 600 (600 + 125% magical attack) of his own Health to deal an equal amount of true damage to the target if it's an enemy, or to restore an equal amount of Health if it's a teammate.
If the instrument is linked to 2 targets, Ming steals 600 (600 + 125% magical attack) Health from the enemy and gives it to the teammate.
If the targets die before Ming finishes channeling, 70% of the cooldown is returned. The Health spent is slowly restored over 5s.
skill3.name: Peace - Longevity

strategy.earlyGame: Open the game by linking Skill 1 to your jungler at their first buff — the attack and attack speed boost speeds up the clear — then follow your marksman to lane. Ming's link directly pumps an ally's main attack stat, so any 2v2 next to your linked partner is numerically in your favor. Play forward and push that edge. Skill 2 links to an enemy and cuts both their defenses by 10%, or an extra 25% on a direct hit. Stick it on the lane opponent right before a trade and the exact same combo from your carry chunks visibly harder.
strategy.midGame: From here on, the default is gluing yourself to your most fed teammate. Keep the link alive and weave in the Passive's empowered basic attack every 5 seconds — on hit it drains HP and heals both you and your linked ally, and that quiet little hit decides wars of attrition. Skill 2 doubles as a vision tool: if the link is still attached when an enemy ducks into a bush, their position stays lit up. Tag the enemy jungler with it before a Tyrant fight and you're moonlighting as the team's gank alarm.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, become the carry's shadow. Your Ultimate, after a 0.75-second cast, changes with your links: linked to one ally, you burn 600 plus 125% magic attack of your own HP to instantly heal them the same amount; linked to both an enemy and an ally, it drains the enemy to heal your ally with zero self-damage. Time it against the enemy's burst on your carry and it's effectively a second life. The consumed HP does trickle back over 5 seconds, but be very careful about self-damage casts while you're near death yourself.
strategy.teamfight: Lock your position half a step behind your linked ally and never open enough distance to break the link. On engage, throw Skill 2 at their ace or the assassin diving in — up to 35% defense shred means your team's focus fire suddenly goes through. The soul chain also damages enemies it touches, so deliberately placing your body so the chain drags across enemies is a real micro-play worth practicing. Hold your Ultimate through the opening exchange and heal reactively after their burst lands. Casting it early is only justified when you're certain you've read the play.

combos.title: Two Links, No Self-Cost
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (link an ally) → Skill 2 (direct hit to link an enemy) → Skill 3 (after a 0.75s channel, drain the enemy to heal the ally)
combos.description: Only with both an ally and an enemy linked does Skill 3 pull the Health out of the enemy instead of out of you. The 0.75s channel is short enough that you can start it after you see their damage turn onto your carry. If a linked target dies mid-channel, 70% of the cooldown comes straight back.

combos.title: One Link, True Damage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (direct hit — an extra 25% defense reduction) → Passive-empowered Basic Attack (drain Health back into your own bar) → Skill 3 (spend your own Health for equal true damage)
combos.description: This shape only holds while no ally is linked and the instrument carries a single enemy. A direct hit stacks an extra 25% shred on top of the 10% base at level 1, and that extra portion fades over 4s. Skill 3 then buys true damage with your own Health, so take the empowered Basic Attack first to refill. Against a non-hero unit it returns only half that Health — spend it on an enemy hero.

strengths: Skill 1's link permanently boosts one ally's offensive output
Skill 2's defense shred and vision tagging set up focus-fire kills
The Ultimate's instant burst heal acts as a second life for the carry
The Passive's drain attack heals both Ming and his linked partner at once
weaknesses: Nearly zero solo combat power or self-peel; dies instantly when isolated
Link range is limited, so highly mobile allies can leave him behind
No hard CC of his own to stop an enemy engage
The Ultimate can self-damage; a mistimed cast gets both of you killed

playstyle.style: A support who links to one ally and pours attack power into them — a carry-amplification device. He plays the supporting role completely, manufacturing his partner's prime.
playstyle.suited: support players happy to play second fiddle — one link feeds an ally attack power, the other strips enemy defenses, and the ultimate spends your own health to keep the carry up.

synergy.reason: Lapulapu launches enemies and leaves them crawling, so Pei can dash in and finish the kill uninterrupted.
Shouyue's scouting devices keep the enemy on screen, so Pei can choose exactly which fight to jump into.

counters.reason: Diaochan blinks out of range and heals off her floral marks, so a drawn-out trade only favors her.
Sun Bin heals back part of the damage taken during Time Flux, so Pei's burst simply gets refunded.

passive.name: Blast / Beastly Instincts
passive.description: While in human form, Pei's Basic Attack range is increased and each Basic Attack restores 5 Energy to him. His Basic Attack also deals an extra 20 magical damage. This extra damage can stack up to 3 times when attacking the same target within 3s.

forms.description: While in human form, Pei's Basic Attack range is increased and each Basic Attack restores 5 Energy to him. His Basic Attack also deals an extra 20 magical damage. This extra damage can stack up to 3 times when attacking the same target within 3s.
While in tiger form, Pei gains 25 physical attack, 60 physical defense, 60 magical defense, and 25 Movement Speed.

skill1.name: Striker Stance / Roaring Tiger Stance
skill1.description:
Pei fires Inner Energy in the target direction, dealing 275 (275 + 130% extra physical attack) (+ 8% of target's current Health) magical damage to enemies in its path, and slowing them by 25% for 1.5s.
Recovers 20 Energy when Skill 1 hits.

forms.description:
Pei fires Inner Energy in the target direction, dealing 275 (275 + 130% extra physical attack) (+ 8% of target's current Health) magical damage to enemies in its path, and slowing them by 25% for 1.5s.
Recovers 20 Energy when Skill 1 hits.

Pei swipes at the target, dealing 300 (300 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage. An extra 1% damage is dealt to the target for every 1% of their lost Health.
If this skill defeats the target enemy, he recovers 20 Energy.

skill2.name: Guarding Stance / Leaping Tiger Stance
skill2.description:
Pei envelops himself in Beastly Instincts, dealing 100 (100 + 70% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies while creating a shield that negates 450 (450 + 170% extra physical attack) damage and increasing his Attack Speed by 30% for 5s.
While the shield is active, he deals 20 (20 + 14% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s.

forms.description:
Pei envelops himself in Beastly Instincts, dealing 100 (100 + 70% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies while creating a shield that negates 450 (450 + 170% extra physical attack) damage and increasing his Attack Speed by 30% for 5s.
While the shield is active, he deals 20 (20 + 14% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s.

Pei pounces in the target direction, dealing 160 (160 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. If he pounces into terrain, he will latch on for 1s, during which he can pounce again by using the movement wheel, dealing 320 (320 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path.
If his pounce hits any enemy, he recovers 20 Energy and reduces Skill 2's cooldown by 30%.

skill3.name: Tiger Form / Human Form
skill3.description:
Pei switches to tiger form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next 2 Basic Attacks for 5s.
First Enhanced Basic Attack: He dashes at the target, dealing 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and inflicting them with extreme slow. After using the first enhanced Basic Attack, the duration of the second will change to 5s.
Second Enhanced Basic Attack: He deals 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range in front of him.

forms.description:
Pei switches to tiger form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next 2 Basic Attacks for 5s.
First Enhanced Basic Attack: He dashes at the target, dealing 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and inflicting them with extreme slow. After using the first enhanced Basic Attack, the duration of the second will change to 5s.
Second Enhanced Basic Attack: He deals 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range in front of him.

Pei switches to Human Form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next Basic Attack for 5s.
The enhanced Basic Attack allows him to fire a stronger Inner Energy at the target, dealing 265 (100 + 100% physical attack) magical damage to the target and enemies in a cone-shaped area behind them.

strategy.earlyGame: Pei toggles between human and tiger with an Ultimate available from level 1, giving him one of the fastest jungle starts in the game. Shred your first buff with tiger-form empowered basics, and once the second buff is down, start eyeing an invade — almost no jungler beats Pei in a straight early-game scrap. Human form has longer basic attack range, and hitting the same target within 3 seconds scales the damage up to triple the base, so finish camps in human form: the kill is faster and the energy refunds come quicker.
strategy.midGame: The gank template is a two-act play: chip in human, execute in tiger. Human form's Skill 1 deals 8% of current HP plus a slow, so even tanks feel the poke, and adding Skill 2's shield plus 30% attack speed makes you genuinely scary at range. Once the target drops below half HP, swap to tiger and pounce with the wall-crossing double dash into empowered basics. Constantly weigh the 4-minute Tyrant against the enemy's buffs — the instant you spot their jungler, steal the resources on the opposite side. Half-map control is the mid-game ideal.
strategy.lateGame: Late teamfights are an exercise in patience. Both forms stay fragile, so open every fight in human form from the very back: throw Skill 1, maintain Skill 2's shield, and kite. The only time you swap to tiger is when the enemy's CC is spent and a target below 40% HP is clearly in view. Dive, finish them with empowered basics, and even after the kill, immediately return to human form and re-establish distance. Repeating 'tiger is for executions only' like a mantra puts you at exactly the right level of caution.
strategy.teamfight: Your default is playing human form like a marksman: chip the frontline with Skill 1's percent damage, cycle your shield, and kite backward. The reason you never tiger-dive the clump is simple — the instant you transform, multiple CCs come flying. Your go signals are the enemy's stuns being spent and the backline's HP bars. When both line up, swap to Tiger Form, use a side wall for the double dash to erase their reaction time, and get into their carry's face. Secure the kill, skip the chase, and return to human-form range to rejoin the line. That whole loop is one set.

combos.title: Soften in Human, Finish as Tiger
combos.sequence: Human Form Skill 1 (8% of current Health + 1.5s slow) → Skill 3 (switch to tiger form, next 2 Basic Attacks enhanced) → Tiger Form Skill 2 (pounce; latch onto terrain for 1s and pounce again) → First Enhanced Basic Attack (dash in with an extreme slow) → Tiger Form Skill 1 (bite)
combos.description: Human form Skill 1 adds 8% of the target's current Health, so the chip damage starts there. After the swap, pounce into terrain and use the 1s latch to change your angle before pouncing again. The enhanced Basic Attacks only last 5s, so dawdling on the wall lets them expire. The closing bite gains 1% damage for every 1% of Health the target has lost, which is what fixes the order.

combos.title: Swap Back and Kite
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (return to human form, next Basic Attack enhanced) → Enhanced Basic Attack (energy blast covering the cone behind the target) → Human Form Skill 2 (shield + Attack Speed boost) → Basic Attacks while backing off → Human Form Skill 1 (slow)
combos.description: Coming out of tiger form turns your next Basic Attack into a blast. It also covers the cone behind the target, so it still catches several enemies while you give ground. Human form has the longer Basic Attack range and returns 5 Energy per hit. Stay on one target within 3s and the bonus damage builds up to triple its base.

strengths: Form swapping covers both ranged poke and melee burst in one kit
The Ultimate is available from level 1, giving elite early fighting power
Human Form Skill 1's percent damage cuts through even tanks
Tiger Form's wall dashes open up a rich menu of ambush angles
weaknesses: Both forms are fragile; teamfight focus fire melts him quickly
No hard CC of his own, so picks depend on allied lockdown
Fighting at the wrong range for his current form halves his damage
Without an early snowball, his late-game presence thins out fast

playstyle.style: An assassin who shifts between human and tiger stances — poke at range as a human, execute up close as a tiger. You are effectively piloting two kits plus an energy bar.
playstyle.suited: players who judge range fast and enjoy a stance dance — human form does the chipping, tiger form's empowered basics do the killing, and misjudging the gap costs half your damage.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one pile with The Animist and stuns them, so Force Field Suppression lands on all of them.
Liu Bang's shield and arrival heal stack onto Biron's own shield, letting him hold the front line.

counters.reason: Menki stacks Dream Bubble slows and walks away from Biron before he can catch up.
Lu Bu's enchanted halberd deals true damage that ignores defenses, so Biron's bulk counts for nothing.

passive.description:
Biron's mace accumulates charge when he lands hits with Basic Attacks or unenhanced skills.
At 30 charge or more, his mace becomes Electrified. Basic Attacks deal 40 (40 + 14% extra physical attack) physical damage and restore 70 (70 + 1.5% extra Health) Health to him. Skills also receive different enhancement effects, but hits from enhanced skills do not build up charge.
Basic Attack hits accumulate 5−10 charge, and skill hits accumulate 8−16 charge. He can stock up to 90 charge.
passive.name: Fearless Chariot

skill1.description:
Swings his weapon twice, dealing 265 (265 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage each time and restoring 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health, plus an extra 2% of lost Health.
Electrified Enhancement: Damage is increased to 400 (400 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage, and restoration is increased to 200 (200 + 2.3% extra Health) Health, plus 4% of lost Health.
skill1.name: Electrifying Charge

skill2.description:
Dashes forward, dealing 270 (270 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. The next Basic Attack after the dash is enhanced, dealing 355 (180 + 100% physical attack + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 25% for 2s.
Electrified Enhancement: If he has accumulated 30 charge or more, the enhanced Basic Attack deals 532 (270 + 150% physical attack + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. It also launches and stuns targets for 1s, then slows them by 25% for 1s.
The first enhanced Basic Attack costs 30 Energy.
skill2.name: Storm Strike

skill3.description:
Biron slams his mace into the ground, dealing 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1.5s. He also generates a shield that negates 900 (900 + 18% extra Health) damage for 6s.
Electrified Enhancement: Increases damage to 580 (580 + 195% extra physical attack) physical damage and boosts the shield to negate 1,450 (1,450 + 21% extra Health). Also generates an electric wave that deals 200 (200 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and steals 25 Movement Speed from each hero, granting it to Biron.
The range of the electric wave increases with the Ultimate's level.
skill3.name: Force Field Suppression

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Biron starts by hitting minions to build charge before he picks a fight with his opponent. With charge built, all his skills are enhanced and his basic attacks gain extra damage and healing, which helps him win trades. Charge can be stored well past what he needs, so building it while clearing the wave is better than starting just before a fight.
strategy.midGame: Once the lane is pushed, move with your jungler's plays. Before heading to the river for Tyrant or Overlord, hit minions or monsters to build charge first. The enhanced Force Field Suppression's electric wave steals Movement Speed from each enemy hero it hits, so the more enemies surround him, the faster he gets, which helps both chasing and escaping. His healing comes from Electrifying Charge and his charged basic attacks, so hit back while the shield absorbs damage to recover Health.
strategy.teamfight: Before a teamfight, build charge on nearby minions or monsters. Go in with Storm Strike, stop the enemy's advance with the enhanced attack's launch, then spread Force Field Suppression's shield and slow. Finish with Electrifying Charge to recover Health and keep holding the front. Against teams that keep their distance and stack slows, keep Flash so you always have a way to get on top of them.

combos.title: Charge Up, Then Engage
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (build charge) → Skill 2 (Storm Strike: dash) → Basic Attack (enhanced attack launches) → Skill 3 (Force Field Suppression: shield and slow) → Skill 1 (Electrifying Charge: heal)
combos.description: Build charge with basic attacks before you go in, and the basic attack after Storm Strike launches and stuns the target. While they cannot move, raise Force Field Suppression's shield and heal back with Electrifying Charge as you hit them. Enhanced skill hits build no charge, so rebuild it with basic attacks once everything is spent.

combos.title: Take Back Lost Health
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Electrifying Charge: enhanced swings) → Skill 2 (Storm Strike: get out)
combos.description: The enhanced Electrifying Charge heals more the more Health he has lost. Swing it in front of a chaser to recover, then leave with Storm Strike's dash. Without enough charge the healing is not enhanced, so check the gauge before you swing.

strengths: Once charged, all three of his skills are enhanced
The enhanced Electrifying Charge heals more the more Health he has lost
The basic attack after an enhanced Storm Strike launches and stuns the target
Force Field Suppression's shield lets him stand in front and absorb the enemy's damage
weaknesses: Without enough charge, he fights with unenhanced skills
Enhanced skill hits build no charge, so he has to rebuild it after spending it
Storm Strike's dash is his only movement skill, leaving few ways to back off
If he is slowed before he gets close, he cannot reach skill range

playstyle.style: Biron is a fighter who builds charge in his mace by landing basic attacks and skills, then spends it on enhanced skills. Once the charge reaches a certain level, his basic attacks gain extra damage and healing, and each of his three skills is enhanced. Alternating between building charge and spending it is how he fights.
playstyle.suited: If you get into the habit of checking his charge before committing, you will start most fights already enhanced. Diving in without looking at the gauge means fighting with unenhanced skills, so players who can take a breath first will find him easier. If you like standing at the center of a brawl, his shields and healing give you plenty of moments to hold on.

synergy.reason: Sun Bin's Time Flux speeds Milady into range, and his heavy slow leaves the target easy to mark with Chaos Field.
Zhang Fei's shield and knockback let Milady hold her spot until Chaos Field's mark finishes.

counters.reason: Mai Shiranui strips Milady's magical defense with KACHOUSEN, then dashes straight in on top of her.
Ziya's lingering area damage and follow-up explosion sweep away Milady's mechanical minions all at once.

passive.description:
When Milady defeats an enemy, a mechanical minion is summoned to automatically attack other enemies for 6s. At the end of their duration, minions merge with another nearby minion of the same level and upgrade themselves (up to a max of Lvl 3). If there are no suitable minions to merge with, they self-destruct, dealing 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage (explosion radius increases with minion level).
Minion Basic Attack: 120 (120 + 25% magical attack) magical damage. Health: 500 (500 + 110% magical attack).
Movement Speed: 450 (450 + 10% magical attack).
Minions deal 75% damage to structures. Merging increases Basic Attack and self-destruction damage by 30%, and max Health by 20%.
Up to 4/2/1 minion(s) can exist at the same time. Once exceeding the limit, older minions will attempt to merge or self-destruct.
passive.name: Mechanical Minions

skill1.description:
Milady commands an aircraft to fly in the target direction, attacking the enemy nearest to it multiple times along its path. Each attack deals 65 (65 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. After every two attacks, the aircraft attacks the nearest target an extra time, dealing 140 (140 + 20% magical attack) magical damage.
Using this skill again during flight splits the aircraft into two smaller aircraft. Each attacks the enemy nearest to it multiple times, dealing 65 (65 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. Enemies attacked by both aircraft have their Movement Speed reduced by 25% for 1.5s.
skill1.name: Air Superiority

skill2.description:
Milady airdrops 2 mechanical minions in the target location, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies upon landing. The mechanical minions activate after a 1s delay to search for the nearest enemy to attack.
She stocks 1 charge of this skill every 12−15s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), up to 3 charges.
skill2.name: Forced Invasion

skill3.description:
Milady fires a signal device at a target enemy or structure, marking it for 3s. Non-structure units are stunned for 0.75s. While marked, the target takes 80 (80 + 4% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s and is slowed by 15%. When the mark expires, it explodes, dealing magical damage to the target and nearby enemies, equal to 25% of the total damage taken during the mark's duration.
If the target dies while marked, immediately summons 3 mechanical minions. While the Ultimate is active, allied mechanical minions in range gain 100% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, and will rush to attack the marked target.
Can be used on structures, but does not stun them.
skill3.name: Chaos Field

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Milady starts by shoving the mechanical minions from Forced Invasion forward together with the lane minions. Forced Invasion banks charges, but spending every one of them on pushing is not recommended. With no mobility skill, mechanical minions dropped at her feet are also one of the few ways she has to hit back at someone who walks up to her. Keeping one drop in hand lets her answer anyone who closes in with mechanical minions.
strategy.midGame: Once the lane is pushed, her job moves to chipping towers. Bank Forced Invasion drops before you fire it and you can start on a tower even when the minion wave is thin. Mechanical minions deal reduced damage to towers, so if you cannot finish it, don't linger; waiting for the next wave is safer. With no way to escape, avoid walking alone into an unwarded river or the enemy jungle. The best time to hit a tower is when you see the enemy mid laner move to another lane. If they turtle, keep chipping with Air Superiority and mechanical minions and wait for them to run out of patience first.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Milady stands at the very back and keeps Forced Invasion drops coming. Recast Air Superiority to split the jet in two; enemies hit by both are slowed, which helps your team catch anyone running. When an assassin dives her, that is the other use of Chaos Field. Stun them with it, send the boosted mechanical minions after them, and use that time to walk away. If the target dies, still more mechanical minions appear, so the defensive move turns straight into a counterattack. She is not built to win head-on damage races, so she stays at the very back until she has seen the enemy diver use a skill.

combos.title: Mark the Tower
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Forced Invasion: drop mechanical minions) → Skill 3 (Chaos Field: on the tower) → Skill 1 (Air Superiority)
combos.description: Drop mechanical minions with Forced Invasion first, then fire Chaos Field at the tower. When the mark goes out, allied mechanical minions in range speed up and rush the marked target. Towers and crystals cannot be stunned, so this sequence is for damage, not for holding anything in place.

combos.title: Answering a Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Chaos Field: on the diver) → Skill 2 (drop at your feet) → Skill 1 (recast to split it in two)
combos.description: Hit a diving enemy with Chaos Field and the boosted mechanical minions rush them during the short stun. Drop Forced Invasion at your feet to add more, and split Air Superiority into two jets so that both hit for a slow. If the target dies before the mark fades, more mechanical minions appear, so turning the dive around also sets up the next fight.

strengths: Forced Invasion banks charges, so her wave pressure rarely runs dry
Chaos Field can be fired straight at enemy towers and crystals
Every takedown adds another mechanical minion, so longer fights tip the numbers her way
Casting Chaos Field speeds up nearby allied mechanical minions and sends them at the marked target
weaknesses: No mobility skill; once someone reaches her, she cannot shake them off alone
Area damage that wipes her mechanical minions at once takes most of her damage with it
Each of her own skill hits is light, so she tends to lose straight damage trades
Enemies who back off out of mechanical minion range leave her few ways to finish them

playstyle.style: Milady is a mage who pushes with numbers. Forced Invasion drops mechanical minions, and every enemy she takes down adds more. Her own skills make most sense as tools for moving the mechanical minions forward. Her ultimate, Chaos Field, can be fired at enemy towers and crystals as well as heroes, so it also finishes off a push.
playstyle.suited: She rarely has to aim and land a skill herself; most of the thinking goes into where to drop mechanical minions. Whether she suits you comes down to enjoying pushing mechanical minions and minions up together and buying time before the enemy can come to defend. With no mobility skill, a habit of stepping forward without checking where enemies are will cost you.

synergy.reason: Marco Polo's Fevered Barrage carries an attached Yaria into the enemy team, putting her Skill 2 in range.
Cirrus ignores terrain once airborne, so an attached Yaria rides over walls straight into ganks.

counters.reason: Garo's attacks deal bonus damage to shields, so the shield Yaria puts on an ally drains fast.
Gan & Mo double every sword volley onto one spot, so the ally Yaria rides takes it all alone.

passive.description: When affected by hard crowd control effects (excluding suppression effects), Yaria instantly removes all crowd control effects from herself and turns into a deer spirit for 4s. While in deer spirit form, she gains new skills, and all of her skills' cooldowns are refreshed. During this period, she cannot use Basic Attacks or be targeted, and nearby enemies are slowed by 15%. This effect has a 60−48s cooldown (depending on skill level).
passive.name: Deer Spirit

skill1.description:
Yaria directs a soul with her staff, dealing 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and knocking them back. The soul will track the nearest enemy hero after reaching its max range, dealing 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to them, launching them for 0.5s, and exposing them for 5s.
Deer Spirit Form: Deer spirit form ends instantly.
skill1.name: Wandering Beam

skill2.description:
Yaria deals 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to the 3 closest random enemies within 5s, prioritizing heroes. She cannot use Basic Attacks for the duration of the skill.
Deer Spirit Form: Leaps forward.
skill2.name: Accelerating Blitz

skill3.description:
Attaches to a teammate, granting them a shield that negates 1,000 (1,000 + 60% magical attack + 8% of target's extra Health) true damage. Attachment ends when the shield is exhausted or when leaping in the target direction to detach. She becomes untargetable and unable to use Basic Attacks while attached.
Attaching to a hero immediately reduces her active skills' cooldown by 30% and grants them these extra effects:
Skill 1: Soul tracking range increased by 20%.
Skill 2: Attack range increased by 20%.
Ultimate: Manually detaching reduces Ultimate's cooldown by 50%.
Deer Spirit Form: Slow aura's area of effect widened.
skill3.name: Verdant Protector

strategy.earlyGame: Before she has her ultimate, Yaria helps her team with poke and scouting. Accelerating Blitz hits nearby enemies on its own and prioritizes heroes, so it adds up damage without any aiming. Keep in mind she cannot use Basic Attacks while it runs. Wandering Beam's soul tracks the nearest enemy hero once it reaches max range, and the hero it hits is exposed for a while. If an enemy gank lands hard crowd control on her, she turns into a deer spirit and removes it, so she escapes the first catch.
strategy.midGame: From mid game on, Yaria's job is choosing who to attach to, again and again. Verdant Protector's shield also negates true damage, so climb onto the teammate an enemy assassin or focused fire is likely to go after, before it happens. Right after detaching she can be targeted again, so near enemies, pay attention to which way you leap. Before Tyrant or Overlord fights, wait with Verdant Protector ready so you can protect whoever gets targeted the moment the fight opens.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights Yaria stays attached and wears enemies down with Accelerating Blitz. Push back divers with Wandering Beam, which knocks back enemies in its path and launches the hero it tracks. The shield goes unused on a teammate no one is attacking, so once you spot the one the enemy is focusing, detach and switch to them. If hard crowd control lands after you step off, Deer Spirit removes it and slows enemies around her, as long as it is off cooldown. While it is on cooldown, pick a landing spot close to your team.

combos.title: Attach and Reattach
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Verdant Protector: attach to a teammate) → Skill 1 (Wandering Beam: wider tracking range) → Skill 2 (Accelerating Blitz: wider attack range) → Skill 3 (leap in a direction to detach)
combos.description: Attaching immediately shortens her active skill cooldowns, so Wandering Beam and Accelerating Blitz come back sooner. The attachment ends when the shield is exhausted, so leap off yourself once it is about to go. Detaching manually cuts Verdant Protector's cooldown a lot, which shortens the gap before the next attach.

combos.title: Recover from Deer Spirit
combos.sequence: (take hard crowd control and turn into a deer spirit) → Skill 2 (Accelerating Blitz: leap forward) → Skill 1 (Wandering Beam: end deer spirit form) → Skill 3 (Verdant Protector: attach again)
combos.description: Turning into a deer spirit removes the crowd control and refreshes her skill cooldowns. While she cannot be targeted, leap out of danger with Accelerating Blitz and end the form with Wandering Beam. Verdant Protector is ready again by the time she is back to normal, so she can climb straight back onto a teammate.

strengths: Verdant Protector's shield negates true damage and protects a targeted teammate
While attached, Yaria herself cannot be targeted
Detaching manually cuts Verdant Protector's cooldown a lot, so she can reattach quickly
Hard crowd control turns her into a deer spirit, removing it and refreshing her skill cooldowns
weaknesses: Deer Spirit has a long cooldown, so a second round of crowd control is not removed
Right after detaching she becomes targetable again
Her skills have no healing, so she has few ways to recover from steady poke
Attaching to the wrong teammate can leave the shield unused

playstyle.style: Yaria's core job is attaching to a teammate with her ultimate, Verdant Protector, and handing them a shield that negates true damage. While attached she cannot be targeted, and Wandering Beam and Accelerating Blitz reach farther. When hard crowd control hits her she turns into a deer spirit and shakes it off, so even if the enemy opens on her, she breaks free once.
playstyle.suited: She keeps deciding, mid-fight, who gets the shield and when to step off before it breaks. Her results show up less in kills than in the moments a teammate did not die. The faster you can read who is being targeted, the less of the shield goes to waste.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's camouflage covers teammates too, so Cirrus can slip into the enemy back line unseen.
Yaria attaches and hands Cirrus a true-damage shield, so he can absorb the first shot after diving in.

counters.reason: Liang's suppression also denies the cleanse on Soaring Whirlwind, leaving Cirrus with no way out.
Donghuang splits all damage taken during his suppression, so a diving Cirrus goes down with him.

passive.description:
Once Cirrus reaches level 4, he takes flight and can permanently ignore terrain. Using Basic Attacks grants Breath, which increases Movement Speed by 0-60 but drains quickly. When hitting enemies with Basic Attacks or skills, he places stacks of Lacerate on them for 2s, for up to 5 stacks. Lacerated enemies take physical damage equal to 0.24% Health when they move (increases by 0.02% for every 50 extra Physical Attack). Damage increases with stack count, for up to 10 times the initial value.
Lacerated enemies take 4.6 (2.7% physical attack) physical damage every 0.2s. Lacerated heroes only take 50% of this damage when not moving, while minions and monsters take full damage regardless of whether they are moving.
passive.name: Through the Clouds

skill1.description:
Cirrus charges up, gaining 60% Movement Speed, then dashes forward, gaining a shield that negates 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) damage. He deals 200 (200 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and stuns enemies hit for 0.5s. If he hits a hero, he can also jump back a certain distance in any direction.
Dashing will knock back non-hero units. Canceling the charge-up will return 20% of the Cooldown.
skill1.name: Cloud Descending

skill2.description: Cirrus throws wind blades, dealing 150 (150 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies twice and slowing them by 12.5% for 1s. For the next 4s, he gains 20% Attack Speed, and his Basic Attack gains increased range and unleashes 3 razor-sharp feathers. The feathers deal 34 (20% physical attack), 51 (30% physical attack), and 85 (50% physical attack) physical damage respectively, each one traveling farther than the last.
skill2.name: Razor Wind

skill3.description:
Cirrus gains 30% damage reduction for a short time and sweeps the target hero into the air, removing any crowd control effects he is under. During this time, he is untargetable and can move. Upon landing, he deals 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage, and launches the target for 0.5s.
He deals 10% more damage on landing for every stack of lacerate. The target sent flying will only take damage from Cirrus while in the air. Cirrus's Movement Speed in the air scales with his level. If there's no enemy within range as he takes flight, he'll still deal the same amount of damage upon landing.
skill3.name: Soaring Whirlwind

strategy.earlyGame: Level 4 is the first real checkpoint. That is when Cirrus takes flight, and from then on he permanently ignores terrain — there is no upkeep, so once you get there it never drops. The flip side: through level 3 he is a grounded assassin who cannot cross walls, and that stretch is his weakest. Camp clearing runs on Lacerate, the 2-second debuff (up to 5 stacks) his basic attacks and skills apply. Lacerated targets take damage every 0.2s, and minions and monsters take the full amount whether or not they are moving. Camps melt, and level 4 arrives early. Until then keep deep invades rare, since an ambush leaves you no escape route. Only touch the 4-minute Tyrant when your team can collapse on it from both sides.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 is where Cirrus comes online. Approach from over-the-wall angles that wards rarely cover. Skill 1 builds 60% Movement Speed while you hold it (level 1) and dashes forward when you release, stunning whatever it hits for 0.5s. The dash travels straight ahead — it does not swing you around behind the target, so set up the angle yourself before you commit. Only after hitting a hero can you jump a set distance in any direction. Use it to disengage, or to land on the side they are running toward. Canceling the charge-up refunds 20% of the cooldown, so pull out instead of forcing a read that has gone wrong. Basic attacks grant Breath, worth up to 60 Movement Speed, but it drains quickly. You are fast for a few seconds after swinging rather than stacking speed the longer you fight. Finish a core item by 10 minutes and farm isolated side laners to widen the lead.
strategy.lateGame: A frontal late-game collision is a death sentence for Cirrus. Wait at a flank or behind a wall, and commit to the back line only after one or two enemy CC skills have been burned. The order is Skill 1's stun into basic attacks, then Skill 2. Once the wind blades land their slow, you get 4 seconds of 20% Attack Speed with extended basic attack range and three feathers per swing. When everyone turns on you, that is Skill 3. It cuts incoming damage by 30% (level 1; 60% at level 3), clears the crowd control on you, and sweeps the target into the air. While airborne you cannot be targeted and can still move — that is the window that makes their return fire whiff, and it ends in your landing hit. Landing damage rises 10% per stack of Lacerate on the target, so how much you carved before the lift is how hard it lands. Lacerate deals percent-HP damage to enemies while they move, which means a tank trying to run bleeds the most.
strategy.teamfight: Never call the engage yourself. After your tank absorbs the opening, come in from fog straight onto the enemy marksman or mage. Stun with Skill 1 and stack Lacerate with basic attacks. If you get chased, cut their speed with Skill 2's slow and leave straight over a wall — terrain does not apply to you. Skill 3 works as a finisher or as an escape hatch. Landing damage grows 10% per stack of Lacerate, so swinging first and lifting second makes the hit land far heavier. Used defensively, the value is simply the airborne window where nothing can target you. One target at a time. Greeding for a second kill is how you never make it home.

combos.title: Lacerate-Loaded Abduction
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (12.5% slow, Lacerate) → Skill 1 (dash, 0.5s stun) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (sweep the target into the air)
combos.description: Landing damage rises 10% per stack of Lacerate, so stack first and carry second. Skill 1 grants 60% Movement Speed while charging (Lvl 1), and hitting a hero also lets him jump back in any direction. A target held in the air only takes damage from Cirrus, so your team's follow-up counts for nothing here. The 0.5s launch on landing closes it out.

combos.title: Cleanse and Exit
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (removes crowd control, take flight) → Reposition in the air → Landing (0.5s launch) → Skill 1 (charge speed to disengage)
combos.description: Casting Skill 3 removes every crowd control effect on Cirrus and keeps him untargetable while airborne. Damage taken also drops 30% for a short time (Lvl 1), which is what turns focus fire aside. Even with no enemy in range as he lifts off, the landing still deals its full damage. From there, charge Skill 1 for 60% Movement Speed (Lvl 1) and leave across the terrain his level-4 flight ignores.

strengths: Terrain-ignoring flight opens gank angles wards cannot cover
Lacerate's percent-HP damage bleeds moving targets, tanks included
Skill 3's untargetable window makes enemy burst whiff
Every basic attack grants Breath for a short burst of chase speed
weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses; eating CC first usually means dying first
Skill 1 only dashes straight forward; over-committing leaves no way back
Cannot join teamfights head-on; entry timing is unforgiving
Open ground with no walls strips away his mobility edge

playstyle.style: An assassin who gains permanent flight at level 4 and crosses terrain as if it weren't there. His power is the angle of attack — appearing from over a wall no one was watching.
playstyle.suited: junglers who read walls as doorways — flight is permanent from level 4, so a gank angle can come from over anything, and Skill 1 only ever goes forward.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one spot, so Li Xin's sword energy cuts through several of them at once.
Cai Yan's bouncing stuns open the gap Li Xin cannot make himself, and her healing keeps him up front.

counters.reason: Zhang Fei shoves Li Xin back the moment he closes, then shrugs off the trade behind a shield and invincibility.
Allain stacks damage reduction and healing with Fury, so the longer the duel runs the more Li Xin loses.

strategy.earlyGame: Li Xin enters the clash lane in Standard Form. In this form, every Basic Attack or Chaos Wave that hits an enemy hero grants him EXP. Chaos Wave reaches opponents at range and slows whoever it hits, so it doubles as wave clear and poke on your lane opponent. Its damage scales with extra physical attack, so don't force trades while your items are thin. Lightning Dash only dashes in a direction; spend it on offense and you have nothing left to back off with. Keep it in hand for when your opponent closes in.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns his awakenings, Li Xin can enter Domination Form or Revenge Form. Right after awakening his Energy is full, and from there it drains over time. Each form's passive is stronger with more Energy, so save the awakening until just before contact. When you need to absorb the front, choose Domination. It lets him hold the line in standoffs before Overlord or Tyrant. When you want to chase someone down, go Revenge. Righteous Fervor purifies slows and speeds him up while charging, so slows won't end the chase. After awakening, Force Break and Force Mastery let him move between forms without being stopped by crowd control.
strategy.teamfight: How he enters a fight depends on the form he starts in. In Domination, open with a charged Righteous Charge or Searing Edge. The charge grants crowd control immunity and damage reduction, so he can finish charging even with enemy CC flying at him. In Revenge, cast Shadow Seal first among gathered enemies and use Brutal Gouge's slow to make escaping the blast harder. In either form, swap with Force Break or Force Mastery once Energy runs low. The swap damages nearby enemies on the spot and fills the new form with a large share of Energy.

combos.title: Enter Light and Cycle Cooldowns
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Light Awakening: enter Domination Form) → Skill 1 (Righteous Charge: charge and dash) → Basic Attack (enhanced, piercing) → Skill 2 (Blade Flurry: sword energy that heals) → Basic Attack
combos.description: In Domination Form, every skill cast turns his next Basic Attack into an enhanced, piercing hit. Enhanced Basic Attacks and skill hits both shorten every cooldown, so a Basic Attack belongs between each pair of skills. Blade Flurry heals on every burst, so firing it once a trade drags on keeps him standing.

combos.title: Plant the Shadow Seal First
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Dark Awakening: enter Revenge Form) → Skill 3 (Shadow Seal: a delayed explosion) → Skill 2 (Brutal Gouge: slow and gouge) → Basic Attack (his shadow attacks too)
combos.description: Shadow Seal explodes some time after the circle appears, so plant it first and use Brutal Gouge's slow to make it harder to walk out. A gouged target takes extra damage from each Basic Attack, and if it is a hero, Li Xin also gets Health back.

strengths: Force Break and Force Mastery have no cooldown and swap forms without being interrupted by crowd control
Righteous Charge and Searing Edge grant crowd control immunity while charging, so he can push in through CC
Righteous Fervor purifies slows and restores Health while he charges
In Standard Form, every hit on an enemy hero grants EXP, which helps him get ahead in levels
weaknesses: Energy in an awakened form drains over time, so awakening too early leaves it weaker by the time the fight starts
Swapping while plenty of Energy is left gives the new form only a little
Standard Form's Chaos Wave scales with extra physical attack, so his early poke is light with few items
Each of his three forms changes his skills, so there is a lot to learn

playstyle.style: How Li Xin fights depends on which form he enters: Domination (light) or Revenge (dark). In Domination Form, extra Attack Speed turns into physical damage reduction, and his skill hits shorten his cooldowns so he can hold the front. In Revenge Form, extra physical attack turns into Attack Speed, and his shadow's extra Basic Attacks let him win on volume.
playstyle.suited: He swaps forms many times a match, so he suits players who don't mind changing how they fight based on the Energy they have left. Each form changes what his skills do, which means a lot to learn. You can start by getting comfortable with one form and add the swapping afterwards.

synergy.reason: Ming's link hands Garo Attack Speed, filling in the slower attack interval her longbow stance costs her.
Zhang Fei's shield and knockback give Garo the escape her own kit never provides.

counters.reason: Marco Polo blinks in again and again, erasing the range advantage Garo's longbow is built on.
Gao Changgong closes the gap in stealth, and his mark turns into a stun that leaves Garo pinned.

passive.description: Garo's Basic Attacks and skills deal 50% extra damage against shields.
passive.name: Piercing Arrow

skill1.description:
Garo enchants her longbow, extending her attack interval by 25% but also increasing her attack range by 125. Every Basic Attack costs 50 Mana and deals an extra 32 (32 + 7% extra physical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 2s.
This skill can be used again to cancel the enchantment, increasing her Movement Speed by 20 and restoring her attack interval and range. Every Basic Attack restores 6 (5 + 1% physical attack) Mana on hit and an extra 200% Mana when the target is an enemy hero.
skill1.name: Enchanted Arrows

skill2.description:
Garo shoots a piercing arrow in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 60% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path while silencing them for 0.5s and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
After a delay of 1s, the area the arrow passed through explodes, dealing 600 (600 + 120% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
She casts the skill faster as she gains Attack Speed. Casting speed increases by 1% for every 1.5% Attack Speed, for a maximum increase of 100%.
skill2.name: Silent Arrow

skill3.description:
Garo creates a magic circle in her current location for 8s. Using this skill again will destroy the magic circle.
When she is in the circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate. Upon destroying the magic circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate if she is inside it, or half of these bonuses if she is outside it. Creating or destroying the magic circle will deal 380 (380 + 85% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
Passive: Critical hits from her Basic Attacks reduce the target's Movement Speed by 30% for 0.5s. If her Basic Attack lands a critical hit on the same target again within 1s, the Movement Speed reduction is increased to 50%.
skill3.name: Sphere of Purity

strategy.earlyGame: Garo's longbow is not a skill you leave switched on. While it is active her range grows but her attack interval stretches and every Basic Attack costs Mana. In the farm lane, switch to it only to poke the opponent or clear a wave from a distance, and keep it put away otherwise. Landing Basic Attacks restores Mana, and hitting an enemy hero restores more. She has no mobility skill, so don't step forward while you don't know where the enemy jungler is. If someone closes in, briefly stop their skills with Silent Arrow and back off while the slow is on them.
strategy.midGame: The passive on Sphere of Purity slows enemies hit by her critical Basic Attacks. A second crit on the same target shortly after makes the slow stronger, so as her items raise her Critical Rate, enemies have a harder time reaching her while she keeps shooting. When pushing a tower, use the longbow's range and chip it from a distance. Her Basic Attacks and skills deal extra damage to shields, so if the enemy has heroes who shield, Garo can be the one who strips those shields. Walking alone away from your frontline leaves her, with no mobility skill, nowhere to run.
strategy.teamfight: As the fight starts, place the Sphere of Purity circle at your feet. Standing inside raises her Critical Rate and Movement Speed, so keep shooting whatever the longbow reaches from within it. Closing it also damages enemies in range, so catch whoever came close in it before you back away.

combos.title: Shoot From Inside the Circle
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Sphere of Purity: circle at her feet) → Skill 1 (Enchanted Arrows: switch to the longbow) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The circle stays where it is created and only helps her while she stands in it, so it goes down first once she has chosen where to shoot. Switching to the longbow afterward lets her reach distant enemies without stepping out. With her Critical Rate raised, the crit slows also land more often.

combos.title: Silence, Then Break Away
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Silent Arrow: silence and slow) → Skill 3 (Sphere of Purity: close it from inside for speed) → Skill 1 (Enchanted Arrows: cancel the longbow) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Against a diver, land Silent Arrow first to briefly stop their next skill. Closing the circle while still inside it gives her the full speed bonus, so close it before stepping out and then open the gap. Cancelling the longbow returns her attack interval to normal, so she can keep shooting back at a chaser without losing hits.

strengths: Her Basic Attacks and skills deal extra damage to enemy shields
Enchanted Arrows extends her range so she can shoot from far away
Her critical Basic Attacks slow the target, and a second crit in quick succession slows them further
Silent Arrow's silence briefly stops an enemy's skills
weaknesses: No mobility skill; once someone reaches her, slows and silence are all she has to make space
Every longbow shot costs Mana, so leaving Enchanted Arrows on drains her dry
The longbow stretches her attack interval, costing her hits in close-range trades
Sphere of Purity's bonuses apply only while she stands inside the circle, and closing it from outside gives half

playstyle.style: The more shields the enemy brings, the better Garo's arrows work. Her Basic Attacks and skills deal extra damage to shields, which makes her a reason to pick against drafts full of shield heroes. Enchanted Arrows switches her to a longbow with more range, and inside the circle from Sphere of Purity she gains Critical Rate and Movement Speed, so she picks her spot first and shoots from there.
playstyle.suited: The longbow is not left on; it goes in and out as her Mana allows. Every trade means thinking about that toggle and where the circle sits, so how easy she feels depends on whether you can keep managing both without stopping. With no mobility skill, she also asks for the patience to stay behind your frontline while shooting.

synergy.reason: Hou Yi has no movement skill and struggles to escape divers on his own. While Dunshan shelters him, Dunshan's Basic Attacks turn ranged and slow each enemy they hit as it closes in.
Allshield knocks enemies back and slows them by 25–50% for 1s, so if Wang Zhaojun drops Frigid Prison where they land, they struggle to walk out before the delayed freeze hits.

counters.reason: Garo's Basic Attacks and skills deal 50% extra damage against shields, so she strips the shields Dunshan hands out with Bastion quickly.

Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect cleanses crowd control from his teammates and makes them immune for 1.5s, undoing the stun after a Collision Course toss and blanking Allshield's knockback during that window.

passive.description:
Shield Eternal's Basic Attacks deal an extra 135 (135 + 2.7% extra Health) physical damage.
While Skill 1 is in effect, Basic Attacks deal ranged damage and slow enemies by 10% for 0.5s. Tap and hold the Basic Attack button to charge the attack, increasing Attack Range and allowing control over the attack direction.
passive.name: Moving Mountain

skill1.name: Bastion
skill1.description:
Select a teammate: Shield Eternal dashes to the target, then shelters them, granting both himself and the teammate a shield that negates 900 (900 + 18% extra Health) damage for 6s (distributed inversely proportional to both heroes' Health). The teammate controls both heroes' movement during this time (Movement Speed is 95% of the average of both heroes' Movement Speed).
Select an allied tower or any tower ruins: Shield Eternal becomes a turret for 6s. During this time, he is untargetable and recovers 125 (125 + 2.5% extra Health) Health per second, while also restoring the same amount of Health to the tower and granting it a shield that negates 600 (600 + 12% extra Health) damage. Use again to exit turret mode. Turret mode has an independent 15s cooldown.
The teammate can cancel the sheltering at any time by dismounting Shield Eternal or by using a movement skill with very long range. After 3s, Shield Eternal can also cancel it, refunding up to 50% of the cooldown based on the shelter duration.

skill2.name: Collision Course
skill2.description:
Shield Eternal charges forward (stopping if he hits an enemy hero), picking up and tossing heroes in front within range (scales with skill level) behind him for 0.5s and dealing 300 (300 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage to targets nearby. Upon landing, tossed enemies stun nearby enemies for 0.5s and deal collision damage equal to 5% of the target's Health to heroes and 177 (5% of own Health) to non-hero units.
When used during Skill 1, he will not toss enemy heroes, but instead push away enemies along his path.

skill3.name: Allshield
skill3.description: Shield Eternal slams his giant shield into the ground, gaining brief crowd control immunity. The shield deals 170 (170 + 55% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range, knocking them back and slowing them by 25% for 1s, while also dealing collision damage equal to 5% of the target's Health to heroes or 177 (5% of own Health) collision damage to non-hero units. The giant shield then travels forward, dealing equal damage, while also launching enemies in its path for 0.5s and knocking down projectiles.
