skill2.name: Shattered Illusions

skill3.description: Jing and her mirror image switch locations. Stocks 1 charge every 10s, up to 4 charges.
skill3.name: Dimensional Shift

skill4.description:
Jing flies forward, pulling enemies along her path with her. When she stops, she opens a Mirror Vortex and immobilizes the enemies at its center for 1s. She and her mirror image then move to either side of the vortex's central axis. While the vortex is present, she recovers 17 (10 + 4% physical attack) Health for every 0.05s spent dashing with Dimensional Shift. She gains 1 charge of shift if she deals damage to an enemy. The Mirror Vortex lasts 10s, during which Jing gains 10% damage reduction, but it will disappear if she leaves before then.
When the vortex is formed, 8 mirror fragments are generated along its border. When Jing or her mirror image deal damage to an enemy, the nearest mirror fragment will fly at the enemy, dealing 30 + 2% of the target's lost Health physical damage.
skill4.name: Mirror Domain

strategy.earlyGame: Jungle Jing lives or dies on understanding the mirror image. With no image on the field, casting Skill 1 or Skill 2 spawns one for 2s, and it replicates everything you do except Skill 4. Your body and the image apply two different types of mark, and when both sit on the same enemy the marks shatter. The shatter deals physical damage equal to 4% of the target's lost Health and refreshes the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2, once every 5s. Drill that reset rhythm on jungle camps first, then hit level 4 as fast as you can. For early ganks, Skill 1's dash and 1.5s slow to stop their feet, plus the mirror's overlapping damage to complete the marks, is already plenty of chip. Practicing clean reset patterns beats greedy invades.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes, with your first physical core item finished, Jing's burst puts squishy targets inside one-combo range. Hunt lone enemies in their jungle or on the side lanes: enter with Skill 1, complete the marks with the mirror, take the reset, re-dash with the refreshed Skill 1 — chain that loop and they never get a turn. Skill 2 hits everything around you and pushes your own Movement Speed up by 50%, diminishing over 1s. The heal is biggest on the first enemy struck, with each additional target adding 25% of that amount. Swing it once you are fully inside their space and you get the damage, the heal, and the speed to leave on. Before the 4-minute Tyrant and the 10-minute Shadow Tyrant, deleting the enemy support who comes for vision frees up your whole team.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Jing is the flanking blade aimed at the enemy marksman's throat. With durability that folds in a few hits, diving the front of a 5v5 unplanned is suicide, so you spend long stretches waiting. Watch which target the enemy's point-and-click crowd control gets used on, then enter with Skill 1. Skill 3, Dimensional Shift, swaps you with your mirror image and covers both extending a kill and getting out. It stocks 1 charge every 10s and caps at 4. Even with a full hand, impose one rule on yourself — always keep one for the road home — and your deaths drop. Skill 4, Mirror Domain, flies forward pulling enemies along, then opens a Mirror Vortex at the stopping point and immobilizes whoever is at its center for 1s. Inside the vortex you also take reduced damage, so the dive comes with a layer of extra durability. Getting your swap read and answered with crowd control is the number one killer, so vary your swap timing every time.
strategy.teamfight: Hold the perimeter until your tank draws the enemy's crowd control, then slide in the moment the backline's feet are exposed. Skill 1 into empowered basic attack into Skill 2 completes the marks; once they shatter and the reset lands, swap with your mirror using Skill 3 to make their counterattack whiff, then re-enter on the refreshed Skill 1 — that in-and-out loop is the ideal form. Because the shatter scales off the target's lost Health, your execution speed climbs as the brawl wears on and health bars drop. While Skill 4 is active the shatter's cooldown falls from 5s to 2s, and inside the Mirror Vortex every hit you land stocks another charge of Skill 3. Every second spent hitting a full-HP tank is wasted, so keep your eyes locked on the softest target alive.

combos.title: Double Mark Reset
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Reflective Assault — dash, spawns a mirror image for 2s) → Empowered Basic Attack (extra 50 at Lvl 1) → Skill 2 (Shattered Illusions — nearby damage, 50% Movement Speed, heals on hit) → Skill 1 again after the reset
combos.description: Jing and her image apply different mark types, and an enemy carrying both has them shatter for 4% of their lost Health. The shatter also refreshes Skill 1 and Skill 2, so the returned dash goes straight back in. It triggers once every 5s at most, or every 2s while Skill 4 is up, and the image hits harder the farther it stands from her.

combos.title: Locked in the Vortex
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Mirror Domain — fly forward pulling enemies along, then immobilize those at the center for 1s) → layer marks with Skill 1 and Skill 2 → Skill 3 (Dimensional Shift — swap places with the image)
combos.description: Skill 4 drags everyone in its path, then opens the Mirror Vortex and holds the enemies at its center for 1s. Eight mirror fragments ring the edge, and each time Jing or her image deals damage the nearest one flies in for 30 at Lvl 1 plus 2% of the target's lost Health. Inside the vortex every hit refunds a Dimensional Shift charge and damage taken drops by 10% at Lvl 1 — but the moment she steps outside, the vortex is gone.

strengths: Dual-mark cooldown resets multiply both tempo and burst
The missing-HP slash makes her a premier executioner of chipped targets
Skill 3's swap covers re-engage and escape in a single motion
On-hit healing from Skill 2 lets her brawl longer than she looks
weaknesses: Damage falls off a cliff whenever marks fail to complete
The mirror image starts at 30% of her damage — keep it hugging her and output stalls
Paper durability; a predicted swap into crowd control is a death sentence
Mirror management piles on the workload and stretches the learning curve

playstyle.style: An assassin who fights alongside her mirror image, marking targets from two directions and swapping positions mid-fight. Every swap breaks the enemy's aim — mastered, she feels uncatchable.
playstyle.suited: players who like playing against the enemy's screen — the image hits harder the farther it stands from her, and one mistimed swap costs the whole life.

synergy.reason: Dr Bian's poison pool slows whoever stands in it, so Agudo's Tumble, Furball! is much harder to dodge.
Zhang Fei's shield covers Agudo, so she can stay on the front line and keep landing Basic Attacks.

counters.reason: Han Xin still holds a second leap once Agudo has spent her only roll, leaving her no way out.
Lam's Death From Below drags Agudo in, and once she is low the Prey mark adds true damage.

passive.description:
Agudo has an affinity with the monsters of the Gorge. When she's near a monster, Recovery will be replaced with Release (grants buffs).
Upon hitting enemies, Agudo's Basic Attacks will drop Seed Mines and absorb nearby mines: She can pick up mines to gain 3% Attack Speed and Movement Speed for 2.5s, for up to 6 stacks.
Enemies that come into contact with a mine will take 30 (30 + 10% extra physical attack) physical damage.
passive.name: Mountain Encounter

skill1.description:
Agudo sows a field in the target area, creating an animal wonderland that provides Agudo and her animal companions with 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, while granting 40 (40 + 0.6% extra Health) Health. Her animal companions will come to the field and fight alongside Agudo. Animal companions' stats scale with Agudo's hero level, while the chance of summoning more companions scales with skill level.
Animal companions gain additional Attack, Attack Speed, and Critical Rate based on 50% of Agudo's stats.
skill1.name: Wild Growth

skill2.description:
Tumble, Furball!: Agudo rolls forward with Furball, gaining 40 Block and immunity to 1 hard crowd control while rolling. Also deals 240 (240 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to any enemies she hits and stuns them for (1/2s). If they hit a wall before the end of the roll, they'll ricochet up to 3 times, resetting the rolling distance while increasing the skill's effect by 25%. Agudo also enhances her next Basic Attack to shoot 3 Seed Mines and deal 65 (65 + 21% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Tumble, Agudo!: Agudo rolls forward and enhances her next Basic Attack to shoot 3 Seed Mines and deal 65 (65 + 21% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill2.name: Tumble, Furball!

skill3.description:
While riding Furball: Agudo commands Furball to leap to the target location, dealing 460 (460 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and stunning them for 2/3s. After that, Furball will battle independently while inheriting 50% of Agudo's stats and 100% of her on-hit effects.
While not riding Furball: When Furball is defeated, it will enter recovery mode. It can rejoin the battle after its Health is fully restored.
She can call Furball back before the skill duration ends.
skill3.name: Gorge Mobilization

strategy.earlyGame: Agudo is a jungle marksman whose Passive lets her vacuum camps at a speed few junglers match. Take both buffs, race to level 4, and keep collecting the seed mines your basic attacks drop to maintain the attack and movement speed stacks (max 6). Skill 2's roll negates one hard crowd control effect, so even a face-check against the enemy jungler leaves you one free escape. Her early dueling is average, though — if an invade is coming, just call teammates. When you gank, pick lanes with walls where the bounce stun can actually land.
strategy.midGame: The 4-minute Tyrant is where Agudo shines brightest. Drop Skill 1's paradise to boost your own and your companion monsters' attack and movement speed by 15%, and the pack melts the objective before a contest can even form. Mid-game skirmishes also start with Skill 1: a zone of healing and speed turns even-numbered fights lopsided. The Ultimate throws Pom-Pom for a ranged area stun, but your body is fragile once the throw is out, so only light the fuse on a brawl when your frontline is actually there.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, where you throw Pom-Pom decides the result. Toss the Ultimate at the enemy marksman's or mage's feet for the stun, let the detached Pom-Pom maul them, and run a second front with your own basic attacks from the very back. Recast to recall Pom-Pom when the damage piles up. After the throw, your body is a plucked bird — check your escape wall and your teammates' positions before committing it. If Pom-Pom dies, half your power is gone until it recovers, so skip the solo side-lane pushes and keep shooting from under your team's umbrella.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight starts before the fight: sow Skill 1's field where the fight is going to happen. The 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed and the healing land on Agudo and her animal companions only — allied heroes get nothing from it. The companions that gather there still stand in front of the enemy, so the extra bodies translate straight into board pressure. When the enemy engages, roll with Skill 2 to negate one hard crowd control while you reposition, and bounce off a wall to answer with the empowered basic attack's triple seed-mine burst. Save Skill 3's Pom-Pom toss as the finisher for the moment an enemy backliner ends up isolated. Between her summons and her own attacks she covers a wide front, so the longer a face-to-face fight drags on, the further it tilts toward Agudo.

combos.title: Wall Bounce Counter
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Tumble, Furball! while riding — negates 1 hard crowd control, grants Block, damages and stuns on contact) → bounce off a wall (skill effect +25%) → Empowered Basic Attack (3 Seed Mines)
combos.description: Rolling with Furball eats one hard crowd control on the way in. The roll carries 40 Block at Lvl 1, and hitting a wall makes her ricochet, resetting the rolling distance while raising the skill's effect by 25%. Finish with the empowered Basic Attack's three Seed Mines, since any mine left on the ground damages an enemy who touches it.

combos.title: Field First, Then the Toss
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wild Growth — 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, summons animal companions) → Skill 3 (Gorge Mobilization — leap Furball to the target location for damage and a stun) → Basic Attacks to scatter Seed Mines → Skill 3 recast (call Furball back)
combos.description: Laying the field first gives Agudo and her companions 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed plus a heal. Skill 3 then sends Furball onto the target, where the landing damages and stuns before Furball starts fighting on its own. While separated, Skill 2 becomes Tumble, Agudo! — a plain roll with no stun and no crowd control immunity. Recast to recall Furball as soon as the pressure arrives.

strengths: Companion summons plus Skill 1's buffs create numbers and board pressure
Skill 2 negates one hard crowd control and stuns off walls — great in attack or defense
The Ultimate's Pom-Pom toss is a ranged area stun you can throw from safety
Seed-mine stacks and the Passive make her jungle clear exceptionally fast
weaknesses: The body is an assassin magnet while Pom-Pom is detached
Losing Pom-Pom guts her power until it finishes recovering
Before summons and stacks come online, her early dueling is merely average

playstyle.style: The gorge's only beast-taming marksman, fighting alongside befriended monsters. Mount-and-split mechanics and a CC-blocking roll give her durability few other marksmen have.
playstyle.suited: players drawn to heroes outside the textbook: a marksman who stands in the middle of the fight, deciding on every engage whether Furball carries her or gets thrown.

synergy.reason: Luban No.7's scattershot only hits enemies caught in a straight line, and Sakeer's launch pins them in place.
Bai Qi amplifies the healing he receives, and Sakeer's fireflies always chase the lowest-Health ally, usually him.

counters.reason: Liang's circles hold vision over the brushes, so Sakeer's next hop is read before he takes it.
Wukong's Protective Shroud simply absorbs Mulberry Power, the one cast Sakeer's setup depends on.

passive.description:
Sakeer's Basic Attack deals melee damage and summons a firefly that deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage to enemies and exposes them for 3s. Sakeer also periodically restores 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health to the nearby teammate with the lowest Health.
When there are no enemies nearby, charging his Basic Attack recovers 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health. He will stop restoring Health to teammates while charging.
passive.name: Firefly Protection

skill1.description:
Sakeer channels Luminescence to the target area, dealing 500 (500 + 10% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and launching them for 1s. Luminescence is consumed on hit, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage per stack. If there are teammates nearby, Luminescence instead heals the teammate with the lowest Health, restoring 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health per stack.
Luminescence: He gains 1 stack every 1.5s, for up to 9 stacks. The skill's range increases with the number of stacks.
skill1.name: Mulberry Power

skill2.description:
Sakeer flies to the target brush, gaining 1 stack of Luminescence and releasing a number of fireflies depending on how far he flies. After 1s, the fireflies fly to the nearby hero with the lowest Health. If the hero is an enemy, the fireflies deal 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage and expose them for 3s. If the hero is a teammate, they restore 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health.
This skill stocks up to 3 charges. Tap it to fly to a brush in front of him without aiming.
skill2.name: Ride the Wind

skill3.description:
Sakeer summons an Illuminating Brush at the target location. He can use this skill again within 6s to fly to the brush and gain a stack of Luminescence.
Illuminating Brush: 1s after the brush has been summoned, it releases fireflies at up to 5 nearby heroes every second. Every firefly deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage to enemies, or restores 50 (50 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health to teammates.
Enemies that step into this brush will have their location revealed. After a while, the Illuminating Brush will stop releasing fireflies and turn into a regular brush that lasts for 30s.
skill3.name: Firefly Fields

strategy.earlyGame: Sakeer's early game starts with juggling two jobs: escorting your marksman and sweeping bushes for vision. The fireflies from your basic attacks reveal stealth, and the Passive automatically heals the lowest-HP ally near you, so standing in the right spot alone stabilizes the lane. Skill 2 holds 3 charges — assign roles up front (one for river scouting, one for escape, one for gank follow-up) and your death count drops. Firefly Power builds 1 stack every 1.5 seconds, and Skill 1's radius and healing scale with stacks, so the patience to sit on them until the moment you fire is itself a form of power.
strategy.midGame: Once you learn the Ultimate, plant the glowing bush at the entrance to the battlefield before the 4-minute Tyrant and mid-game skirmishes. Fireflies launch every second — damaging enemies, healing allies — and you gain vision of any enemy who steps inside, so the side that placed it fights on terrain that wins both numbers and information. For gank follow-up, fly ahead with Skill 2 to a bush along the enemy's escape route and place Skill 1's knock-up on their exit — a brutal trap. At 9 stacks, Skill 1's radius is a different animal, so burn its maximum size into your muscle memory to sharpen your interceptions.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Sakeer stands half a step behind the carry, focused on one thing: delivering the 1-second knock-up at the perfect moment. The instant an enemy assassin or fighter touches your backline, launch them with a fully stacked Skill 1 and cut the follow-up cold — that single play swings teamfights directly. Firefly healing flies to the lowest-HP ally automatically, so as long as your own position is right, the support never stops. Against stealth heroes, your fireflies' true sight is close to a unique answer — build the habit of pre-firing a basic attack into any suspicious bush.
strategy.teamfight: Whether the glowing bush is placed before a teamfight nearly doubles Sakeer's contribution. After setting it, fly with Skill 2 to a bush near your backline and bank Firefly Power while you wait for the engage. Answer enemy dives with Skill 1's knock-up, and let the automatic firefly healing raise your whole team's HP floor through the brawl. Your personal damage is low, so there's no need to chase or step forward. Accept that not dying converts directly into healing output, and keep moving bush to bush, always one step outside the enemy's reach.

combos.title: Bank, Then Intercept
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Ride the Wind — fly to a brush and gain 1 stack of Luminescence) → Skill 1 (Mulberry Power — launches enemies in the area for 1s)
combos.description: Skill 1 launches everyone in the area for 1s and spends Luminescence for an extra 100 magical damage per stack. With teammates nearby, those same stacks instead restore 50 Health to the lowest-Health ally. Stacks build one every 1.5s up to nine, and the more you hold, the wider the area gets — so fly to a brush with Skill 2 right before you fire.

combos.title: Holding the Lit Brush
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Firefly Fields — summon an Illuminating Brush at the target location) → recast Skill 3 within 6s (fly to it and gain 1 stack of Luminescence) → Skill 1 (1s launch)
combos.description: One second after it appears, the brush sends fireflies at up to five nearby heroes every second. Enemies take 100 magical damage, teammates get 50 Health, and anyone who steps into the brush has their location revealed. Recasting within 6s carries Sakeer there himself. From that ground, hold Skill 1's launch and deny the entrance.

strengths: Healing, a knock-up, vision, and stealth detection packed into one support kit
Bush-hopping through Skill 2 and the Ultimate gives him rare mobility for the role
The glowing bush dominates space and scouts around objectives
Fireflies auto-target the lowest-HP ally, so the support never misses
weaknesses: Skill 1 stays thin until Firefly Power builds, so he cannot spam it
Open terrain without bushes cuts his mobility and scouting in half
Low personal damage and no answer to chained hard crowd control
Healing dies when separated from allies — solo play is not an option

playstyle.style: A forest-keeper who grows his own bushes and sends fireflies to scout and heal. He is the only hero who adds terrain to the map, monopolizing the economy of hiding places.
playstyle.suited: anyone who wants to win the vision war — planting bushes where the map has none, hopping between them, and leaving the healing to the fireflies.

synergy.reason: Mai Shiranui's launch freezes enemies in place, letting Charlotte's enhanced Basic Attack land in full.
Guiguzi pulls enemies into one stunned clump, so Charlotte's Power Gradation catches several of them at once.

counters.reason: Arthur's silence breaks the Follow-Up chain Charlotte relies on, and her own slow only speeds his healing.
Arli's Autumn Storm knocks Charlotte away, cutting short the close-range pressure Charlotte needs to build.

passive.name: SPLASH GRADATION
passive.description:
All of Charlotte's skills are considered Initial Skills. When any of her skills hit, the next different skill she uses will be enhanced to a Follow-Up Skill and she will gain 1 mark for 4s, for up to 5 stacks.
Upon reaching 3 stacks, her next Basic Attack is enhanced into the Follow-Up Skill SPLASH GRADATION, where she dashes toward the target and strikes 7 times, each strike dealing 121 (80 + 25% physical attack) physical damage while also slowing the enemy by 10%. The final strike deals extra physical damage equal to 12% of the target's lost Health. While launching an enhanced Basic Attack, she gains 21%-35% damage reduction.
Follow-Up Skills place 1 stack of Maim on enemies hit, reducing the enemy's Attack Speed by 10%-20% for 4s, for up to 2 stacks. Enemies lose 1 stack of Maim every time they use a Basic Attack.

skill1.name: TRI-SLASH

forms.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a short delay, deals 366 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

Follow-up Skill: Charlotte quickly unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a delay that's shorter than that of the Initial Skill, deals 475 (260 + 130% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

skill1.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a short delay, deals 366 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

skill2.name: SPLASH FOUNT

forms.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte dashes in the target direction and quickly strikes 6 times, each strike dealing 69 (45 + 15% physical attack) physical damage and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health.

Follow-up Skill: Charlotte dashes in the target direction and quickly strikes 6 times, each strike dealing 69 (45 + 15% physical attack) physical damage and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health. Cooldown is shorter than that of the Initial Skill.

skill3.name: POWER GRADATION

When the same target is hit multiple times, subsequent hits only deal 30% damage.

Subsequent hits on the same target deal only 30% damage.
When the star forms, she unleashes POWER GRADATION, striking enemies at the center for equal damage and launching them for 0.75s. While active, she gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction.

skill3.description:
Initial Skill: Charlotte carves a seven-pointed star where she stands, dealing damage to nearby enemies up to 3 times, each dealing 320 (320 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s. While the skill is active, she gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction.
When the same target is hit multiple times, subsequent hits only deal 30% damage.

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Charlotte sticks to hitting and leaving until she has her ultimate. TRI-SLASH speeds her up when it lands, so cast it early as a placed skill, close the gap the moment it connects, then chip with SPLASH FOUNT while healing and back off. Marks fade after a short time, so hold back from half-hearted trades that cannot reach the third. Committing deeply only when the opponent misses a skill cuts down on early deaths.
strategy.midGame: After leaving lane, push side waves to draw out enemy fighters and start one-on-ones. The key moment is the enhanced attack from three marks: seven dashing strikes, a final strike that grows with lost Health, and reduced damage taken while it lasts, so she gets stronger in head-on brawls. Her enhanced skills' Attack Speed reduction hits basic attackers hardest, so a side lane where the enemy marksman has retreated is a good hunting ground. Join Tyrant fights a little late from the side, building marks with skills on the edge before committing.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, she goes in second. Once the enemy's attention and crowd control are drawn by your engage, enter with SPLASH FOUNT, reduce incoming damage with POWER GRADATION while completing her marks, then unleash the seven strikes. POWER GRADATION works best cast a little late, timed after seeing the enemy's stun animation; cast too early, it does far less. Even when no kills are available, keeping the Attack Speed reduction on the enemy marksman lowers the damage your front line takes. If the enemy builds anti-healing, SPLASH FOUNT's healing shrinks, so check their items each time.

combos.title: Three Marks Into Seven Strikes
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (TRI-SLASH: initial skill) → Skill 2 (SPLASH FOUNT: enhanced, heals while striking) → Skill 3 (POWER GRADATION: enhanced, launches the enemy at the center) → Basic Attack (seven-strike enhanced attack)
combos.description: Each skill hit adds a mark and enhances the next different skill she uses. The enhanced POWER GRADATION launches the enemy at the center once the star is complete. Stack the seven strikes unlocked by three marks on top of that, and the final strike grows sharply with the target's lost Health.

combos.title: Hit and Leave With the Speed Boost
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (TRI-SLASH: land it for speed) → Skill 2 (SPLASH FOUNT: enhanced, heals while striking) → back off
combos.description: Landing TRI-SLASH speeds her up, and she uses that momentum to step in. Strike with the enhanced SPLASH FOUNT to restore Health, then pull back. The enhanced SPLASH FOUNT also has a shorter cooldown, so she can start the next trade quickly.

strengths: Three marks unlock a seven-strike enhanced attack whose final strike grows with lost Health
Enhanced skills lower the Attack Speed of enemies hit, which is strong against basic attackers
SPLASH FOUNT's healing and POWER GRADATION's damage reduction make her strong in brawls
Landing TRI-SLASH speeds her up, which makes it easy to dash in and out
weaknesses: A missed skill breaks both the enhancement chain and the marks, and her damage drops
Few answers to enemies who poke from range or keep kiting
Her Attack Speed reduction falls off as enemies use basic attacks, so it does little against heavy single hits
If silenced, she cannot reach her enhanced basic attack

playstyle.style: Charlotte is a swordswoman whose next different skill is enhanced after any skill lands, no matter which one she starts with. Each hit adds a mark, and at three marks her next basic attack becomes a dash that strikes seven times, with the final strike growing with the target's lost Health. Her enhanced skills also lower the Attack Speed of enemies they hit, which helps her in brawls against basic attackers.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who enjoy deciding on the spot which skill to open with and how to chain the enhancements. Missing a skill breaks the chain and the marks, so being patient enough to get in range shapes her damage. She has few answers to enemies who keep firing from a distance, so she has to create her own chances to close in.

counters.reason: Gan & Mo knock enemies back while stepping away, so the melee range Devara relies on disappears.
Arli blinks away and speeds up with her parasol down, so Devara struggles to hold melee range.

synergy.reason: Kongming's magic fields slow enemies to a crawl, letting Devara stay in the melee range he wants.
Li Bai's dashes stun enemies in place, so the delayed blast of Divine Judgment lands on them.

passive.description:
At close range, Devara's Basic Attacks become melee attacks that have shorter attack intervals and grant 1 stack of Thunder Resolve, for up to 6 stacks. Upon reaching max stacks, Devara calls upon the power of thunder, gaining one extra basic skill use.
After using a basic skill, Devara gains an enhanced Basic Attack that deals an extra 85 (85 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and recovers 75 (75 + 1.2% extra Health) Health.
Ranged enhanced Basic Attacks deal 75% damage to non-target units and do not trigger on-hit effects.
passive.name: Wish of the Living

skill1.description: Devara charges forward like lightning, dealing 240 (240 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and gaining a shield that negates 360 (360 + 5.5% extra Health) damage for 2.5s.
skill1.name: Thunderblaze

skill2.description:
Devara unleashes a ball of lightning forward. Upon reaching its max range or colliding with an enemy, the lightning explodes after a short delay, knocking back enemies and dealing 240 (240 + 50% magical attack) magical damage.
The closer the unit is to Devara, the farther they are knocked back.
skill2.name: Divine Judgment

skill3.description:
Devara responds to an echo across millennia, rising into the air as he enters the Legacy Manifest state.
The transformation takes 1.5s, during which he ignores terrain and gains crowd control immunity and 30% Movement Speed. The golden staff at his back strikes nearby enemies in succession, prioritizing heroes. Each strike deals 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) magical damage, while also granting him 1 Thunder Resolve and a shield that negates 160 (160 + 2.5% extra Health) damage for 2s. Upon landing, he deals 200 (200 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
He remains transformed for 8s, during which the range of his enhanced Basic Attacks is increased, Basic Attacks grant 2 Thunder Resolve, and ranged Basic Attacks create chain lightning that bounces between multiple enemies, dealing 86 (50% physical attack) physical damage.
skill3.name: Millennium Echo

strategy.earlyGame: The first habit to build in the clash lane is slipping one Basic Attack in after every skill. The enhanced attack damages enemies around him and restores Health, so he can trade while clearing the wave without falling behind on HP. Until he learns his ultimate, Thunderblaze's dash is his only movement skill. Spend it on an attack and an enemy jungler arriving right after leaves him nowhere to go, so while you cannot see their jungler, keep it as your exit. Fill Thunder Resolve with close-range attacks before a trade and he gets one extra basic skill in it.
strategy.midGame: Once skirmishes start, Millennium Echo is how Devara gets into them. While he rises he has crowd control immunity and ignores terrain, so he can come down beside enemies from over a wall or from deep in a bush. The staff strikes in the air prioritize enemy heroes, and each one gives him a shield and Thunder Resolve. After landing, the transformation widens his enhanced Basic Attacks and makes each Basic Attack build more Thunder Resolve, so the extra basic skill comes around sooner. His ranged Basic Attacks chain between enemies, so the more tightly they stand, the more of them he hits. When the transformation ends, all of that goes back to normal. While Millennium Echo is down, keep Thunderblaze as your way out.
strategy.teamfight: Devara's teamfight starts with Millennium Echo dropping him beside the enemy. He is immune to crowd control while airborne, so he can answer an enemy engage by going in on top of it. After landing, keep slipping Basic Attacks between Thunderblaze and Divine Judgment to damage everyone nearby while healing. Enemies who stick to him can be shoved far away with a point-blank Divine Judgment. Thunderblaze can be used to attack, but saving it as the one way out once the transformation ends lets him survive into the next fight.

combos.title: Weave Skills and Basic Attacks
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Thunderblaze: shielded dash) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 2 (Divine Judgment: delayed blast and knockback) → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: The enhancement sits on that next attack, so the basic pattern is one Basic Attack between each skill. Hitting at close range also builds Thunder Resolve toward the next extra cast.

combos.title: Fill the Gauge, Then Commit
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (fill Thunder Resolve at close range) → Skill 1 (Thunderblaze) → the extra basic skill use from the thunder → Basic Attack (enhanced)
combos.description: The extra cast from Thunder Resolve still enhances his next Basic Attack, so a short trade gets one more round of damage and healing. Fill the gauge before the trade starts and you go in with more actions than your opponent.

combos.title: Rise and Drop In
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Millennium Echo: rise and ignore terrain) → Skill 1 (Thunderblaze) → Basic Attack (enhanced) → Skill 2 (Divine Judgment: point-blank)
combos.description: While rising in Millennium Echo he has crowd control immunity and ignores terrain, so he can reach enemies on the other side of a wall. The staff strikes in the air grant shields and Thunder Resolve, and during the transformation his Basic Attacks build Thunder Resolve faster. Anyone who sticks to him takes Divine Judgment at point-blank range, where the knockback sends them farthest.

strengths: The enhanced Basic Attack after each skill hits nearby enemies and restores Health
A full Thunder Resolve gauge grants one extra basic skill use
While airborne in Millennium Echo he ignores terrain and can come in over walls
Thunderblaze's dash comes with a shield, so it works for going in or getting out
weaknesses: If he cannot alternate skills and Basic Attacks, damage and healing drop together
Apart from Millennium Echo, Thunderblaze is his only movement, so engaging with it leaves no exit
Divine Judgment knocks enemies back less the farther away they are
Ranged enhanced Basic Attacks do not trigger on-hit effects

playstyle.style: A fighter whose basic skills each enhance his next Basic Attack, adding damage to enemies around him and a burst of healing. Close-range Basic Attacks build Thunder Resolve, and a full gauge gives Devara one extra basic skill use. Alternating skills and Basic Attacks is what keeps both his damage and his staying power going.
playstyle.suited: What decides it is whether you can stay on top of an enemy and keep slipping a Basic Attack between skills. If you tend to dump every skill at once, you get fewer enhanced attacks and less healing out of the brawl. His ultimate drops him into the middle of a fight on his own terms, so players who like walking into brawls on purpose will get a lot out of him.

synergy.reason: Dyadia's immobilize pins enemies in place, so Ying's Cloudchaser dash lands cleanly every time.
Yaria attaches to Ying and shields her from true damage, letting her stay in the fight.

counters.reason: Di Renjie's Legal Immunity blocks damage and crowd control alike, so Ying's engage lands on nothing.
Lady Sun keeps shaving time off Rolling Raid with every Basic Attack, so Ying struggles to close the gap.

passive.name: Spear Will - Sweeping Fire
passive.description: Ying is mentally linked with her spear, Sweeping Fire. Using skills grants 1 stack of Spear Will. Basic Attacks expend all Spear Will, use the corresponding Spear Will skill (Stalwart - Peacemaker, Zealous - Devastation, or Zenith - Wildfire), and reduce Moonslash and Cloudchaser Cooldown by 1.5s. Spear Will skills can crit and benefit from 50% of Attack Speed.

skill1.name: Moonslash / Stalwart - Peacemaker

forms.description: Ying swings her spear upward, then slashes downward, executing 2 strikes that each deal 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The upward strike launches enemies for 0.5s.

This skill is cast by using an enhanced Basic Attack at 1 stack of Spear Will.

skill1.description: Ying swings her spear upward, then slashes downward, executing 2 strikes that each deal 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The upward strike launches enemies for 0.5s.

skill2.name: Cloudchaser / Zealous - Devastation

forms.description: Ying raises her spear and charges up, gaining up to 25% Movement Speed. After charging, she dashes forward and executes a horizontal sweep, dealing 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack)-360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15% for 1s.

This skill is cast by using an enhanced Basic Attack at 2 stacks of Spear Will. The lower her Health, the greater the recovery effect (up to 2×).

skill2.description: Ying raises her spear and charges up, gaining up to 25% Movement Speed. skill3.name: Starburn / Zenith - Wildfire

Ying ignites Sweeping Fire's tip and dashes back and forth through the area before her. Each dash deals 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage and launches enemies.
