Ying leaps into the air and charges up before unleashing a sweeping strike, dealing 305 (150 + 90% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. The lower the target's Health, the greater the damage, up to a maximum of 611 (300 + 180% physical attack) physical damage when the target's Health is below 50%.
This skill is cast by using an enhanced Basic Attack at 3 stacks of Spear Will. While airborne, Ying ignores terrain, gains 200% Movement Speed, and gains 10% damage reduction.

skill3.description:
Ying ignites Sweeping Fire's tip and dashes back and forth through the area before her. Each dash deals 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage and launches enemies. Upon dashing to maximum range, she launches a flurry of stabs. Each stab deals 90 (90 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage, for a total of 4 stabs.
While using this skill, Ying gains crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction.
Upon activating the second phase of the skill, Roaring Sun, she sweeps forward with Sweeping Fire, leaving a trail of fire behind. The sweep deals 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage, and the trail of fire deals 50 (50 + 16% extra physical attack) magical damage every 0.2s over 3s, for a total of 1 time.
While Starburn is active, the second phase of the skill can be used to sweep the area around her, interrupting subsequent dashes, dealing 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage, and leaving a circular trail of fire behind for 3s.

strategy.earlyGame: In the jungle, Ying drills the order of a Basic Attack after each skill while clearing. Stalwart - Peacemaker, from one stack, comes with a shield, which also cuts the damage she takes from monsters. Once she learns Starburn, she can join river skirmishes together with Moonslash's launch. She struggles to do much if she is stopped before building Spear Will, so avoid going deep into the enemy jungle alone.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, skirmishes around Tyrant and Overlord are where Ying shines. Close in from a side bush with Cloudchaser's charged dash, launch with Moonslash, then slip in a Basic Attack, and the two-stack Zealous - Devastation keeps the damage going. Zealous - Devastation heals more the lower her Health, so she can keep brawling even after taking damage. Starburn suits diving in with its back-and-forth launches after seeing the enemy use one of their main crowd control skills. While Starburn is down, her ways to dive in and get out are limited, so avoid chasing too deep. The September 10 update lowered the damage of all three Spear Will skills.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, layering Starburn onto your team's engage is steadier than diving in the moment the fight starts. After that, weave a Basic Attack after each skill to keep Spear Will skills and their cooldown reduction cycling. Against fleeing enemies, build three stacks before the Basic Attack and leap in with Zenith - Wildfire.

combos.title: Build Three Stacks and Leap
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Cloudchaser: charge and dash) → Skill 1 (Moonslash: launch) → Skill 3 (Starburn: launch with back-and-forth dashes) → Basic Attack (Zenith - Wildfire at three stacks)
combos.description: Three skills in a row followed by a Basic Attack become Zenith - Wildfire, a leap into the air followed by a sweeping strike. While airborne she ignores terrain and moves faster, and the strike hits harder the lower the target's Health. It works as the finishing move for chasing a retreating enemy.

combos.title: Trade One Stack at a Time
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Moonslash: launch) → Basic Attack (Stalwart - Peacemaker at one stack) → Skill 2 (Cloudchaser: slow) → Basic Attack (Stalwart - Peacemaker at one stack)
combos.description: Weaving one Basic Attack after each skill brings out Stalwart - Peacemaker every time. Besides the flurry of strikes it gives her a short burst of speed, so she can adjust her position while trading.

combos.title: Cut Off Their Engage With Starburn
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Starburn: launch with back-and-forth dashes, crowd control immunity) → Skill 3 (Roaring Sun: stop the remaining dashes and sweep around her) → Skill 1 (Moonslash: launch)
combos.description: During Starburn she gains crowd control immunity and takes less damage. Meet the enemy's engage with the back-and-forth launches, then use the second phase, Roaring Sun, to stop the remaining dashes and sweep the area around her. The sweep leaves a trail of fire behind, so keep fighting on it with Moonslash and Basic Attacks.

strengths: Each Spear Will skill shortens Moonslash and Cloudchaser's cooldowns, so the longer the fight, the more she can do
Moonslash and Starburn launch enemies, letting her lift several at once
During Starburn she gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction
Zealous - Devastation heals more the lower her Health, so she holds on in brawls
weaknesses: She has to alternate skills and Basic Attacks, which takes time to learn
While Starburn is down, she has few ways to stop several enemies at once in teamfights
If crowd control stops her before she builds Spear Will, she is easily killed without doing much

playstyle.style: Ying is a jungler who builds Spear Will with every skill and turns her next Basic Attack into a Spear Will skill based on how many stacks she has. One stack gives Stalwart - Peacemaker, two give Zealous - Devastation and three give Zenith - Wildfire, and each one shortens the cooldowns of Moonslash and Cloudchaser. Spear Will skills can crit, and they come out faster as her attack speed rises.
playstyle.suited: She suits players who can count their Spear Will stacks while fighting. Throughout a fight she keeps choosing between attacking right after a skill or adding another skill to wait for a bigger Spear Will skill. Miscounting means the move you wanted does not come out, so drill the order into your hands while clearing the jungle.

synergy.reason: Diaochan's marks detonate into a slow, which is exactly when Feyd's dash lands cleanly.
Mulan's Balance detonation silences and heavily slows enemies, so Feyd can seal the whole group at once.

counters.reason: Liang's suppression lasts even longer on Feyd while he stands on a wall, leaving him stuck.
While Donghuang suppresses Feyd, the two share all damage, so even Feyd's allies end up hurting him.

passive.description:
Feyd can move freely on walls, where his Basic Attacks become ranged (and can be used while jumping).
He gains the following while on top of a wall:
Jade Carriage: Stocks Stepping on Jade uses 10% faster.
View from Above: Gains 15% increased field of vision.
Crowd Control Penalty: Crowd controls last 25% longer.
passive.name: Jade Carriage - View from Above

skill1.description:
Feyd moves swiftly forward, dealing 360 (360 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and launching them for 3/4s. At the same time, he gains 50% Attack Speed and enhances his next 3 Basic Attacks.
Melee: Each attack deals 75 (75 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage and restores 155 (155 + 1.5% extra Health) Health.
Ranged: Each attack deals 50 (50 + 13% extra physical attack) physical damage and bounces to the nearest unit within range on hit.
skill1.name: Jade Chase - Returning Strike

skill2.description:
When on the ground: Feyd leaps onto the target wall. The leap's range increases by 4% for each skill level.
When on a wall: Feyd steps on jade, jumping to the target wall.
Stocks 1 use of this skill every 10s, for up to 4 uses.
skill2.name: Stepping on Jade

skill3.description:
Feyd swings his jade blade in a horizontal sweep around him, dealing 240 (240 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage. (If he's on a wall, he will dash to the target area, then slash.) He marks all hit enemies and activates the skill's second phase, Hardened Jade Strike.
Hardened Jade Strike: Feyd slashes each marked target 4 times, causing the marks to shatter, dealing 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage that ignores untargetable states.
If a target's Health falls below 1/8, they will be Jadeified and shatter, being defeated.
skill3.name: Hardened Jade Seal

strategy.earlyGame: Feyd's wall-walking Passive is one of a kind, and you should lean on it from minute one. Clear your jungle, then scout the enemy's farm state from the walls before level 4 — you get 15% wider vision up there and your basic attacks become ranged, so you're poking and gathering information at zero risk. The standard gank is Skill 2 onto a wall, then Skill 1 to drop down and land the 0.75-second knock-up. One caveat to burn into memory: slows and CC applied to you last 25% longer while you're standing on a wall.
strategy.midGame: Around 8 minutes, once your first physical damage item is finished, the side-lane walls become your hunting grounds. Roam wall to wall with at least two Skill 2 stacks in reserve (you bank one every 10 seconds, up to four), and when you spot a low-HP target, unload the full kit: Skill 1, three empowered basic attacks, the Ultimate's mark, then its follow-up strike. Any enemy below 1/8 HP dies to that strike guaranteed — Feyd never knows the pain of a kill escaping on a sliver. Front-on brawls are not his game, so kill and leave, every time.
strategy.lateGame: From 15 minutes on, commit to entering fights late. Dive in at the start and his lack of bulk gets exposed, so perch on a wall, wait for a few enemy CC abilities to be spent, then drop. Your target list is short: the isolated marksman or mage, nobody else. Skill 1's drop knock-up leads into empowered basics (which heal you at melee range), and the Ultimate's mark plus follow-up strike closes the deal. When you're down to your last Skill 2 stack, stop chasing and save it for the trip back to a wall — that discipline is what keeps you alive.
strategy.teamfight: Skip the head-on collision entirely and time your entrance from the outer walls. The moment enemy eyes lock onto your frontline, drop in from the side and put Skill 1 into a backliner. Skill 3's sweep marks everything it touches, and the follow-up, Hardened Jade Strike, ignores untargetable states as it shatters those marks. An enemy who goes untargetable to slip away still takes it, so long as the mark is on them. Take the kill, Skill 2 back to a wall, and reset for the next pick. A trick that pays real dividends: choose a wall along the enemy's escape route before the fight starts — the kills you collect go up noticeably.

combos.title: Wall Entry Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (leap from the ground onto a wall) → Basic Attack from the wall (ranged) → Skill 1 (move + 0.75s launch, +50% Attack Speed) → 3 melee enhanced Basic Attacks → Skill 3 (sweep applies marks) → Hardened Jade Strike
combos.description: On a wall his Basic Attacks turn ranged, so he chips away from a spot they cannot reach. Skill 1 moves him forward as it damages the path, which carries him off the wall and into the launch. Land the three enhanced Basic Attacks in melee range: each one restores 155 Health at Lvl 1, while the ranged version carries no healing at all.

combos.title: The 1/8 Execute
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.75s launch) → Skill 3 (sweep applies marks) → Hardened Jade Strike (shatters the marks)
combos.description: The shortest path onto a fleeing low-Health target. Once a target sits below 1/8 Health, the Hardened Jade Strike jadeifies them and the kill is guaranteed. It also ignores untargetable states, so going untargetable buys them nothing. Whether you reach them at all comes down to the Skill 1 launch stopping their feet.

combos.title: Wall Swap Reset
combos.sequence: Hardened Jade Strike → Skill 2 (jump to a different wall) → Basic Attack from the wall (ranged)
combos.description: Skill 2 stocks one use every 10s and holds up to 4. Spend one the moment the kill lands and the ranged chip damage starts again from safety. Crowd control lasts 25% longer while he stands on a wall, so a wall inside enemy range turns the reset into a death sentence.

strengths: Wall movement plus ranged basics enable zero-risk scouting and poke
Skill 3's execute guarantees kills below 1/8 HP — nothing slips away
The follow-up strike shatters marks even through untargetable states
Skill 1's knock-up and 50% attack speed give brutal short-window stickiness
weaknesses: Slows and CC on him last 25% longer while he is standing on a wall
Mobility falls off a cliff once his Skill 2 stacks run dry
No stats for front-on brawling — late fight entries are mandatory
Struggles to show his identity in open areas with few walls

playstyle.style: An assassin who walks on walls, claiming a vertical dimension no one else can use. Ranged attacks from above and sudden drops give him attack lines that simply don't exist for grounded heroes.
playstyle.suited: players who find value in the space nobody else uses — scouting and poking from the wall layer, and accepting that crowd control lasts 25% longer up there.

synergy.reason: Yaria attaches and shields Alessio, so he can hold a forward position and keep firing.
Guiguzi pulls enemies into one stunned cluster, so Alessio's area shots hit the whole group at once.

counters.reason: Li Bai cannot be targeted during his ultimate, so Alessio's attacks find nothing at all.
Lady Sun's Frag Grenade slows Alessio hard, so her Ultimate Shell is far harder for him to dodge.

passive.description:
Alessio's Basic Attack fires a shell that deals area damage, plus extra physical damage equal to 0.5% of the target's Health. While he is grounded, the shell can be blocked by enemy heroes.
—The new Captain Red Hawk's ability to improvise is his greatest virtue, according to him.
passive.name: Rebellious Little Hawk

skill1.description:
Alessio enhances his next 3 Basic Attacks to use upgraded shells, which have a greater area of effect and deal 180 (180 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage and extra physical damage equal to 1% of the target's Health.
—Biron chipped in to help fund Alessio's upgraded shells, but even then, Alessio can only use them sparingly.
skill1.name: Upgraded Shell

skill2.description:
Alessio throws a smoke bomb, creating a smoke cloud that grants stealth to himself and his teammates for 3.5s. The bomb's explosion sends him into the air, granting him Movement Speed for 0.8s. While airborne, he can move and use Basic Attacks and skills while ignoring terrain. Using Basic Attacks or the Ultimate while airborne causes him to stay airborne longer.
While airborne, Skill 2 will not throw smoke bombs, and Basic Attacks cannot be blocked by enemies.
—"Give 'em a good scare!" Alessio is a master when it comes to making an entrance.
skill2.name: Legendary Hero Debut

skill3.description:
Alessio leaps into the air, gaining brief crowd control immunity, then locks onto an enemy hero and fires 5 shells at them, with each shell dealing 350 (350 + 80% extra physical attack) (+ 6% of target's lost Health) physical damage to enemies within the explosion's range. If the same target is hit by multiple shells, subsequent shells only deal 25% damage. Only 1 shell can be diverted to another enemy hero other than the locked-on target.
"You here for the fireworks?"
skill3.name: Sunset Fireworks Show

strategy.earlyGame: In the farm lane, Alessio clears the wave with exploding shells and catches his opponent in the blast. Firing at angles where minions and the opponent overlap clears and pokes at the same time. Grounded shells can be blocked by enemy heroes, so when their frontliner stands in the way, switch to taking last hits. When things turn dangerous, use Legendary Hero Debut to lay smoke and take to the air, leaving over terrain. The smoke is his key tool for both escaping and attacking, so don't spend it just to travel faster.
strategy.midGame: When he leaves lane for an objective, moving inside the smoke with his team hides their approach and sets up ambushes. In trades, stack Upgraded Shell's three shots when the enemy bunches up so the wider blasts hit several at once. When someone dives him, escape into the air with Legendary Hero Debut and fire Sunset Fireworks Show from there to stay up while hitting back. One shell can be taken by another enemy hero, so it finishes more reliably when the target is isolated. Keep one step behind your front line.
strategy.teamfight: Open teamfights by chipping widely with upgraded shell blasts from behind your front line, and step forward once the enemy's engage skills are used. Using Legendary Hero Debut after Sunset Fireworks Show has lifted him makes his basic attacks unblockable, so he can shoot past the front line at their back line. Pile shells onto any low-Health enemy left standing. Once he is on the ground with both smoke and ultimate used, he has no escape, so stay close to your front line during that window.

combos.title: Take to the Air and Unload
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Upgraded Shell: load upgraded shells) → Skill 2 (Legendary Hero Debut: smoke and go airborne) → Basic Attack (fire from the air) → Skill 3 (Sunset Fireworks Show: shells)
combos.description: In the air he moves over terrain and can still use basic attacks and skills. Basic attacks and Sunset Fireworks Show used while airborne keep him up longer, so the more he fires, the longer he stays off the ground. The shells grow with lost Health, so chip the target with upgraded shells first to make the finish easier.

combos.title: An Air Fight They Cannot Block
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Sunset Fireworks Show: leap and fire) → Skill 2 (use it in the air) → Basic Attack (keep firing from the air)
combos.description: Shells fired from the ground can be blocked by enemy heroes, but using Legendary Hero Debut in the air skips the smoke bomb and makes his basic attacks unblockable. Even against a wall of frontliners, he can shoot the back line directly.

combos.title: Smoke Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Legendary Hero Debut: hide in smoke) → Basic Attack (fire from stealth) → Skill 1 (Upgraded Shell) → Basic Attack (three upgraded shells)
combos.description: The smoke hides his teammates as well as him. Lay it down before an objective and pile upgraded shells onto whoever walks in; that is the ambush. Upgraded shells have a wider blast and larger bonus damage based on max Health.

strengths: His basic attack shells hit an area and add damage based on the target's max Health
The smoke hides him and his teammates for a while
In the air, his basic attacks cannot be blocked, so he can hit targets behind the front line
Sunset Fireworks Show grows with the target's lost Health, making wounded enemies easier to finish
weaknesses: On the ground with Legendary Hero Debut and his ultimate down, he has no escape
Grounded shells can be blocked by enemy heroes, so a frontliner in the way stops them
One shell from Sunset Fireworks Show can be taken by another enemy hero instead
Repeated shells on the same target deal less from the second one on

playstyle.style: Alessio is a marksman whose shells explode over an area. Legendary Hero Debut's smoke hides him and his teammates, and the blast sends him into the air, where he can move over terrain while still firing. His ultimate, Sunset Fireworks Show, rains shells on one locked-on enemy hero and hits harder the more Health they have lost.
playstyle.suited: Shells fired from the ground can be blocked by enemy heroes, so you build his play around when to take to the air and how long to stay there. If you enjoy vanishing in smoke and changing position, he trades very differently from other marksmen. On the ground with smoke and ultimate both down, he has no escape, so that window needs careful positioning.

synergy.reason: Lu Bu's ultimate bunches enemies up and pins them, so Furtive Attack's line runs through the whole group.
Menki's stacking slows leave enemies unable to walk out of Luara's serpent blades.

counters.reason: Diaochan's blink keeps refunding its own cooldown, so Luara can never hold her kiting distance.
Gao Changgong speeds up while closing in, so Luara cannot walk away before his mark stuns her.

passive.description:
When using Skill 1 and her Ultimate, Luara gains up to 2 serpent blades that attack enemies during her Basic Attacks.
She gains a 5% Attack Speed boost for 3s when using skills, for up to 3 stacks.
passive.name: Serpent's Envoy

skill1.description:
Luara gains 60 Movement Speed that diminishes over 1.5s and a serpent blade. While the serpent blade is active, she gains a brief Movement Speed burst and can leap over a wall once.
The serpent blade attacks targets continuously, dealing 60 (35 + 15% physical attack) physical damage (attack speed scales with her Attack Speed).
Every 3 serpent blade attacks count as 1 Basic Attack. Attacks grant vision of the attacked target, and deal 50% damage to secondary targets.
skill1.name: Deadly Fang

skill2.description:
Luara summons the Fire Serpent at the target location. After a short delay, the Fire Serpent charges at her, dealing 450 (450 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path, slowing them by 25% for 2s, and pulling them back slightly (not considered a crowd control effect).
If Luara has active serpent blades, the serpent blades immediately attack enemies hit by the Fire Serpent. If she does not have active serpent blades, 25% of Skill 2's Cooldown is returned.
skill2.name: Furtive Attack

skill3.description:
Luara summons the Fire Serpent in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and blinding them for 1.5s. This skill can be used while moving.
Luara enhances herself and gains a serpent blade. While enhanced, she gains Energy every time she deals damage with Basic Attacks and skills. Each time she reaches max Energy, she rains fire on nearby enemies, dealing 150 (150 + 48% extra physical attack) magical damage and launching enemies within range for 1/3s.
Blinded enemies cannot deal damage with Basic Attacks, and their skill projectiles will deviate from their normal trajectories by a random offset and hit enemies along the way.
skill3.name: Blazing Glare

strategy.earlyGame: Each Deadly Fang adds one serpent blade. In the farm lane, cast it before you start attacking: the blade keeps cutting the opponent and grants vision of them. Deadly Fang also lets her leap a wall once, so keeping one cast as an escape instead of spending it on engages is safer.
strategy.midGame: Every skill cast raises her Attack Speed a little, and the serpent blades cut faster as her Attack Speed rises. Three blade cuts count as one Basic Attack, so more Attack Speed means more Basic Attacks overall. Keep Deadly Fang and Furtive Attack rolling instead of holding them, so the Attack Speed bonus stays up. In skirmishes, place Furtive Attack behind the enemy and use the slow and slight pull to drag them toward your team. When a Basic Attack hero gets on top of her, blind them with her ultimate, Blazing Glare. A blinded enemy deals no damage with Basic Attacks and their skill projectiles stray at random, which gives her time to hit back. Energy stops building while she backs out of attack range during the enhancement, so decide whether to stay or retreat by checking which skills the enemy still has.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, she keeps attacking from behind the frontline with her serpent blades cycling. Blazing Glare can be cast on the move, so if it reaches the enemy marksman as the fight opens, that marksman's Basic Attacks deal no damage while the blind lasts. If someone dives her while she is enhanced, keep attacking, and the fire rain that comes with a full Energy bar launches them. Once there is space, speed up with Deadly Fang and leap a wall to reposition. When someone chases her, placing Furtive Attack behind them slows them with the charge back toward her.

combos.title: Kite With a Serpent Blade
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Deadly Fang: a serpent blade and a speed boost) → Basic Attack (the blade cuts) → leap a wall to reset the distance
combos.description: Casting Deadly Fang first means her Basic Attacks start with a serpent blade already active. The blade grants vision of whoever it cuts, so a target who backs into a bush does not disappear. The speed boost and the wall leap come from the same skill, so she can reopen the gap straight after the trade.

combos.title: Blind Them, Then Brawl
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Blazing Glare: blind and self-enhancement) → Basic Attack (build Energy) → Skill 2 (Furtive Attack: slow and pull)
combos.description: With the blind already applied, she can trade with an enemy who relies on Basic Attacks without taking that damage. While enhanced, the damage she deals builds Energy and a full bar brings down fire rain, so keeping her attacks going is what produces the launch. When the blind wears off and the target starts to back away, land Furtive Attack so the slow and pull make the escape harder.

combos.title: Catch Them From Behind
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Deadly Fang: hold a serpent blade) → Skill 2 (Furtive Attack: summon behind the enemy)
combos.description: Using Deadly Fang before Furtive Attack means enemies hit by the Fire Serpent are also cut by the serpent blade. The Fire Serpent charges toward Luara, so placing it behind the enemy sends its return path straight through them. Without a blade, part of the cooldown is returned instead, so when the extra cut is not needed, casting it alone is fine.

strengths: Serpent blades grant vision of whatever they cut, so a target hiding in a bush stays visible
Blazing Glare's blind stops the damage of the target's Basic Attacks
Deadly Fang lets her leap a wall once, opening an escape route when she is chased
Keep dealing damage while enhanced and fire rains down, launching nearby enemies
weaknesses: Blind only stops Basic Attack damage; skill projectiles are only knocked off course
Calling down the fire rain means staying close enough to keep attacking while enhanced
Without a serpent blade, Furtive Attack cannot add extra cuts to the enemies it hits
Using Deadly Fang to engage leaves her without the wall leap until it comes back

playstyle.style: How Luara fights depends on whether she is holding serpent blades. Each cast of Deadly Fang and of her ultimate, Blazing Glare, adds a serpent blade, and the blades keep cutting enemies alongside her Basic Attacks. They also grant vision of whatever they cut, so an enemy who ducks into a bush stays in sight and the trade goes on.
playstyle.suited: The Fire Serpent from Furtive Attack hits enemies on its way back from where it was placed toward Luara. Every cast means deciding whether to put it behind the opponent or ahead of where she is heading, so she suits players who would rather win on reading placement than on reaction speed. She also has to track how many serpent blades she holds and whether Blazing Glare's enhancement is active, which adds up to a lot to watch on screen.

synergy.reason: Diaochan needs repeated hits to build her marks, and Ata's Ghost Ship wall pens enemies in place.
Xiao Qiao's Meteor Storm keeps raining on whoever is nearby, and Ata's Sea Anchor slow keeps them there.

counters.reason: Shouyue's Wild Wind scales off max Health, so the more Health Ata stacks, the harder it hits.
Lady Sun's rolls come back faster with every Basic Attack she lands, so Ata struggles to close the gap.

passive.description: Ata's lost Health is stored in a buffer for 7s, and he recovers Health from the buffer equal to 40%/20% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes / non-hero units respectively (recovery is increased by 1%/0.5% for every 1,000 extra Health). After 7s, Ata's buffered Health will diminish by 3% Health per second. Basic Attacks deal 70 (70 + 35% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
passive.name: Child of the Sea

skill1.description:
Ata leaps and slams his anchor into the ground, dealing 460 (460 + 13% extra Health) physical damage. He then bounces forward, dealing the same amount of physical damage and launching enemies within range for 0.5s.
If he hits multiple enemies, the damage is reduced by 20% for each additional enemy, down to 60% of the initial damage. Deals 30% extra damage to minions.
After the bounce, he rolls in the target direction. He gains crowd control immunity while using this skill.
skill1.name: Wavewalking

skill2.description:
Ata hurls his anchor in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and reducing their Movement Speed by 30% for 1.5s. If the anchor hits a wall, Ata will pull himself and any enemies in his path to the wall and smash into it, dealing 250 (250 + 10% extra Health) physical damage and stunning any enemies smashed for 0.5s.
Passive: Using Skill 2 enhances the next Basic Attack, pulling the target enemy to Ata.
skill2.name: Sea Anchor

skill3.description:
Ata erects a high wall in a cone-shaped target area that blocks heroes and lasts for 4s. When erected, the wall deals 350 (350 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in front of him.
While using the Ultimate, he gains crowd control immunity.
skill3.name: Ghost Ship

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Ata holds the lane while chipping minions as a group with Wavewalking. Wavewalking deals extra damage to minions, so it also helps clear waves. Health he has lost comes back partly when he hits the opponent, so hitting back right after taking damage keeps his losses small. If he can drive the opponent against a wall beside the lane, hitting the wall with Sea Anchor's anchor gives him a stun. His buffered Health diminishes over time, so back off without forcing it when there is no chance to hit back.
strategy.midGame: From the mid game on, he is the one who dives first in small fights. Wavewalking deals damage on both landings, launches on the second, and makes him immune to crowd control while in use, so he can reach back-liners without worrying about enemy crowd control. The enhanced basic attack after Sea Anchor pulls the target in front of him, so he can smash them into a wall, pull them in and set up his team's focus fire. In fights over Shadow Tyrant or Shadow Overlord, Ghost Ship's wall is where his engages start. It raises a cone-shaped wall heroes cannot pass, so placing it between the enemy front line and back line lets his team hit only one side. In the narrow paths in front of the bosses, the longer detour makes the wall last longer in effect. Leap at the separated enemy damage dealer with Wavewalking and have his team's damage follow the launch from the second landing.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, he dives at the front as his team engages and treats taking hits as his job. His buffered Health comes back the more he hits enemy heroes, so the center of the brawl is where Ata holds on best. Using the crowd control immunity of Wavewalking and Ghost Ship in turn lets him cut off the enemy's escape and reinforcements with the wall without being stopped. The wall can be angled to trap enemies or to shut out reinforcements. Watch where his teammates are and choose the angle that gives them the most room to move.

combos.title: Smash Them Into a Wall, Then Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Sea Anchor: hit a wall to dash and stun) → Basic Attack (enhanced, pulls the target in front of him) → Skill 1 (Wavewalking: second landing launches)
combos.description: When the anchor hits a wall or other terrain, he dashes and smashes enemies in his path into it, stunning them. The following enhanced basic attack pulls the target in front of him, and Wavewalking's second landing launches them again. If he throws the anchor before driving the enemy against a wall, the dash never happens.

combos.title: Split the Battlefield With the Wall
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Ghost Ship: raise the wall and damage enemies in front) → Skill 1 (Wavewalking: leap in immune to crowd control and launch) → Basic Attack
combos.description: He is also immune to crowd control during Wavewalking, so enemy crowd control cannot stop him from stepping in. His buffered Health comes back from damage dealt to enemy heroes, so the longer he stays at the center of the brawl, the longer he lasts.

strengths: He wins back lost Health by attacking, so the longer the brawl, the longer he lasts
A wide range of crowd control: the anchor's wall stun, the enhanced Basic Attack's pull and Wavewalking's launch
He is immune to crowd control during Wavewalking and Ghost Ship, so he cannot be stopped mid-skill
Ghost Ship's wall can split the enemy team or cut off their escape
weaknesses: Short Basic Attack range, so if the anchor misses he struggles to catch enemies attacking from afar
Low damage for finishing a single target, so kills rely on his team's damage
A badly angled wall can shut his own teammates out

playstyle.style: Ata is a tank who stands at the front while winning back lost Health by hitting enemies. Damage he takes is stored in a buffer for a while, and dealing damage to enemies during that time recovers part of it. He smashes enemies into walls with his anchor, and his ultimate, Ghost Ship, raises a wall that heroes cannot pass, dividing the battlefield.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who prefer hitting back to hold on rather than absorbing damage passively. His buffered Health diminishes over time, so he needs to decide quickly to hit back after taking damage. A badly angled wall can shut his own teammates out, so working out the angle before the fight is also essential.

synergy.reason: Yaria attaches and shields Umbrosa, letting her finish the full dance deep in the enemy line.
Zhuangzi's ultimate grants crowd control immunity and a shield, so Umbrosa keeps dancing instead of getting locked down.

counters.reason: Di Renjie's Legal Immunity blocks damage and crowd control, so Umbrosa's dive lands on nothing.
Daji's Strike a Pose is a targeted stun that cuts Umbrosa's dance short before it finishes.

passive.description:
When attacking distant targets, Umbrosa's Basic Attack throws out a rebounding blade. She can only attack again once the blade returns. However, if she uses her Basic Attack just before the blade returns, it will instantly rebound forward for another strike.
While in ranged mode, every 1% Attack Speed increases her damage by 1.5. Each consecutive rebound of the blade further increases its damage and flight speed by 5%, for up to 3 stacks.
When attacking nearby targets, Umbrosa switches to melee mode. Her Basic Attack becomes a flurry of 3 rapid strikes, dealing a total of 170 (100% physical attack) physical damage, plus an extra 70 (70 + 22% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Each Basic Attack applies a mark to the enemy. Marked enemies take extra damage when hit by Feathered Tempest.
passive.name: Whirling Featherblades

skill1.description:
Umbrosa instantly gains a burst of Movement Speed that diminishes over 1s and fires up to 6 Featherblades at nearby enemies, each dealing 45 (45 + 15% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Then Umbrosa enters the Frenzied state, gaining 60 Movement Speed that diminishes over 3s and 50% Attack Speed for 3s.
If there are multiple targets nearby, the Featherblades are distributed randomly among them.
Each Featherblade applies a mark to the enemy. Marked enemies take extra damage when hit by Feathered Tempest.
skill1.name: Feverish Dance

skill2.description:
Umbrosa dashes forward, dealing 150 (150 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path and knocking them back (not considered a crowd control effect). At the same time, she triggers the Featherblade marks of all hit targets and spreads them to nearby enemies.
If there are enemies ahead, Umbrosa performs a graceful dance, throwing rebounding flying blades that strike 10 times, each dealing 110 (110 + 38% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 50 (50 + 0.8% extra Health) Health (halved against non-hero units; the speed of the flying blades is dependent on her Attack Speed). The final strike deals an extra 100% damage. Each hit consumes 1 mark to deal an extra 45 (45 + 15% extra physical attack) physical damage.
She can move freely while dancing, and using the skill again will cancel its effects. If the dance is not triggered, she recovers 50% of the skill's Mana cost and the cooldown will be reduced to 50% of the original.
skill2.name: Feathered Tempest

skill3.description:
Umbrosa reignites her former glory as an Austren, dealing 400 (400 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies while temporarily gaining 50% Health, 150 Movement Speed (diminishes over time), and Indomitable for 4s. Any recovery effects will be tallied only after the state ends.
If Umbrosa is defeated while this skill is not on cooldown, she will resurrect after a short delay (gaining 50% of the Health from actively using the skill) and deal 400 (400 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies, after which this skill will enter cooldown.
If her temporary Health is fully depleted, Indomitable will end early.
skill3.name: Final Frenzy

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, Umbrosa chips her opponent with the ranged blade and stacks marks as she goes. Feathered Tempest only dances when an enemy is ahead of her; when it doesn't, the cooldown is shortened and part of the Mana comes back. The dance heals only half as much against minions, so to win back a lot of Health, catch the enemy hero in it. Once she learns her ultimate, holding Final Frenzy means a death brings her back, which lets her accept slightly deeper trades.
strategy.midGame: Once she starts moving around the map, pick targets with Feverish Dance's blades in mind. With several enemies nearby the blades scatter at random, so a lone target collects more marks and takes a heavier dance. She has no skill that stops an enemy, so fleeing targets are chased with the speed from Feverish Dance and Final Frenzy. Deepfrost Siege in her build slows whoever it hits, which makes runners easier to stay on once it is done. If the fight turns, recast Feathered Tempest to cut the dance short. After Final Frenzy has been used, the revival is gone too, so until it is back it is safer not to chase too deep.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, how she plays depends on whether she enters with Final Frenzy held or already used. Held, a death brings her back after a short delay, damaging nearby enemies as she rejoins. Used, she brings the temporary Health and the damage around her in from the start. Marks on enemies hit by Feathered Tempest's dash spread to those nearby, so sending it through a clump leaves more marks for the dance to cash in. She can move while dancing, so she keeps firing while repositioning.

combos.title: Stack Marks, Then Dance
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Feverish Dance: mark with blades) → Basic Attack (melee flurry to add marks) → Skill 2 (Feathered Tempest: dance to spend marks)
combos.description: Each hit of the dance spends one mark for extra damage. The more marks you stack first, the more hits carry that extra, which is why Feverish Dance and Basic Attacks come first. Feverish Dance also leaves her Frenzied with bonus Attack Speed, so she can fit those mark-stacking attacks into a short window.

combos.title: Into the Dance With Temporary Health
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Feverish Dance: apply marks) → Skill 3 (Final Frenzy: temporary Health and Indomitable) → Skill 2 (Feathered Tempest: dance to spend marks)
combos.description: Final Frenzy damages nearby enemies as she gains temporary Health, so casting it up close lets her go straight into the dance. Recovery during Indomitable is tallied after it ends, so Health from the dance comes in afterward. Casting it gives up the revival, so check that the target can be finished before committing.

combos.title: Rebound Poke
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (throw the blade at range) → Basic Attack (time it just before the blade returns) → Skill 2 (Feathered Tempest: close in and spend marks)
combos.description: Time a Basic Attack just before the ranged blade returns and it rebounds for another hit, growing in damage and speed as you keep it going. Each hit is a Basic Attack, so it also applies a mark. Stacking marks from range and then stepping in with Feathered Tempest makes use of the time before you commit.

strengths: Her Basic Attack switches between blade and flurry to match the enemy's distance
Feathered Tempest's dance can be used on the move and heals her on every hit
Dying with Final Frenzy unused revives her and damages nearby enemies
When the dance does not trigger, Feathered Tempest's cooldown shortens and part of the Mana comes back
weaknesses: No skill that stops an enemy, so fleeing targets can only be chased with speed boosts
Indomitable from Final Frenzy ends early once the temporary Health is gone
Casting Final Frenzy also gives up the revival until it comes off cooldown
Feverish Dance spreads its blades at random, so in a crowd fewer marks land on the target you want

playstyle.style: Umbrosa's ultimate, Final Frenzy, pushes her forward with temporary Health when she casts it, and turns into a revival if she holds it and dies. Her Basic Attack changes with range: a rebounding blade at a distance, a quick three-hit flurry up close. Stack marks with Feverish Dance and Basic Attacks, then cash them in with the dance of Feathered Tempest for extra damage.
playstyle.suited: Each fight asks whether to open with Final Frenzy or save it for when she goes down. The better you read your own Health and the enemy's remaining skills, the longer she stays in the fight. The ranged blade rebounds when you time a Basic Attack just before it returns, so expect some practice to get that timing down.

synergy.reason: Dolia refreshes an ally's longest cooldown, which on Heino is his heavy ultimate Fate Rewind.
Da Qiao's koi launches a whole group, giving Heino an opening to dive in with Leap of Fate and heal more.

counters.reason: Butterfly's Death Dealer cuts Basic Attack damage, so Heino's melee scepter swings barely hurt her.
Zhang Fei carries a huge shield from Unbridled Outburst for so long that Heino cannot chew through him.

passive.description:
Heino engages in combat in either melee or ranged mode as fate dictates. His skills and melee Basic Attacks mark enemies for 7s on hit.
Ranged: He channels the Power of Fate to attack distant enemies, dealing 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage and (15% magical attack) magical damage.
Melee: He brandishes his scepter to attack all nearby enemies, dealing 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage and (45% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Fate's Guidance

skill1.description:
Heino reduces his cooldown by 0.2s for each marked enemy hit, up to 1s.
Ranged: He turns his scepter into energy and throws it, dealing 410 (410 + 75% magical attack) magical damage upon hit. He also throws 1 extra scepter at every marked enemy in front of him, dealing 75% damage.
Melee: He throws his scepter spinning, dealing 260 (260 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and slowing them by 15% for 2s. He recovers 150 (150 + 5% extra Health) Health for each target hit.
Ranged: When extra scepters hit the same target multiple times, subsequent hits only deal 50% of the initial damage. Melee: Recovers Health up to 3 times.
skill1.name: Scepter of Fate

skill2.description:
Heino dashes forward. If there are no enemy heroes near the end of the dash, he goes into ranged mode. Otherwise, he goes into melee mode.
Ranged: Gains 15% Movement Speed for 2s. For each enemy hero near the starting point of the dash, his Movement Speed increases by 25%, up to 50%. If Skill 2 causes him to switch from melee to ranged mode, both the Movement Speed increase and its limit are doubled.
Melee: Gains 100 max Health and 100 max Mana, and recovers 450 (450 + 12% extra Health) Health while increasing max Health by the same amount. For each enemy hero near the endpoint of the dash, his Health recovery increases by 25%, up to 50%. If Skill 2 causes him to switch from ranged to melee mode, both the Health recovery and its limit are doubled.
skill2.name: Leap of Fate

skill3.description:
Heino leaves behind a memory whenever he changes to ranged mode. He creates a field that grants 15% damage reduction and recovers 400 (400 + 6% extra Health) Health. During this time, he has crowd control immunity but cannot move. After a 1.5s delay, the field deals 400 (400 + 100% magical attack) magical damage and he returns to the memory he left behind. If there is an allied tower within the field, that tower returns to its state from 5s earlier.
The lower his Health, the more Health he recovers, up to 2 times the base value.
skill3.name: Fate Rewind

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Heino starts in ranged mode, throwing Scepter of Fate to clear the wave and poke safely. The core is mark management: marks from skills and melee basic attacks enable Scepter of Fate's healing and cooldown reduction, so keeping them up is the basis of both his damage and his staying power. Until he has his ultimate, don't overextend; use the time to get a feel for how Leap of Fate switches modes.
strategy.midGame: Once he learns Fate Rewind, his way of entering and leaving fights changes. The point where Leap of Fate put him into ranged mode is remembered, and Fate Rewind lets him hold out briefly and then return there, so he can set a memory somewhere safe, push forward to fight, and heal back once worn down. In objective fights, get into the habit of making the memory behind your team before diving in melee mode. When your front line is thick, keep throwing Scepter of Fate in ranged mode; when it is thin, stack Leap of Fate's healing and max Health growth in melee mode and stand in front. When defending a tower, including it in Fate Rewind's field returns it to an earlier state.
strategy.teamfight: Before a teamfight, set a ranged-mode memory somewhere safe. That alone turns a melee-mode dive into an attack he can come back from. Once in, hold the brawl with Leap of Fate's healing and Scepter of Fate, and use Fate Rewind when focused. He takes reduced damage while it holds, leaves area damage behind, and returns to the memory. Casting it too early wastes the extra healing at low Health, so returning after absorbing the enemy's burst pays off more.

combos.title: Leave a Memory, Step In, Return
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Leap of Fate: switch to ranged where no enemies are, leaving a memory) → Skill 2 (switch to melee near enemies and heal) → Skill 1 (Scepter of Fate: melee heal per marked target) → Skill 3 (Fate Rewind: return to the memory)
combos.description: Only one memory point exists at a time, so make it before stepping forward. Leap of Fate's mode is decided by whether enemy heroes are near the end of the dash, not by choice. He cannot move during Fate Rewind, but the healing grows the lower his Health, so use it planning to absorb the enemy's attack before returning.

combos.title: Poke Without Losing the Marks
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Scepter of Fate: ranged throw applies a mark) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (an extra scepter flies at marked enemies)
combos.description: Marks come from skills and melee basic attacks and last for a while. Each hit on a marked enemy shortens Scepter of Fate's cooldown, and the second throw sends an extra scepter at marked enemies ahead for bonus damage.

strengths: He switches between ranged and melee modes to change his role mid-fight
Fate Rewind returns him to his memory point, so he can retreat safely after pushing forward
Fate Rewind heals more the lower his Health, so he holds on when cornered
Including an allied tower in Fate Rewind's field rewinds that tower to an earlier state
weaknesses: His skill healing and faster casting depend on marks, and his strength drops when they lapse
He cannot move during Fate Rewind, so being surrounded draws focused damage
If he dies before returning, Fate Rewind's whole value is lost
Managing both his mode and his memory point keeps his hands busy

playstyle.style: Heino fights differently in his ranged and melee modes. If Leap of Fate's dash ends with no enemy heroes nearby he switches to ranged mode, and if enemies are near he switches to melee; ranged mode speeds him up, while melee mode heals him and raises his max Health. His ultimate, Fate Rewind, remembers a point where he went into ranged mode, holds his ground for a moment, then returns him there.
playstyle.suited: He suits players who enjoy denying opponents their preferred range. You plan a full cycle: leave a memory somewhere safe, step forward to fight, and use Fate Rewind to return once worn down. Tracking his mode and his memory point at the same time keeps you busy.

synergy.reason: Kongming's Spirit Bomb scales with Health already lost, so Mayene's combo damage sets up his finisher.
Mozi's stuns freeze the target in place, giving Mayene a clean opening to start her combo on.

counters.reason: Arthur's silence shuts Mayene down, since she fights entirely in chained skill combos.
Liang's suppression locks Mayene in place and cuts her combo chain apart halfway through.

passive.name: Slack Off a Lil Bit
passive.description:
Mayene's skills consume Punch Strength or Kick Strength. When idle and not taking damage, she sits down to slack off, accelerating Strength recovery by 25%. While slacking, she snacks on treats, randomly recovering 110 (110 + 2% extra Health) × 1/1.5/2 Health.
Attacking, taking damage, or moving interrupts this effect. She won't slack off in Serious State.
Using a different skill combo within 3s of another boosts its effect by 25%.

skill1.name: Whatever (I) / Exploit Weakness / Defend by Attacking

forms.description:
Mayene runs forward and pulls in enemies in front of her, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in a cone-shaped area and slowing them by 30% for 1s.
Exploit Weakness: When using Whatever (I) again quickly after, she will leap into the air and deliver a powerful strike, dealing 400 (400 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and extra physical damage equal to 10% of the target's Health, as well as launching them for 1s.
Deals 50% extra damage to enemies in the center of the skill.
Mayene takes 25% less damage while using the skill.
Feint to Retreat: Mayene delivers a smooth combo of strikes, starting with 3 punches that deal 200 (200 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage each, followed by a knee strike that deals 200 (200 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage while pushing the target backward slightly (not a crowd control effect). She also recovers 200 (200 + 5% extra Health) Health.
This skill costs 1 Punch Strength. She recovers 1 Punch Strength every 8.5s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), and can stock up to 2 bars at a time.

When using Whatever (I) again quickly after Whatever (I),
Mayene leaps into the air and delivers a powerful strike, dealing 400 (400 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage (+ 10% of the target's max Health) to enemies within range and launching them for 1s.
Enemies in the center take an extra 50% damage.
Gains 25% damage reduction while using this combo.

When using Whatever (I) quickly after Whatever (II),
Mayene teleports behind the enemy and launches a spinning kick, knocking back the target and dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) (+ 15% of the target's lost Health) physical damage.
If the target is defeated, she recovers 300 (300 + 5% extra Health) Health and 50% Strength. The recovery effect is doubled if she defeats an enemy hero.

Flee Danger: When using Whatever (II) again quickly after, she delivers a flying kick to the enemy, dealing 500 (500 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 200 (200 + 5% extra Health) Health. She then somersaults into the air, during which she has crowd control immunity and 25% damage reduction, and recovers 300 (300 + 5% extra Health) Health.
Defend by Attacking: When using Whatever (I) quickly after, she blinks behind the enemy and delivers a spinning kick, knocking back the target and dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) (+ 15% of the target's lost Health) physical damage.
If the target is defeated, she recovers 300 (300 + 5% extra Health) Health, as well as 50% Punch and Kick Strength. These effects are doubled if she defeats an enemy hero.
