skill3.name: Get Serious
skill3.description:
Mayene gets serious, dealing 360 (360 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
Upon entering the Serious State, she recovers 1 Punch Strength and Kick Strength, and max Strength is increased to 3 bars each. The Serious State lasts for 10s, during which she gains 15% Movement Speed, and any slowing effect inflicted on her is reduced by 50%.

strategy.earlyGame: In a clash-lane 1v1, Mayene is about as scary as it gets. From level 2, with Skill 1 and Skill 2 online, the derivation combos put your opponent in a guessing game they cannot win. Default to Skill 1 → Skill 2 for the punch flurry and its healing to win repeated trades; when they back off, switch to Skill 2 → Skill 1, teleporting behind them for bonus damage equal to 15% of their missing HP. Fist and Leg charges refill one every 8.5 seconds, so the one house rule is: after dumping both, take half a step back and don't eat the counter-swing. In quiet moments, let the Passive kick in — she sits down, snacks, and heals.
strategy.midGame: Once the lane is broken, spend minutes 8 to 13 split-pushing a side lane as bait. Whoever comes to collect you eats Skill 2 → Skill 2: the flying kick's crowd control immunity, damage reduction, and healing let you tank the attempt outright, and against two or fewer pursuers it often flips into a kill. One player bending multiple enemies around her while the team takes the Tyrant or towers — that is the Mayene win condition. She is helpless if jumped at zero charges, so make checking for two full gauges before every fight a reflex.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, cast the Ultimate first, not last. Its serious mode instantly refunds one Fist and one Leg charge and raises the cap to three, letting you chain derivations without pausing for breath. Hunt the backline: flank, lift them with Skill 1 → Skill 1, then finish with Skill 2 → Skill 1's missing-HP bonus. Takedowns with that finisher refund 50% energy (doubled for hero kills), so every kill reloads the next combo. When the 10-second window closes, your output falls off a cliff — overstaying is the one unforgivable sin.
strategy.teamfight: Hold the flank and wait for the enemy's CC to be aimed at someone else. Enter with Skill 2 → Skill 2 — crowd control immunity carries you straight through their counters. On landing, refill with the Ultimate and pick the derivation the moment demands: Skill 1 → Skill 1 to lift, Skill 1 → Skill 2 to sustain, Skill 2 → Skill 1 to execute. And honestly, the moment you stop running fixed sequences — reading "they're retreating: 2 into 1" and "they're standing their ground: 1 into 2" on reaction — is the moment Mayene actually begins.

combos.title: Pull and Launch (1 → 1)
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dash + pull in + 30% slow) → Skill 1 again immediately (leaping strike, 1s launch)
combos.description: The first cast drags the target in front of her, so you set the spacing yourself. The second adds physical damage equal to 10% of the target's max Health at Lvl 1, and enemies caught dead center take another 50%. She also takes 25% less damage during the strike at Lvl 1, so you can push through the counterattack.

combos.title: Blink Behind Finisher (2 → 1)
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (evasive flip) → Skill 1 immediately (blink behind + spinning kick, knockback)
combos.description: The kick adds physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health, so it scales with how much you have already chipped off. A takedown restores 300 Health at Lvl 1 plus 50% Strength, doubled when the target is an enemy hero. That refund is what reloads the next combo.

combos.title: Serious State Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Serious State + nearby damage) → Skill 2 → Skill 2 (flying kick) → Skill 1 → Skill 1 (1s launch)
combos.description: Entering the Serious State refunds 1 bar each of Punch and Kick Strength and raises the cap to 3. Using a different combo within 3s of the previous one boosts its effect by 25%, so closing with 2 → 2 and then launching with 1 → 1 lines up cleanly. It runs 10s, and once it ends her output thins out fast, so watch the timer before overextending.

strengths: Four derivations cover engages, sustain, defense, and executions
Crowd control immunity and healing mid-combo make her 1v1 among the best in the game
The Ultimate's instant charge refund unlocks explosive teamfight chains
Takedown energy refunds let momentum turn her nearly unstoppable
weaknesses: Useless with empty gauges — charge accounting never stops
Split-second derivation choices back up her Very Hard difficulty rating
The Passive's lazy healing shuts off in combat, leaving mid-brawl sustain thin
The window right after serious mode ends is where she gets punished

playstyle.style: An eccentric brawler juggling two stamina gauges — slack off and she literally sits down to snack. Weave her cartwheel dodge and pull correctly and her flurries take over the fight.
playstyle.suited: players who read resource management as a puzzle rather than a chore, watching two stamina bars and choosing a derivation on the spot — the Very Hard tag is honest.

synergy.reason: Lady Sun's Ultimate Shell needs a target that cannot move, and Destined Encounter pins enemies already carrying bitter bond.
Jing's Mirror Domain gathers enemies into one spot and pins them, so Destined Encounter sweeps the whole clump.

counters.reason: Gao Changgong stays in stealth far longer than the exposure from Bitter Farewell lasts, so it expires first.
Liang's Power Word - Control locks Dyadia in place, and fated bond simply expires while she stands there.

passive.description:
Dyadia enhances her next Basic Attack every 7.5-6s (decreases with hero level): She swings toward the enemy, dealing 379 (210 + 100% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage and knocking them back, then jumps back using the momentum.
When a teammate receives Blessing of Fate (does not trigger at full Health; Gold halved if used on teammates with more than 50% Health), or an enemy hero is affected by Bitter Reconciliation, she earns an extra 20 Gold and reduces the preparation time of her enhanced Basic Attack by 50%.
passive.name: Melodic Swing

skill1.description:
Dyadia blesses a teammate with fated bond, restoring 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) Health. For the next 5s, heroes blessed with fated bond gain 30% Movement Speed when they move toward each other. When they come close, Blessing of Fate is triggered, restoring 400 (400 + 60% magical attack) Health to both and maintaining the Movement Speed boost for 2s.
If she uses the skill again on a teammate already blessed with fated bond, she will dash to them and instantly trigger Blessing of Fate. The teammate recovers 400 (400 + 60% magical attack) Health and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s, while Dyadia recovers 400 (400 + 60% magical attack + 8% extra Health) Health.
She can use this skill again within 5s. If it is not used again, the cooldown will be reset.
skill1.name: Heartlink

skill2.description:
Dyadia marks an enemy with a bitter bond, exposing them and dealing 45 (45 + 6% magical attack) magical damage while penalizing them with a loss of 2 Gold (does not affect non-hero units) every second for 5s. When the effect ends, it deals an extra 225 (225 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. When two enemies with bitter bond move toward each other, they are slowed by 25%. When they come close, Bitter Reconciliation is triggered, stopping them from taking more damage and returning the penalized Gold.

If she uses the skill again on a target already affected by bitter bond, she will dash to them, triggering Bitter Reconciliation, immobilizing them for 0.75s and dealing a total of 600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage. During this time, she takes 25% less damage (this effect is doubled against the affected target).

The penalized Gold is held by Dyadia. If the target defeats/assists in defeating her, they will recover 100%/50% of the Gold respectively.

She can use this skill again within 5s. If it is not used again, the cooldown will be reset.
skill2.name: Bitter Farewell

skill3.description:
Dyadia commands a swarm of wisps to fly forward, granting fated bond to teammates in their path, restoring 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) Health, and inflicting bitter bond on enemies in their path, dealing 320 (320 + 45% magical attack) magical damage.
If a teammate already has fated bond, the duration is refreshed. They also recover an extra 150 (150 + 25% magical attack) Health and gain 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
If an enemy already has bitter bond, the duration is refreshed. They also take an extra 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and are immobilized for 1s.
Passive: Each time Dyadia gains 1 extra Gold from using a skill, the base Health restored and magical damage dealt from Destined Encounter are increased by 1.
skill3.name: Destined Encounter

strategy.earlyGame: Early on, a roaming Dyadia spends her time handing out bitter bond with Bitter Farewell. A bonded enemy hero is exposed while it lasts, takes damage over time and has Gold taken from them. Gold she earns from skills raises Destined Encounter's healing and damage, so every early bond she lands pays off later. When your jungler comes to gank, recast Bitter Farewell on the bonded target to fly in and immobilize them.
strategy.midGame: As fights start mixing allies and enemies, a single Destined Encounter can heal your team and hit theirs at once. Allies in the wisps' path get fated bond and recover Health; enemy heroes get bitter bond and take damage. Enemies who already carry bitter bond are also immobilized, so sending it through someone you tagged with Bitter Farewell earlier turns one cast into lockdown as well. Bitter-bonded enemies are slowed when they move toward each other. If they actually meet, Bitter Reconciliation stops the damage and gives back the Gold, so push the attack with your team while they are slowed trying to regroup. In games with stealth heroes, anyone hit by Bitter Farewell cannot hide while it lasts.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights Dyadia belongs right next to her backline. Bitter Farewell's second cast pays off most when used to stop someone sitting on your carry, since its damage reduction covers her as she flies in. For wounded allies, tie fated bond with Heartlink, then recast to fly over and trigger the blessing. If your team does not turn on the enemy you immobilized, do not chase; go back to handing out bonds.

combos.title: Double Root Catch
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Bitter Farewell: apply bitter bond) → Skill 2 (Bitter Farewell: recast to fly to them and immobilize) → Skill 3 (Destined Encounter: immobilize the bonded enemy)
combos.description: Recasting Bitter Farewell on an enemy with bitter bond flies her to them and immobilizes them. While she is flying in she takes less damage, and even less from the target she pinned. Destined Encounter only immobilizes enemies that already carry bitter bond, so casting it before the bond is applied breaks the chain.

combos.title: Fly to an Ally and Heal
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Heartlink: fated bond on an ally) → Skill 1 (Heartlink: fly to the bonded ally for Blessing of Fate)
combos.description: Casting Heartlink again on an ally who already has fated bond flies Dyadia to them and triggers Blessing of Fate on the spot. The ally gets healing and a speed boost and she heals too, which makes it the tool for pulling back together with a wounded teammate.

combos.title: Swing Peel
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (enhanced: swing to knock back and jump away) → Skill 2 (Bitter Farewell: apply bitter bond) → Skill 2 (Bitter Farewell: recast to immobilize)
combos.description: The enhanced Basic Attack swings her in front of the enemy, knocks them back and carries her backward on the momentum. It peels a diver off your teammate while opening space for herself. Each Blessing of Fate on an ally and each Bitter Reconciliation on an enemy shortens the wait for her next enhanced attack, so the next swing comes back sooner.

strengths: Bitter Farewell's bitter bond exposes enemy heroes and stops them hiding in stealth
Combining Bitter Farewell and Destined Encounter lets her immobilize a target twice in a row
Her enhanced Basic Attack knocks a diver back and carries her backward with the momentum
Every bit of Gold she earns from skills makes Destined Encounter heal and hit a little harder
weaknesses: If the enemy she marked kills her, they reclaim the Gold she took
The second cast of Bitter Farewell flies her to the target, which puts her next to enemies
When two bitter-bonded enemies meet, Bitter Reconciliation stops the damage and returns the Gold
Blessing of Fate only triggers when bonded allies come close, so for a distant ally she has to fly over

playstyle.style: Dyadia is a support who goes around tying fated bonds to teammates and bitter bonds to enemy heroes. Teammates with fated bond heal when they come close to each other, and enemies with bitter bond lose Gold to her over time. Casting the same skill on the same target again sends her flying to them, so both her healing and her lockdown reach farther.
playstyle.suited: Heartlink and Bitter Farewell both work in two steps: the first cast ties the bond, the second draws out the effect. You need room in your head to remember who carries which bond and to time the second cast by watching how far apart allies and enemies are. The Gold she takes is reclaimed if the marked enemy kills her, so it also takes patience to earn it without stepping too far forward.

synergy.reason: Hou Yi has no escape, so Flowborn's knockbacks peel the divers off him while he keeps firing.
Kongming's Spirit Bomb needs a channel, and Flowborn's launch buys exactly that window.

counters.reason: Marco Polo's Destroyed Defense adds true damage, which slips straight past Flowborn's stacked defenses.
Lu Bu ignores crowd control while diving with Tremble, Mortals, so Flowborn's launches cannot stop him.

passive.description:
Flowborn can draw the Flow into their body at the Base to enhance stats.
Vitality: Increases max Health by 300 and Physical and Magical Defense by 50.
Piercing Heart: Increases max Health by 300 and Physical Attack by 30.
Haste: Increases max Health by 300 and Movement Speed by 12.5.
Focus: Increases max Health by 300 and Cooldown Reduction by 5%.
Spend 1 stack of Flow to perform an enhanced Basic Attack that deals 408 (220 + 100% physical attack + 4% extra Health) physical damage and recover 125 (125 + 2.5% extra Health) Health.
passive.name: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, reducing the cooldown of other skills by 50% while gaining 5 stacks of Flow and recovering 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health. Gains 1 extra stack and recovers extra Health for every teammate and every 2 minions nearby, for up to 9 stacks and double the recovery.
Flowborn deals 100 (100 + 2% extra Health) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocks them back (without applying crowd control).
skill1.name: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn charges toward the target, knocking back enemies in the path, then slashes forward to deal 600 (600 + 185% extra physical attack) physical damage and gain a 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) shield for 3s.
Using this skill continuously on the same target for 1.5s changes its effects in the following order.
Clearing Slash: Deals equal slash damage to enemies, launches them for 0.33s, and gains a shield of the same amount.
Rifting Slash: Deals equal slash damage to enemies, launches them for 0.66s, and gains a shield of the same amount.
If the skill is not on cooldown, spend 4 stacks of Flow to stop it from entering cooldown after this use.
All non-hero units within range of this skill are affected by the same crowd control effect.
skill2.name: Power From Within

skill3.description:
Flowborn leaps to the target location and attacks, dealing 400 (400 + 70% extra physical attack + 8% extra Health) physical damage and knocking back enemies for 0.75s. Deals an extra 50% damage at the center of the attack.
If the skill is not on cooldown, can spend 5 stacks of Flow to stop it from entering cooldown after this use.
skill3.name: All In

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Flowborn (Tank) begins the game by choosing their Flow enhancement at the Base. In lane, use Convergence near the minion line to build plenty of Flow, and keep trading with the healing from enhanced Basic Attacks. Convergence also shortens the cooldowns of other skills, so slipping it in before Power From Within brings the charge and shield back sooner. Once they learn All In, they can add its knockback to the jungler's ganks.
strategy.midGame: In objective fights from the mid game on, the Flow they have stored turns directly into the number of engages. After going in with All In, layer Power From Within on the same target to chain launches and hold them until the team's damage arrives. When the enemy steps forward thinking their skills are spent, a second All In paid for with Flow catches them off guard. On the front line, keep cycling the charge so Power From Within's shield never lapses while they keep hitting.
strategy.teamfight: Before a teamfight, check that they have enough Flow for recasts, then take the front. Open with All In and put the target at the center of the leap. Enemies at the center take extra damage, so follow straight up with Power From Within on the same target and let the team pour in damage while they are airborne. If the back line is targeted, cut in with Power From Within's charge and push the enemy back behind the shield.

combos.title: Fill Up on Flow, Then Engage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Convergence: gain Flow and shorten other cooldowns) → Skill 3 (All In: hit the center and knock back) → Skill 2 (Power From Within: charge and slash) → Skill 2 (Clearing Slash) → Skill 2 (Rifting Slash)
combos.description: Before engaging, use Convergence near a group of minions or teammates to build up Flow. Pay for the second and third Power From Within with Flow and land them on the same target to advance to Rifting Slash.

combos.title: Spend Five for a Double Leap
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (All In: spend 5 Flow to cast) → Skill 3 (it does not go on cooldown, so cast it again)
combos.description: An All In paid for with Flow does not go on cooldown, so the second leap can follow right away. Flow can only be spent while the skill is not on cooldown, so if the first cast is made without paying, the second does not follow.

combos.title: Cutting In for the Back Line
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Power From Within: charge them off and gain a shield) → Basic Attack (enhanced: spend 1 Flow to heal) → Skill 1 (Convergence: knock back and refill Flow)
combos.description: The enhanced Basic Attack spends 1 Flow and restores Health, so after cutting in with the charge they can stay put and hit back. Convergence's knockback does not apply crowd control, so leave holding enemies in place to the team.

strengths: Spending Flow lets them recast Power From Within and All In without the skills going on cooldown
Landing Power From Within in succession advances to Clearing Slash and Rifting Slash, chaining launches
Power From Within's shield and the enhanced Basic Attack's healing keep them on the front line
The enhancement chosen at the Base lets them adjust their stats to the enemy
weaknesses: Once Flow runs out they cannot recast, so they get fewer engages
Convergence builds little Flow when few teammates or minions are nearby
Their only movement is a charge and a leap, so they struggle to catch enemies who poke from range
Managing Flow and chaining inputs makes them busier than they look

playstyle.style: Flowborn (Tank) is a tank who spends the Flow stored up with Convergence to recast Power From Within and All In without putting them on cooldown. Using Power From Within on the same target in succession changes its form, with Clearing Slash and then Rifting Slash launching for longer. At the Base, they can draw in the Flow to gain Health plus one of defense, Physical Attack, Movement Speed or Cooldown Reduction.
playstyle.suited: They suit players who can count their remaining Flow and choose which skill to recast. Each skill needs a different amount of Flow to recast, so how much they have stored decides how many engages they get. Convergence builds more Flow the more teammates and minions are nearby, so fighting beside the team suits them better than moving alone.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's shield and his wind's stun buy the stationary Flowborn the time to finish Arcane Arts.
Lian Po's crowd control immunity guarantees the launch at the end of Tremor Smash, pinning targets for Starflow Cascade.

counters.reason: Jing's paired marks reset the dash she engages with, so Flowborn can never keep her at range.
Liang's circles claim the ground, and a turret mage like Flowborn gets whittled down standing in them.

passive.description:
While at base, Flowborn can channel the Flow into their body, gaining an extra 50–100 Magical Attack (scales with hero level) and enhancing one of four stats:
Vitality: Gains an extra 300–600 Health.
Piercing Heart: Gains an extra 50–100 Magical Pierce.
Haste: Gains an extra 12.5–25 Movement Speed.
Focus: Gains an extra 5%–10% Cooldown Reduction.
Flowborn can use 1 stack of Flow to unleash an enhanced Basic Attack, spreading its damage to up to 3 nearby enemies and dealing an extra 120 (120 + 24% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back (without applying crowd control). Also recovers 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health, gains 5 stacks of Flow, and reduces the cooldown of Starflow Cascade and Arcane Arts by 50%.
Nearby teammates and minions grant additional recovery (up to 100%) and Flow stacks (up to 9 stacks).
skill1.name: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn throws an orb in the target direction that explodes upon hitting a hero, monster, or reaching its endpoint, dealing 280 (280 + 55% magical attack) magical damage and slowing enemies by 25% for 0.75s, then dealing 3 strikes of 50 (50 + 10% magical attack) magical damage.
Using the skill repeatedly within 2s enhances the effects:
Dual Radiance: Stuns enemies for 1/3s instead of slowing them.
Orb Volley: Increases range by 25 and stuns enemies for 0.5s instead of slowing them.
When the orb pierces a minion, it triggers explosion damage in advance. Can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use an extra Starflow Cascade.
skill2.name: Starflow Cascade

skill3.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow forward, dealing 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and slowing enemies by 25% for 0.75s. They then form a beam that pulls in all nearby enemies, dealing a total of 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) magical damage once every 0.2s.
Can spend 5 stacks of Flow to use an extra Arcane Arts. Other skills can be used during this skill.
skill3.name: Arcane Arts

strategy.earlyGame: Your game starts before you leave the fountain: pick the Flow boon at base. The cooldown option (5-10% CDR) is the default for combo uptime, while the magic-pierce boon punishes opponents who stack magic defense. In mid lane, Skill 2's orb is the chip damage — it detonates on a hero or a monster, or when it reaches the end of its path. It passes through minions, but piercing one shortens the fuse, so clearing the wave and touching the laner behind it rarely happen in the same cast. Decide which one you want before you fire. Treat Skill 1 less as a weapon and more as fuel: it cuts the cooldowns of Skill 2 and the Ultimate by 50% and restocks Flow, so fire it during safe windows while the wave sits on your side and you will never run dry at the 4-minute Tyrant fight. Until the Ultimate arrives at Level 4, winning the chip war is the whole job — don't force kills.
strategy.midGame: Around eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are finished, a single orb starts taking frightening chunks out of people. The job now is recasting inside the two-second window to supply your own crowd control. The first cast slows 25% for 0.75s. The second, Dual Radiance, stuns for a third of a second; the third, Orb Volley, stuns for 0.5s and widens the radius by 25. Flow caps at nine stacks, so the iron rule is topping off with Skill 1 before every fight. Walk in empty and the four-stack bonus cast never comes, along with half your output.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, holding the full combo in reserve becomes the win condition. With magic attack scaled through the final core items, Orb Volley's 0.5s stun into Skill 3's beam drops anyone with marksman-grade durability. Skill 3 lets you cast other skills mid-channel, so the ideal picture is holding the beam while firing fresh orbs. If someone dives you, you are not empty-handed: Skill 1 knocks them back, Skill 2 slows, and the follow-up casts stun twice. Four Flow stacks keep Skill 2 off cooldown entirely, so how many times you can shove a diver away comes down to the stack count. What Flowborn does not have is a dash or a blink — the moment they stand ahead of the frontline is the moment they die. When setting up before Overlord, always keep a wall and your teammates at your back.
strategy.teamfight: Open every fight from the absolute backline. Skip the enemy tank; land Skill 2 on the fighter pushing into your carries, then chain the second and third casts' stuns to freeze their front. Once you see an enemy blink go down, commit the Ultimate — its beam links to the enemies around it and keeps ticking every 0.2 seconds. A Skill 2 paid for with four Flow stacks never touches its cooldown, so you can keep firing as long as stacks remain; that loop is the whole point of this hero. When you're spent, don't chase — fall back and let Skill 1's healing patch you up.

combos.title: Three-Stage Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Restock Flow) → Skill 2 (Slow) → Skill 2 (1/3s Stun) → Skill 2 (0.5s Stun)
combos.description: Recast Skill 2 within 2s and the orb becomes Dual Radiance, then Orb Volley. That supplies a 1/3-second stun and a 0.5-second stun without waiting on a teammate's crowd control, and Orb Volley's extra 25 range makes the third cast the easiest to land. Skill 1 is the refill: casts paid with 4 Flow stacks never enter cooldown.

combos.title: Layering Under the Beam
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Beam) → Skill 2 (Slow) → Skill 2 (1/3s Stun)
combos.description: Other skills stay available while the beam channels. Keep it burning, fire an orb, and recast within 2s for the stun. The beam links to the enemies around it and damages them once every 0.2 seconds, so the tighter they stand, the more it returns.

strengths: Spending Flow stacks lets Skill 2 and the Ultimate ignore cooldowns entirely
Recasting Skill 2 supplies two stuns with no outside help
Casting other skills during the Ultimate's beam packs absurd damage density
Skill 1's healing and cooldown cut give far more staying power than expected
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once Skill 1's small knockback is baited, nothing else peels
Damage ceiling depends heavily on precise nine-stack Flow management
Skill 1's stack income and healing shrink without teammates nearby
Skill 2 is a straight-line orb, so stepping sideways lets it pass by

playstyle.style: A turret mage who picks their own stat upgrades through Flow selection. The beam and the three-stage orb are simple area control — a polished template of the mage role.
playstyle.suited: players who like re-picking their build direction match to match. The piloting stays light: recasting Skill 2 inside two seconds supplies its own stun. Fire without counting Flow stacks, though, and the bonus cast is missing exactly when it is needed.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's ultimate camouflages nearby teammates too, so Flowborn can get within Claw Flurry range unseen.
Kui hooks an enemy and keeps it stunned with his ultimate, so Flowborn can chain Claw Flurry on a pinned target.

counters.reason: Musashi's duel delays Flowborn's healing until it ends, so Claw Flurry's recovery can't keep them in the fight.
Arthur dashes in with a silencing strike, and Flowborn, whose healing and dashes all come from skills, loses both while silenced.

passive.description:
While at base, Flowborn can channel the Flow into their body, gaining an extra 12.5–25 Movement Speed (scales with hero level) and enhancing one of four stats:
Vitality: Gains an extra 300–600 Health.
Piercing Heart: Gains an extra 30–60 Physical Attack.
Haste: Gains an extra 50–100 Physical Pierce.
Focus: Gains an extra 5%–10% Cooldown Reduction.
Flowborn can use 1 stack of Flow to unleash an enhanced Basic Attack, dealing an extra 135 (135 + 45% extra physical attack) + 3% max Health magical damage to enemies in the center of the attack area.
passive.name: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, dealing 100 (100 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back (without applying crowd control). Also recovers 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health, gains 5 stacks of Flow, and reduces the cooldown of Claw Flurry and Mortal Talons by 50%.
Nearby teammates and minions increase the recovery up to 100%, and stacks of Flow up to 9 stacks.
skill1.name: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn dashes in the target direction. If there is an enemy near the destination, Flowborn recovers 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health (halved if a non-hero unit) and then repeatedly phases through enemies while attacking:
The first two phase strikes deal 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range.
The final strike deals 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage and slightly pulls in enemies.
Use repeatedly within 2s to cycle through the different skill effects in sequence:
Darkest Shadow: Final strike damage is increased by 50%.
Cutthroat: Final strike damage is increased by 50%, and it also deals extra physical damage equal to 10% of the target's lost Health.
Flowborn can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use an additional Claw Flurry.
skill2.name: Claw Flurry

skill3.description:
Flowborn unsheathes their twin claws and dashes to the target location, gaining crowd control immunity and dealing 200 (200 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path. Upon reaching the destination, deals an additional 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocks back enemies.
Flowborn can spend 5 stacks of Flow to use an additional Mortal Talons.
skill3.name: Mortal Talons

strategy.earlyGame: In the jungle, Flowborn keeps their Health up by landing Claw Flurry on monsters. Healing is halved against monsters, but it is enough to keep clearing. Used alone, Convergence gives only its base healing and Flow; near teammates both increase, so using it while a teammate helps with the first clear pays off. Hold the first gank until Mortal Talons is learned. With no way of their own to stop a target, lanes where your laner has crowd control make kills easier.
strategy.midGame: Before a gank, use Convergence next to your minions or laner; the more units nearby, the more Flow they store and the more extra casts they get. With enough Flow they can chain three Claw Flurries, and the third grows with the target's lost Health, so the more your team has already damaged the target, the bigger the hit. At Tyrant or Overlord, store Flow near your team before going in. Alone in the enemy jungle, Convergence stores little Flow and leaves few extra casts.
strategy.teamfight: Before a teamfight, use Convergence near your team to store as much Flow as possible. Leave the engage to your front line and wait off to the side. Dive their back line with Mortal Talons; the knockback at the destination scatters a grouped enemy. Follow with chained Claw Flurries and finish wounded targets with the third. Claw Flurry restores Health each time they land near enemies, so they can hold on while surrounded as long as they keep casting. When out of options, slot in Convergence to push enemies away, recover cooldowns and Flow, then go back in.

combos.title: Push Them Out With Talons, Then Chase
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Convergence: store Flow) → Skill 3 (Mortal Talons: dash) → Skill 2 (Claw Flurry) → Skill 2 (cast again)
combos.description: Storing Flow with Convergence first saves it for extra casts later. Dash in with Mortal Talons to push out the enemy at the destination, then catch them with Claw Flurry. Recasting in quick succession makes the final strike heavier.

combos.title: Finish With the Third Claw Flurry
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Claw Flurry) → Skill 2 (second cast) → Skill 2 (third cast grows with lost Health) → Basic Attack (enhanced with Flow)
combos.description: Casting Claw Flurry repeatedly makes the second cast's final strike heavier, and the third adds damage based on the target's lost Health. Extra casts need Flow, so use what you stored to reach the third, then spend what is left on an enhanced basic attack.

combos.title: Spend Everything, Then Reload
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Mortal Talons: dash) → Skill 2 (Claw Flurry) → Skill 1 (Convergence: shorten cooldowns, refill Flow) → Skill 3 (extra cast with Flow)
combos.description: Slotting Convergence in right after Mortal Talons and Claw Flurry shortens both cooldowns and restores Health. It also refills Flow, so they can cast Mortal Talons again straight away.

strengths: Claw Flurry restores Health whenever they land near enemies, so they can hold on after diving in
Convergence shortens the cooldowns of Claw Flurry and Mortal Talons, bringing their dashes back quickly
Mortal Talons ignores crowd control during the dash, so they can go in on opponents who are waiting for them
The third Claw Flurry grows with the target's lost Health, making wounded enemies easier to finish
weaknesses: Without an enemy near the landing point, Claw Flurry is just movement with no healing or attack
No stuns or slows; all they can apply are knockbacks and a slight pull
Every skill is close range and needs them right next to enemies
Extra casts depend on Flow, and once it runs out, they have fewer chained casts

playstyle.style: Flowborn (Assassin) is a jungler who keeps dashing in with Claw Flurry, restoring Health each time they land near enemies, to cut into ganks and teamfights. Stored Flow lets them cast Claw Flurry and Mortal Talons again without waiting for the cooldown, and repeated Claw Flurries in quick succession make the final strike heavier. Convergence knocks back nearby enemies, refills Flow and shortens the cooldowns of both skills.
playstyle.suited: Claw Flurry gives no healing and no attack unless an enemy is near the landing point, so what decides how they play is whether you can land at the enemy's feet. Tracking Flow and Convergence's cooldown at the same time keeps you busy, so while learning, cycling just Convergence and Claw Flurry is enough to fight.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's shield and stun let Flowborn stand in the fight and finish a full arrow chain.
Cai Yan's sound wave chains stuns down the enemy line, opening a clean window for Arrowstorm.

counters.reason: Gao Changgong opens from stealth and stuns Flowborn through his dagger mark, leaving no room to fire back.
Jing pressures from two sides at once, and every mark shatter refreshes her skills, so the chase never stops.

passive.description:
Flowborn can draw the Flow into their body at the Base, increasing Attack Speed by 10%-20% (increases with hero level) and enhancing one of four other stats.
Vitality: Increases max Health by 300.
Piercing Heart: Increases Physical Attack by 30.
Haste: Increases Movement Speed by 12.5%.
Focus: Increases Cooldown Reduction by 5%.
Enhanced Basic Attack: Fires a piercing projectile, dealing 80 (80 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. Hitting an enemy extends its travel distance while reducing damage by 30%.
Each enhanced Basic Attack consumes 1 stack of Flow.
passive.name: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, dealing 100 (100 + 25% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back (without applying crowd control). Also recovers 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health, gains 5 stacks of Flow, and reduces the cooldown of Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm by 50%.
Nearby teammates and minions increase the recovery (up to 100%) and stacks of Flow (up to 9 stacks).
skill1.name: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn shoots an enormous projectile at the target (can be blocked by enemy heroes), dealing 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back non-hero units.
Flowborn can dash a short distance upon use (use it again within 1.5s to become enhanced).
Second Use: Enhances projectile damage by 25%.
Third Use: Levitates and enhances projectile damage by 50%.
Can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use this skill again.
Casting speed increases with Attack Speed.
skill2.name: Arrow of No Retreat

skill3.description:
Flowborn shoots 7 volleys of light projectiles at the target location (casting speed increases with Attack Speed), dealing 75 (40 + 21% physical attack) physical damage (every 3 projectiles counts as 1 Basic Attack). Projectiles lock on to targets within range. Also gains a 10% Movement Speed increase. Use this skill again to levitate.
Can spend 5 stacks of Flow to use this skill again.
skill3.name: Arrowstorm

strategy.earlyGame: Choose one Flow enhancement at the Base before heading to the farm lane. Against an aggressive opponent, Vitality's extra Health helps absorb pressure; in a calmer matchup, Piercing Heart brings damage forward. Until the ultimate is learned, this is not the time for hard trades, so collect last hits and experience steadily. If the opponent closes in, reset with Convergence's knockback and healing. Convergence also starts the cooldown reduction for Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm, so using it defensively is never wasted.
strategy.midGame: As items raise Attack Speed, skills cast faster and Flowborn's output grows. When called to Tyrant or Overlord, join from the very back and start by landing Arrow of No Retreat on the nearest enemy. The arrow allows a short move after firing, so get used to stepping back after each shot to avoid being caught. Weaving extra casts of Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm from Flow between basic attacks keeps the damage going regardless of cooldowns. Convergence refills Flow, and more nearby teammates or minions give more, so keep it topped up between fights.
strategy.teamfight: Stay at the very back and wear down the closest enemy. If chased, push them back with Convergence, take the healing and shortened cooldowns, then fire again. The ultimate, Arrowstorm, speeds Flowborn up while firing, which suits shooting while backing off. Once the enemy front line breaks, spend the saved Flow on repeated Arrow of No Retreat casts to finish their back line. Right after skills and Flow are spent is when Flowborn is most vulnerable, so hold back at the edge of range until they return.

combos.title: Triple Arrow of No Retreat
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Arrow of No Retreat) → Skill 2 (the second deals more damage) → Skill 2 (the third fires from the air)
combos.description: Stacking casts in a short window raises the arrow's damage, and the third becomes an airborne attack. The normal cooldown is too long for three in a row, so stored Flow fills the gap with extra casts. The arrow stops at the first enemy hero it hits, so it will not get through at angles that need to pass a frontliner.

combos.title: Push Back, Then Fire Back
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Convergence: knockback and heal) → Basic Attack (piercing shot) → Skill 2 (Arrow of No Retreat)
combos.description: When someone closes in, Convergence pushes them back, restores Health and refills Flow. It also shortens the cooldowns of Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm, so Flowborn can fire straight back while retreating. More nearby teammates and minions mean more healing and more Flow.

combos.title: Chase With the Arrowstorm
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Arrowstorm: gain Movement Speed) → Skill 3 (fire from the air) → Basic Attack (piercing shot)
combos.description: Arrowstorm locks onto targets in the area and rains arrows on them while making Flowborn faster. Casting it again turns it into an airborne attack, and saving Flow allows an extra cast, so retreating enemies can be chased down.

strengths: The more Attack Speed, the faster their skills cast
Convergence's knockback and healing let them reset when someone closes in
Stored Flow fires Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm again without waiting for the cooldown
Many of their skills allow movement after casting, which helps them keep firing while backing off
weaknesses: Arrow of No Retreat stops at the first enemy hero it hits, so it cannot reach past a frontliner
The piercing shot travels further after hitting an enemy but loses damage
With Flow used up, they have no extra shots left
If caught after using Convergence, they have few ways to escape

playstyle.style: Flowborn (Marksman) draws the Flow into their body at the Base, gaining Attack Speed and choosing one of four extra enhancements before heading out. Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm cast faster as Attack Speed rises, and stored Flow lets Flowborn fire them again without waiting for the cooldown. Convergence knocks back nearby enemies while restoring Health, refilling Flow and shortening the cooldowns of both skills.
playstyle.suited: With two clear attacks, the enormous arrow and the arrowstorm, Flowborn is not demanding to control. Most of the decisions come down to checking how much Flow is left and choosing between firing extra shots or saving it for defense. Which enhancement to take at the Base depends on the opponents in that match.

synergy.reason: Huang Zhong is immobile in Turret Mode, so he can sit on the casting platform and keep its shield and range.
Lady Zhen's launch and heavy slow leave enemies barely moving, so Flowborn's stream of sound waves is hard to dodge.

counters.reason: Musashi's duel delays all of the target's recovery, so Flowborn cannot lean on self-healing to outlast him.
Wang Zhaojun's snowstorm lingers on the ground, grinding down Flowborn and allies who hold position on the casting platform.

passive.description:
While at base, Flowborn can channel the Flow into their body, gaining an extra 50–100 Magical Attack (scales with hero level) and enhancing one of four stats:
Vitality: Gains an extra 300–600 Health.
Piercing Heart: Gains an extra 50–100 Magical Pierce.
Haste: Gains an extra 12.5–25 Movement Speed.
Focus: Gains an extra 5%–10% Cooldown Reduction.
Flowborn can use 1 stack of Flow to unleash an enhanced Basic Attack, firing a sound wave that deals an extra 90 (90 + 13.5% magical attack) magical damage to the target and ricochets to nearby units 2 times, dealing equal damage. When it ricochets to a teammate, it restores 80 (80 + 12% extra magical attack) Health.
passive.name: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, dealing 100 (100 + 15% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back (without applying crowd control). Also recovers 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health, gains 5 stacks of Flow, and reduces the cooldown of Protection Melody and Lingering Melody by 50%.
Nearby teammates and minions increase the recovery up to 100%, and stacks of Flow up to 9 stacks.
skill1.name: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn raises a casting platform beneath their feet for 4s, knocking back nearby enemies (without applying crowd control). Teammates on the platform gain vision, a shared shield that negates 320 (320 + 5% extra Health) damage, and 75 attack and skill range. Upon leaving the platform, they dash in the direction they are moving.
Use the skill repeatedly while on the casting platform to cycle through the different skill effects in sequence:
Scudding Clouds: Expands the casting platform and extends its duration, while granting an extra 25 attack and skill range and 25% shield.
Harmonious Song: Expands the casting platform and extends its duration, while granting an extra 50 attack and skill range and 50% shield.
Can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use an extra Protection Melody. Gains an extra 50% increase to attack and skill range while on the platform.
skill2.name: Protection Melody

skill3.description:
Flowborn gains 90 Movement Speed and continuously unleashes 8 sound waves in the target direction, recovering 60 (60 + 0.9% extra Health) Health when they hit.
Hits an enemy: Deals 92 (92 + 14% magical attack) magical damage.
Hits an ally: Restores 60 (60 + 9% extra magical attack) Health.
Hits a wall: Ricochets up to 3 times, creating new sound waves that deal 75% damage.
Flowborn can spend 5 stacks of Flow to use an additional Lingering Melody.
skill3.name: Lingering Melody

strategy.earlyGame: As a roamer, Flowborn starts by using Convergence next to their laner and the minion wave. Convergence's healing and Flow increase with the number of nearby teammates and minions, so it is worth more beside teammates than alone. Once they learn Lingering Melody, move along with the jungler's ganks. They have no skill to stop enemies, so leave the signal to engage to their teammates.
strategy.midGame: Before fights over Tyrant or Overlord, build up plenty of Flow with Convergence. The platform only appears beneath their own feet, so stand next to the teammate they want to protect before casting. Teammates on the platform gain attack and skill range and can fire from farther away than usual. Right after placing a platform to attack, they cannot knock enemies back with Protection Melody until its cooldown ends. Keeping Flow in reserve lets them cast it once more on the spot to push enemies off. Teammates leaving the platform dash quickly, so stepping off right after a knockback lets the whole back line retreat together.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfights start with placing Protection Melody just behind the front line. Back-liners on the platform can fire with extra range while carrying the shield. When enemies close in, push them back with Convergence. It shortens the cooldowns of Protection Melody and Lingering Melody and restores Flow, readying the next platform and sound waves. Lingering Melody's sound waves damage enemies and heal allies they hit, so aiming them where enemies and teammates are mixed reaches both at once. Sound waves that hit a wall ricochet and create new waves, so firing at walls in jungle paths multiplies them.

combos.title: Grow the Platform to Its Third Stage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Convergence: gain Flow) → Skill 2 (Protection Melody: casting platform) → Skill 2 (Scudding Clouds) → Skill 2 (Harmonious Song)
combos.description: Use Convergence near teammates or minions to build up plenty of Flow. Spending Flow lets them cast Protection Melody again, so they can recast it repeatedly while on the platform. Each recast expands the platform and extends its duration, adding more shield and range at each stage.

combos.title: Cast Lingering Melody Twice
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Convergence: gain Flow) → Skill 3 (Lingering Melody: fire a stream of sound waves) → Skill 3 (spend Flow for an extra cast)
combos.description: Securing Flow with Convergence first lets them fire two volleys of sound waves back to back. Every hit also restores their own Health, so they are harder to bring down while firing.

combos.title: Push Away Enemies Near the Platform
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Protection Melody: knock back and raise the platform) → Skill 1 (Convergence: knock back and heal) → Basic Attack (enhanced, heals on ricochet)
combos.description: Knock back a diving enemy with Protection Melody, and if they are still close, knock them back again with Convergence. Meanwhile, teammates on the platform keep their shield. Spending 1 stack of Flow from Convergence enhances their basic attack, and the ricocheting sound wave heals any teammate it reaches.

strengths: Protection Melody gives every teammate on the platform a shared shield and extra range
Convergence's healing and Flow increase the more teammates and minions are nearby
Lingering Melody's sound waves damage enemies they hit and heal allies they hit
Their enhanced Basic Attack ricochets to nearby units and heals teammates it reaches
weaknesses: None of their knockbacks apply crowd control, and they have no stun or knock-up
The shield and range boost only apply to teammates on the casting platform
Each extra cast spends Flow, and once it is gone they have fewer options until Convergence is back
Their shield and self-healing scale with extra Health, while damage and ally healing scale with magical attack, splitting their item priorities

playstyle.style: Flowborn (Roamer) is a support who hands out shields and range to teammates with a casting platform raised beneath their feet, and deals damage and heals at the same time with sound waves. They have skills that knock enemies back, but none of them apply crowd control, so they have no way to stop enemies. Spending the Flow stored up with Convergence lets them cast Protection Melody or Lingering Melody again.
playstyle.suited: They suit players who don't mind staying next to their teammates. Both the shield and the range boost only reach teammates standing on the casting platform. Spending a long time warding alone keeps them from doing their job, and they need the habit of counting whether they have enough Flow before an extra cast.

synergy.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect strips crowd control from allies, so a pinned Florentino can move and fight again.
Guiguzi's The Animist pulls enemies into one spot, so Blossom's bouquets land right in that pile and keep refreshing Triple Threat.

counters.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract suppresses Florentino, cutting off Triple Threat's chain and his bouquet pickups.
Liang's Power Word - Barrier walls off the approach, and the stun on contact cuts Florentino's dash short.

passive.name: Shuffle
passive.description:
When Florentino leaves combat or touches a bouquet, his next Basic Attack is enhanced for 5s to include a dash and deal 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) extra physical damage. If it hits an enemy hero, he recovers 140 (140 + 2% extra Health) Health (halved against non-hero units).
After the dash ends, he can dash a certain distance again.

skill1.name: Blossom
skill1.description:
Florentino tosses a bouquet forward, dealing 300 (300 + 95% extra physical attack) physical damage, stunning the first enemy hit for 0.75s, and scattering 3 bouquets around the target that last 3.5s.
If Florentino touches a bouquet, he gains the enhanced Basic Attack Shuffle and refreshes Triple Threat's cooldown.

skill2.name: Triple Threat
skill2.description:
Florentino attacks the target 3 times with his sword.
1st Attack: Deals 120 (120 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage and inflicts extreme slow for 1s.
2nd Attack: Deals 120 (120 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage.
3rd Attack: Deals 120 (120 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage over 2 hits.
Each hit deals an additional 120 (120 + 35% extra physical attack) true damage to the target and reduces Blossom's cooldown by 1s.
There is a 1.5s cooldown between the first 2 attacks. After the third attack, the skill goes on cooldown. After each attack, Florentino can dash a certain distance.

skill3.name: Gentlemen's Duel
skill3.description:
Florentino dashes in the target direction, marking the first enemy hero hit and increasing their damage taken by 10% for 5s while scattering 3 bouquets around them.
During the skill's duration, the recovery effect of Shuffle's enhanced Basic Attack is doubled, and Florentino gains crowd control immunity for 3s, extended by a further 1s for every bouquet he touches.
Touching a bouquet grants Shuffle's enhanced Basic Attack and refreshes Triple Threat's cooldown.
After the dash ends, he can dash a certain distance again.

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Level 1 starts with Skill 1. The 0.75-second stun sprouts three flowers around your target, so collect them mid-stun, then chain enhanced basic attack into Skill 2 for a trade loaded with true damage that your opponent simply cannot match. The enhanced basic heals 140 HP when it strikes a hero, which means the longer the slugfest runs, the wider the HP gap grows — that's the Florentino experience. Once the Ultimate arrives at Level 4, the mark's 10% bonus damage taken plus crowd control immunity makes your duels nearly unloseable. Just pick flower routes on the side ganks can't reach.
strategy.midGame: Around nine minutes, with your first two core items finished, it's time to move. Chip the enemy tower down, then show up mid: Skill 3's dash into the flower loop makes you a one-man gank engine. In the standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, one Skill 1 threaded from a river bush is enough to take a pick. When nothing is happening, splitting side towers is genuinely one of your best uses of time. Watch your sustain, though — the enhanced basic's healing is halved against minions, so don't loiter in a lane at low HP expecting to heal it back.
strategy.lateGame: With a frost gauntlet and a sustain piece rounding out your build, the late game rewards duels over head-on 5v5s. Pressure a side lane, then catch whoever comes to answer with Skill 3 and finish them — that's the golden pattern. At rank 3 the mark raises their damage taken by 20%, and cycling Skill 2's true damage through flower pickups on a target like that kills even tanks on a timer. The only real threat is getting surrounded. Crowd control immunity runs 3 seconds and extends 1 second per bouquet you touch, but that ceiling is real — CC timed for the moment it drops will still put you down.
strategy.teamfight: You are not the frontal engage. Wait in a side bush, let the enemy's CC land on your frontline, then commit the Ultimate onto their backline. The dash blooms three flowers on arrival, so once you land, dance the loop — flower, Skill 2, flower, Skill 2 — and your damage never pauses. While the Ultimate runs, enhanced basic healing doubles, letting you shrug off a surprising amount of focus mid-combo. Your one losing script is getting burst before the first flower pickup. In the instant before you dive, check what skills the enemy still has up — every time.

combos.title: Bouquet Pickup Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.75s Stun, 3 Bouquets) → Touch a Bouquet (Enhanced Basic Attack, Skill 2 Reset) → Enhanced Basic Attack (Dash) → Skill 2 → Touch a Bouquet → Skill 2
combos.description: A landed Skill 1 scatters 3 bouquets around the target for 3.5s. Every bouquet Florentino steps on empowers his next Basic Attack and refreshes Skill 2's cooldown. Each of Skill 2's three strikes adds true damage and trims 1s from Skill 1's cooldown. The bouquets last 3.5s: if the route to all three is not clean, take one and get out.

combos.title: Marked Duel
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Mark, 3s Crowd Control Immunity) → Touch a Bouquet (Enhanced Basic Attack, Skill 2 Reset) → Enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 2 → Touch a Bouquet → Skill 2
combos.description: The dash marks the first enemy hero it hits and raises their damage taken for 5s. Three bouquets bloom around that target. Crowd control immunity starts at 3s and gains 1s for every bouquet touched. Enhanced Basic Attacks heal double while the skill runs, and each pickup hands Skill 2 back. The duel comes down to how much true damage fits inside those 5 marked seconds.

combos.title: Hit and Step Away
combos.sequence: Enhanced Basic Attack (Dash) → Skill 2 (1st Strike, 1s Extreme Slow) → Skill 2 (2nd Strike) → Disengage
combos.description: Simply leaving combat empowers the next Basic Attack. In lane, cash that in for the dash hit and the first two strikes of Skill 2, then walk out. The opening strike carries a 1s extreme slow, so the chase loses ground. Skill 2 enters its real cooldown only after the third strike: stop at two, and that strike plus the quick move behind it becomes the exit.

strengths: Flower pickups reset Skill 2 endlessly, cycling true damage nonstop
Enhanced-basic healing — doubled during the Ultimate — wins any slugfest
The dash's crowd control immunity forces 1v1s on his terms
Constant dashes and bonus moves make roams and split pushes fast
weaknesses: Miss Skill 1 and no flowers bloom — the combo loses its front door
Flower spots are predictable; CC placed on the pickup path shreds him
Few answers to long-range poke and disciplined kiting
Flower tracking and micro-movement demand real practice time

playstyle.style: A fencer who scatters bouquets and weaves between them, each pickup refreshing his empowered strikes. He duels by designing routes through his own flowers — elegant to watch, demanding to pilot.
playstyle.suited: players who choreograph their footwork mid-fight, since every bouquet touched refreshes Triple Threat and the route between the flowers is the combo.

synergy.reason: Marco Polo's Fevered Barrage hits for as long as enemies stay in range, and Starry Night's launch keeps them there.
Lian Po's Tremor Smash slows enemies so they cannot walk away, letting Starry Night's delayed detonation land.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi cycles through crowd control immunity, so he can shrug off Starry Night's delayed launch.
Arli's Maple Dance knocks down the projectile Lorion leaves outside him, and his whole kit runs through it.

passive.name: Eternal
passive.description:
Lorion's skills detonate when they hit a target, dealing damage and activating his projectile.
While the projectile is outside him, the activated projectile deals 59 (59 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to the unit with the lowest Health within range every 0.75s for 4s.
While the projectile is inside him, the activated projectile deals damage to all units within range at double the frequency, and he recovers 25 (25 + 0.4% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

skill1.name: Here's What I Think
skill1.description:
Lorion moves his projectile to the target location, dealing 220 (220 + 44% magical attack) magical damage to units in its path. Upon reaching the destination, it detonates, dealing an extra 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. When the skill is used, if the projectile is outside him, it deals 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts 20% slow for 1.5s to units between its start and end points.
The projectile is recalled to Lorion when too far away.

skill2.name: Abyssal Pact
skill2.description:
When the projectile is outside him, Lorion recalls and then detonates it, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and gaining 20% Movement Speed for 2s.
When the projectile is inside him, 30% of the cooldown is refunded.

skill3.name: Darkness Falls
skill3.description:
When the projectile is outside him, Lorion flies to it and detonates it, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. During this period, he gains 25% damage reduction for 2s after he lands and crowd control immunity.
When the projectile is inside him, 30% of the cooldown is refunded.

skill4.name: Starry Night
skill4.description:
After a 2s delay, the projectile detonates, dealing 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and launching them for 1.25s.
When using his Ultimate, he immediately gains 1 Skill 1 charge.
If the Ultimate does not hit a hero, 50% of its cooldown is refunded.

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, Lorion spends most of his time clearing waves with the projectile held inside him. Activated there, it hits everyone around him and heals him with each hit, so losing a little HP in a skirmish is easy to recover from. Send it out with Here's What I Think only when you want to poke, and as soon as it lands, recall it with Abyssal Pact. While it stays outside, the healing from the inside mode is not available.
strategy.midGame: Once he leaves lane and moves with the team, the projectile becomes something you park on the enemy's route. In standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, send it to the path they would use to back off, or to the pit entrance. Add Starry Night on top and enemies who fear the blast cannot step into that space, which lets your side choose where the fight happens. Detonating too early just gets dodged and ends as a bluff, so the ideal moment is right as a teammate catches someone. Because the outside projectile targets low-HP enemies on its own, leaving it near a wounded opponent is often enough to push them out. Darkness Falls can be used to attack, but it is also his main way to back off safely. While the enemy assassin is out of sight, place the projectile behind you before stepping forward; if they dive, you fly to it and out of reach.
strategy.teamfight: Most of his teamfight work is done before it starts, by choosing where the projectile sits. Set it where the enemy is likely to bunch up, then sweep the line between start and end with the second cast of Here's What I Think to slow them; that breaks their formation and makes Starry Night much easier to land. If your team can follow up on the knock-up, the numbers swing right there. When the fight turns into a scramble with enemies on top of you, recalling the projectile with Abyssal Pact is a real option: it hits everyone nearby and heals you, so he lasts longer than he looks. The whole fight is a running choice between showing the enemy the projectile or himself.

combos.title: Set It on the Escape Route, Then Detonate
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Here's What I Think: send the projectile) → Skill 1 (sweep between start and end) → Skill 4 (Starry Night: detonate)
combos.description: The first cast sends the projectile to the enemy's feet or across their escape route. Casting again while it is outside hits and slows everyone between its start and end points. Starry Night takes a moment to go off, so stacking it on an ally's crowd control makes it far harder to dodge. A blast that hits no hero comes back sooner, so setting it early as a threat costs little.

combos.title: Recall It and Hold On
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (projectile outside) → Skill 2 (Abyssal Pact: recall and activate) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Outside, the projectile only hits the single lowest-HP unit in range. When enemies dive into you, recalling it with Abyssal Pact makes it hit everyone around you and heal you with each hit. Healing from minions and monsters is small, so if you are counting on it you need to fight near enemy heroes.

combos.title: Fly to the Projectile and Get Out
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (send it toward the exit) → Skill 3 (Darkness Falls: fly to it) → Skill 2 (recall and speed up)
combos.description: Darkness Falls flies Lorion to the projectile while it sits outside him. For an escape, send it toward the way out, not into the fight. Recall it with Abyssal Pact when you land and leave with the speed boost. The projectile comes back on its own if you stray too far, so keep it just past the escape route.

strengths: Switching the projectile between inside and outside lets him fight at any range
Starry Night's knock-up can be set in narrow corridors and escape routes ahead of time
While flying to the projectile with Darkness Falls he takes less damage and is immune to crowd control
The projectile left outside picks the lowest-HP target in range on its own
weaknesses: A badly placed projectile weakens almost every skill he has
Starry Night takes a moment to detonate, so fast enemies can step out of it
Using Darkness Falls to attack leaves him with no way out afterward
Moving too far from the projectile pulls it back inside and the threat it was holding disappears

playstyle.style: Lorion is a mage whose whole kit changes depending on whether his one projectile is out in the world or held inside him. Placed outside, it is a turret that keeps hitting the lowest-HP target in range; recalled, it strikes everyone around him and heals him as it does. His ultimate, Starry Night, also detonates at the projectile, so where it sits decides both attack and defense.
playstyle.suited: Before every cast you have to think about where the projectile should be right now. If that extra step sounds fun, you will enjoy how one placement turns the same skill into either an attack or an escape. He rewards reading the fight ahead of time more than raw aim.

synergy.reason: Hou Yi has to stand still to keep firing, and Hurricane Wall covers exactly that window.
Consort Yu needs a wind-up before Oak Bolt fires, and Annette's shield carries that charge through.

counters.reason: Gan & Mo instantly refill their flying swords with Freshly Forged, closing the window Annette needs to step up.
Kongming's Spirit Bomb hits harder the more Health Annette has lost, so a chipped Annette only gets easier to kill.

passive.name: Whisperwind
passive.description: While Annette is moving, her skill cooldowns are faster and she gains Mana. While there are teammates nearby, she also gains 25 Movement Speed.

skill1.name: Gust Force
skill1.description:
Annette conjures a magic circle at the target location that activates every 0.5s for 4s.
The magic circle deals 160 (160 + 28% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts 5% slow on enemy units for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.
The magic circle grants teammates 5% Movement Speed for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.

skill2.name: Wind Cuffs
skill2.description:
Annette fires an orb in the target direction, flying back from the recoil, gaining a shield that negates 400 (400 + 6% extra Health) damage for 3s, and gaining 75 Movement Speed for 2s.
The orb deals 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies it hits.
The orb grants a shield that negates 400 (400 + 6% extra Health) damage to all teammates it hits.
If the orb passes through a Gust Force magic circle, it pushes the magic circle to its destination.

skill3.name: Hurricane Wall
skill3.description:
Annette conjures a barrier around herself for 4s (requires channeling), knocking back enemies within range and dealing 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage. Enemies that touch the barrier will take equal damage and be stunned for 1.25s. Teammates within the barrier gain crowd control immunity.
While channeling, Annette becomes untargetable and is slowed by 50%.

strategy.earlyGame: Shadow your marksman from the start and support the farm-lane scraps with Skill 2's orb. Hit an ally and it shields; hit an enemy and it damages; and you bounce backward on every cast — one aiming decision covers offense and defense at once. Before the 4-minute Tyrant, your job is tagging along on ganks: Skill 1's formation stacks slows on enemies who cross it and speeds up allies who do, a ready-made chase engine. Since the Passive refunds cooldowns and restores mana as you move, walking the river beats standing still in lane — Annette performs best in motion.
strategy.midGame: Once your support item upgrade and cooldown boots are in, skirmishes start brewing around mid. Annette's spot is half a step ahead of her carry. The instant an enemy fighter telegraphs a dive, open Skill 3: every enemy inside the radius at that moment is knocked back. Anyone who walks into the barrier afterwards is not pushed away — they take damage and a 1.25-second stun instead. Teammates standing inside gain crowd control immunity. Because the knockback fires on cast, you can wait and watch their engage before committing. The trick of pushing your formation forward with the orb is also worth practicing for chipping enemies who hide under tower.
strategy.lateGame: The late game is an exercise in patience: hold the Ultimate for the one enemy who decides fights. With your defensive capes stacked, you won't fall over even standing forward. The ideal sequence at a fight's entrance is Skill 1 first to control the ground, then catching the enemy assassin mid-leap with the barrier as they jump your marksman. While it's active you become untargetable but your move speed is halved, so opening in the wrong spot strands you away from your team while the fight is decided. Open it right beside the person you're protecting — no exceptions.
strategy.teamfight: Stand next to your carry. The job is three tasks: lay Skill 1 across the enemy frontline's path to blunt the charge; thread Skill 2's orb through your most-focused teammate to keep shields flowing; and when the real dive arrives, meet it with the Ultimate — knockback, stun, and crowd control immunity for everyone inside. Keep that order and you'll tilt teamfights while dealing almost no damage yourself. The one hazard is the orb's recoil: bounce backward into a flanker and the story ends badly. Glance behind you before every cast — make it a reflex.

combos.title: Dive Breaker
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Knock Back, 1.25s Stun, Crowd Control Immunity for Allies) → Skill 1 (Slowing Magic Circle) → Skill 2 (Shield an Ally)
combos.description: Open the barrier the instant someone jumps your carry. Enemies in range are knocked back, anyone who touches the wall is stunned for 1.25s, and allies inside gain crowd control immunity. Once they are off, Skill 1 slows the retreat and the orb hands a shield to the teammate it passes through. Channeling makes Annette untargetable but cuts her Movement Speed by 50% at Level 1, so open it right beside the ally she is protecting.

combos.title: Circle Delivery
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Place the Magic Circle) → Skill 2 (Orb Pushes the Circle)
combos.description: An orb that touches the magic circle carries the whole circle to the orb's destination. That reaches enemies kiting at max range or sitting under tower. The circle activates every 0.5s and lasts 4s. Push it immediately after it lands.

combos.title: Recoil Retreat
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Fire at the Chaser, Recoil Backward) → Skill 1 (On the Landing Spot)
combos.description: Firing the orb throws Annette in the opposite direction. The 3s shield and the 2s Movement Speed bonus are locked in by the cast itself. A hit is not required for them; landing one only adds magical damage to the chaser. Drop the magic circle where she lands and the pursuit has to walk through the slow. The one thing to check at the moment of firing is what sits behind her.

strengths: The Ultimate's knockback, stun, and crowd control immunity erase entire dives
Skill 2 is damage, shielding, and a reposition in a single button
Movement refunds her cooldowns, so skills keep cycling as long as she moves
Layered speed-ups and slows control the tempo of chases and retreats
weaknesses: Minimal personal damage — she can't convert her setups into kills alone
No healing, so teammates who are already chunked stay chunked
The barrier halves her move speed; a bad opening spot means instant separation
Forget the orb's recoil and it bounces you straight into trouble

playstyle.style: A support who literally cannot stand still — movement refunds her cooldowns. She accelerates allies through her circles, hands out shields, and her barrier ultimate bounces entire engages back.
playstyle.suited: players who want to support at a sprint — movement itself refunds her cooldowns, and the orb's recoil has to be measured before it is fired.

synergy.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect clears crowd control and grants immunity, so Butterfly can dive without being locked down.
Mozi's Cannon Blast stuns whoever it hits, so Butterfly's Death Dealer lands on a target that cannot move.

counters.reason: Lu Bu's ring of slaughter raises both his defenses, so Butterfly struggles to trade with him.
Diaochan keeps trimming Petals in the Wind's cooldown, so she blinks away before Butterfly can close.

passive.description: Butterfly gains 2 marks from defeating heroes and 1 mark from assists and from killing monsters/minions. At 3 stacks, the next skill used will not enter cooldown.
passive.name: Assassination

skill1.description: Butterfly deals 362 (240 + 70% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. Each extra enemy hit increases damage by 25%. Also gains a shield that negates 381 (250 + 75% physical attack) damage lasting 2s, and gains 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time.
skill1.name: Whirlwind

skill2.description:
Butterfly deals 333 (220 + 65% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. The first enemy hit takes 1.5 times this damage and is slowed by 50% for 1.5s.
Hitting an enemy increases her Attack Speed by 25% and Critical Rate by 10% for 4s, for up to 2 stacks.
skill2.name: Sword Propel

skill3.description:
Butterfly jumps to a target enemy, dealing 557 (400 + 90% physical attack) physical damage (if the target is marked, deals extra true damage equal to 12% lost Health) and marking them for 4s. For 4s after hitting the target, she takes 50% less damage from all Basic Attacks.
While the mark is active, she recovers Health equal to 35% of damage dealt to the target. If the target is defeated, it will immediately reset her Ultimate's Cooldown.
Hitting marked targets with Basic Attacks will also reduce the Cooldown of Skills 1 and 2 by 1s.
skill3.name: Death Dealer

strategy.earlyGame: You're the jungler. Skill 1 gains 25% bonus damage for every additional enemy it hits, so casting from the center of each camp is free clear speed. The opening route is both buffs plus the river camps, aiming for Level 4 around the 3-minute mark. Passive stacks build from monster kills too, and at three stacks your next skill costs no cooldown — bank them before a gank and you walk in with an extra cast. As for the 4-minute Tyrant: touch it only when you've reached Level 4 before the enemy jungler has. Otherwise it's bait.
strategy.midGame: Once your jungle item and first damage item are finished, the real work begins: erasing chipped enemies. The ideal prey is a backliner under half HP. Death Dealer's leap applies the mark, converts 35% of your damage into healing, and — the headline — resets its own cooldown instantly on a takedown. Open ganks with Skill 2: the first enemy hit takes 1.5x damage and a 50% slow, and the attack speed and crit buffs it grants let your basics finish the job. The one rule that never changes, even in this window: do not walk into a healthy enemy team from the front.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Butterfly is the cleanup crew, not the opening act. Even when the 5v5 starts, hold your side bush until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline. The Ultimate adds true damage equal to 12% of a marked target's lost HP, so anyone already chipped dies — armor stacked or not. One kill refunds the Ultimate on the spot, a hero takedown banks two passive stacks, and the chain reaction begins. The flip side: without that first kill, nothing starts. Whatever else you compromise on, never compromise on your entry timing.
strategy.teamfight: Your brawl loop is enter, kill, reset, next. Lead with Skill 2 before committing — the slow keeps them in reach, the attack speed buff quickens your swings, and each basic on a marked target shaves a second off both Skill 1 and Skill 2. When focus piles up, Skill 1's shield and decaying 50% speed boost carry you back to the edge of the fight. While your mark is active you take half damage from basic attacks, so a chasing marksman often can't actually finish you. One nuance: enemy support shields can rob your takedown reset, so start with the softest unshielded target — that's the correct kill order.

combos.title: Soften First, Then Leap
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (1.5x Damage, 50% Slow) → Skill 3 (Leap, Mark) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Shield, Haste)
combos.description: The first enemy Skill 2 hits takes 1.5 times the damage plus a 50% slow for 1.5s. Landing it also stacks the Attack Speed and Critical Rate buff, which is why it belongs before the leap rather than after. Basic Attacks on the marked target cut 1s from Skill 1 and Skill 2 cooldowns and return 35% of the damage dealt as Health. Skill 1 closes the pattern with a shield and a speed burst that covers either the chase or the exit.

combos.title: Takedown Reset Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Mark) → Basic Attack (Takedown) → Skill 3 (Cooldown Reset, Next Target) → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: Killing the marked target resets Skill 3's cooldown on the spot. A hero takedown also banks 2 passive marks, and at 3 the next skill used skips its cooldown entirely. Marked targets take extra true damage equal to 12% of their lost Health, so start with wounded enemies. Leap onto a healthy one and no reset comes — the chain ends right there.

combos.title: Jungle Clear Rotation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Catch Several Targets) → Skill 2 (Attack Speed and Critical Rate) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Skill 1 gains 25% damage for each extra enemy caught, so it belongs in the middle of a camp, not at its edge. Skill 2's hit grants the Attack Speed and Critical Rate buff, up to 2 stacks (25% and 10% at Level 1). Every monster killed banks 1 passive mark; reach 3 before you leave for a gank and the next skill costs no cooldown.

strengths: Takedown-triggered Ultimate resets give unmatched chain-kill power in brawls
35% damage-to-healing plus halved basic-attack damage while the mark runs
Lost-HP true damage finishes chipped targets through any amount of armor
Skill 1's shield and speed burst keep her entries and exits cheap
weaknesses: Without a first kill the resets never spin up and she fades hard
No CC of her own to start fights — she depends on teammates' lockdown
Hard CC exposes pure assassin fragility the moment it lands
Lacks a decisive answer to full-HP targets and healthy frontlines

playstyle.style: A snowballing assassin: takedowns build marks, and at three stacks her next skill has no cooldown. Every kill fuels the next — once she's rolling, nobody stops the chain.
playstyle.suited: players chasing momentum itself: patient early, then closing hard the instant a health bar drops, because the first kill shapes the whole match.
